sections.heading: What Is CG PET 2026? A Quick Overview

content.text: Before diving into the result and answer key details, here is a brief overview of the CG PET exam for candidates who need context.

The Chhattisgarh Pre Engineering Test (CG PET) is a prestigious state-level engineering entrance examination conducted by the Chhattisgarh Vyavasayik Pariksha Mandal (CG Vyapam). It serves as the gateway for admission to the following undergraduate programmes in government and private colleges across Chhattisgarh:

The CG PET 2026 examination was conducted as a pen-and-paper (offline) based test from 10:00 AM to 1:15 PM at 33 district headquarters across Chhattisgarh, covering subjects of Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.

sections.heading: CG PET 2026 - Key Dates at a Glance

content.text: This section provides a consolidated timeline of all important events related to CG PET 2026, from the application phase to result and counselling. Keeping track of these dates ensures you do not miss any critical deadline.
Important: All candidates are advised to regularly check vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in for the latest updates, as exact dates are officially notified on the portal.

sections.heading: Understanding the CG PET 2026 Final Answer Key

content.text: The final answer key is the officially validated set of correct answers published by CG Vyapam after reviewing all candidate objections raised against the provisional key. Here is what candidates need to know about it.

sections.heading: What Is the Difference Between Provisional and Final Answer Key?

items: The provisional answer key is released shortly after the exam and is open for challenges.
Candidates can raise objections - called "Dava Aapatti" - by paying a fee of ₹50 per challenge.
After reviewing all objections, CG Vyapam releases the final answer key, which is the authoritative version.
The final answer key is directly used to calculate every candidate's score and prepare the merit list.
No further objections are accepted against the final answer key.

sections.heading: What If a Question Is Found Incorrect?

content.text: If any question in the CG PET 2026 paper is found to be incorrect or dropped after the objection review process, all candidates are awarded marks for that question regardless of their response. In the 2025 edition, for example, four questions were dropped by the board and marks were awarded to all candidates.

sections.heading: No Negative Marking in CG PET

content.text: A significant advantage of the CG PET examination pattern is that there is no negative marking for incorrect or unattempted answers. Each correct answer carries marks based on the official key.

sections.heading: How to Check CG PET 2026 Result and Download Scorecard

content.text: Checking the CG PET 2026 result is a straightforward online process. Follow the step-by-step guide below to access your scorecard without any confusion.

items: Visit the official CG Vyapam website: vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in
Navigate to the "Results" or "CG PET 2026 Result" link on the homepage.
Log in using your Vyapam profile credentials (Registration Number and Date of Birth).
Your CG PET 2026 result and scorecard will appear on the screen.
Download and save the scorecard - it is mandatory for the counselling and admission process.
Take a printout for future reference.

sections.heading: What Details Are Shown on the CG PET 2026 Scorecard?

content.text: Your CG PET 2026 scorecard will contain the following details:

items: Candidate's Name, Roll Number, and Registration Number
Father's and Mother's Name
Date of Birth and Category
Subject-wise Marks (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics) - out of 50 marks each
Total Marks Obtained
Merit Rank

sections.heading: CG PET 2026 Merit List - What You Need to Know

content.text: The merit list is one of the most closely watched documents published alongside the CG PET 2026 result. This section explains who makes it to the merit list and what information it contains.

sections.heading: Minimum Qualifying Marks for CG PET 2026

content.text: To be included in the CG PET merit list and become eligible for counselling, candidates must clear the minimum qualifying threshold:
The final qualifying marks are officially notified by CG Vyapam and may vary slightly each year. Candidates must confirm the exact threshold on the official website.

sections.heading: What Does the Merit List Include?

content.text: The CG PET 2026 merit list contains the following details for each qualified candidate:

items: Roll Number and Application Number
Candidate's Full Name
Category and Class Type
Gender and Date of Birth
Disability Status (if applicable)
Domicile Status
Total Marks Obtained and Merit Rank

sections.heading: After the Result: CG PET 2026 Counselling Process

content.text: Clearing the CG PET 2026 exam is only the first step. The actual seat allotment happens through the counselling process conducted by the Directorate of Technical Education (DTE), Chhattisgarh. Here is a complete overview of what comes next.

sections.heading: Overview of Counselling Rounds

content.text: CG PET counselling is typically held in 3 to 4 rounds, including spot rounds, scheduled from June to August 2026. Two separate phases of counselling are conducted:

items: Phase 1 - For Government and Government-Aided Colleges
Phase 2 - For Private Colleges

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Counselling Process

items: Counselling Registration - Register on the DTE Chhattisgarh counselling portal (separate from the CG Vyapam exam portal).
Choice Filling - Select your preferred colleges and courses in order of preference.
Seat Allotment - Seats are allotted based on CG PET rank, category, and choices filled.
Document Verification - Report to the allotted college or designated centre for document verification.
Reporting and Admission - Report to the allotted institute and complete the admission formalities.

content.text: Important: Missing the counselling registration deadline means losing your seat even if your rank is strong. Act promptly once the result is declared.

sections.heading: Documents Required for CG PET Counselling

content.text: Ensure all the following documents are self-attested and ready before counselling registration opens:

items: CG PET 2026 Scorecard / Rank Card
Class 10th and 12th Mark Sheets and Passing Certificates
Category Certificate (OBC/SC/ST, if applicable)
Domicile Certificate (mandatory for Chhattisgarh state quota seats)
Transfer Certificate (TC) from the last attended institution
Character Certificate
Passport-size Photographs
Photo ID Proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, etc.)
Disability Certificate (if applicable)

sections.heading: Who Can Apply for Admission via CG PET 2026?

content.text: The CG PET 2026 serves students from Chhattisgarh as well as candidates from other states. Notably, candidates from other states can also apply for admission through JEE Main scores as an alternative pathway. Chhattisgarh domicile holders are eligible for the state quota seats during counselling.

sections.heading: Re-Evaluation Policy: Can You Challenge the Result?

content.text: A common question among candidates is whether re-evaluation of the answer sheet is possible. CG Vyapam evaluates all OMR answer sheets through a machine-based automated process aligned with the final answer key. Due to this, re-evaluation of the OMR sheet is not provided. However, candidates are encouraged to challenge any incorrect answer during the provisional answer key objection window (Dava Aapatti), which is the only official avenue for raising concerns before the result is finalised.

detail.title: ISC Class 12 Syllabus 2026-27 - Overview
detail.short_info: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) has published the ISC Class 12 Environmental Science Syllabus 2026-27 for the 2027 board examinations. The syllabus includes seven units divided into three sections, covering ecological concepts, population conservation, pollution monitoring, sustainable agriculture, environmental economics and international environmental issues.

content.text: Environmental Science (Subject Code 877) carries a total of 100 marks, including 70 marks for the three-hour theory examination and 30 marks for practical and project work. Students can download the official syllabus PDF to check the prescribed topics, assessment requirements and project guidelines.

content.text: CISCE has made the Environmental Science syllabus available for ISC Examination Year 2027. The official PDF contains the complete Class 12 theory syllabus, unit-wise subject content and practical/project work requirements.

links.text: Download ISC Class 12 Environmental Science Syllabus 2026-27

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Environmental Science Exam Pattern 2026-27

content.text: The ISC Class 12 Environmental Science examination consists of two papers. Paper I is a written theory examination of three hours, carrying 70 marks. Paper II covers practical and project work, carrying 30 marks.

CISCE does not prescribe a separate question paper for the practical/project component. Students must complete the prescribed project work under teacher supervision, and the work is evaluated by an approved visiting examiner.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Environmental Science Unit-Wise Syllabus 2026-27

content.text: The Environmental Science syllabus is organised into three sections containing seven units. Students must prepare the prescribed topics in all three sections for the theory examination.

sections.heading: Section A: Environmental Science Syllabus
Unit 1: Human Beings and Nature

content.text: This unit examines the relationship between human societies and the natural environment. It introduces major environmental philosophies and explains how different schools of thought influence the conservation and use of natural resources.
Important topics:

items: Modern schools of ecological thought
Deep Ecology and Shallow Ecology
Stewardship of Land and the ideas of Wendell Berry
Social Ecology, Marxist Environmentalism and Socialist Ecology
Environmental ideas of Gary Snyder and Barry Commoner
Feminism and Ecofeminism
Green Politics and environmental movements
Sustainable Development
Environmental organisations, including Earth First, WWF and Greenpeace

sections.heading: Unit 2: Population and Conservation Ecology

content.text: This unit deals with population growth, ecological regulation and the conservation of biodiversity. Students study population dynamics, human population problems, ecosystem threats and different methods of protecting forests and wildlife.
Important topics:

items: Population dynamics, birth and death rates, immigration and emigration
Population age structure and population pyramids
Survivorship curves and r-selection and K-selection strategies
Malthusian Theory of Population
Demographic Transition Model and carrying capacity
Exponential and logistic population growth curves
Factors regulating population size
Human population control and women's empowerment
Habitat destruction, genetic erosion and biodiversity loss
Forest conservation and Joint Forest Management
National parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves
In-situ and ex-situ conservation
Project Tiger as a conservation case study

sections.heading: Unit 3: Monitoring Pollution

content.text: The Monitoring Pollution unit explains how environmental pollution is measured and assessed. Students learn basic monitoring techniques, air quality standards, water testing parameters and soil quality indicators.
Important topics:

items: Primary and secondary pollutants
Air pollution monitoring and emission control
Carbon credits and carbon trading
Air monitoring stations and sampling requirements
Manual monitoring techniques, including passive samplers and High Volume Samplers
Instrumental monitoring using NDIR and Chemiluminescence
National and international air quality standards
Central Pollution Control Board and State Pollution Control Boards
Water quality testing, including pH, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, hardness and nitrates
Biochemical Oxygen Demand and Chemical Oxygen Demand
Biological, physical and chemical soil indicators
Soil respiration, soil aggregates and infiltration rate

sections.heading: Section B: Environmental Science Syllabus
Unit 4: Third World Development

content.text: This unit examines the relationship between economic development, urbanisation, migration and environmental sustainability. It also discusses alternative development approaches and environmental planning in cities.
Important topics:

items: Urban-rural divide and migration
Push and pull factors influencing migration
Environmental consequences of conventional development
Unequal distribution and excessive consumption of natural resources
Gandhian approach to development
Village self-reliance, Antyodaya, Sarvodaya and Panchayati Raj
Cottage industries and intermediate technology
Urban sanitation, water supply, transportation and energy problems
Rainwater harvesting, composting and waste management
Decentralised Wastewater Management Systems
New Urbanism and Smart Growth
International examples of urban environmental planning and management

sections.heading: Unit 5: Sustainable Agriculture

content.text: The Sustainable Agriculture unit explains traditional and modern agricultural practices and their environmental consequences. Students study irrigation, the Green Revolution, soil conservation, food processing and long-term food security.
Important topics:

items: Traditional agriculture and farming systems in India
Natural farming, organic farming and modern agriculture
Traditional and modern irrigation methods
Canal irrigation, dams, sprinkler irrigation and drip irrigation
Traditional rainwater harvesting systems
Agriculture before, during and after British rule
Green Revolution and its social and environmental effects
High-Yielding Varieties, chemical fertilisers and pesticides
Land reforms
Mixed farming, mixed cropping and intercropping
Crop rotation, green manure and biofertilisers
Integrated Pest Management and biopesticides
Food processing, preservation, packaging and storage
Food adulteration, food additives and quality marks
Food security, sustainable food systems and equitable access to food

sections.heading: Section C: Environmental Science Syllabus
Unit 6: Environmental and Natural Resource Economics

content.text: This unit introduces the economic value of natural resources and environmental services. It examines resource scarcity, economic welfare, externalities and the role of natural capital in sustainable development.
Important topics:

items: Natural resources, scarcity and economic growth
Classification of natural resources
Renewable and non-renewable resources
Natural resource accounting
Gross Domestic Product and Gross National Product
Advantages and limitations of economic growth indicators
Environmental economics and net economic welfare
Natural capital and ecological capital
Positive and negative externalities
Cost-benefit analysis
Extended Producer Responsibility
Natural capital regeneration and ecosystem services
Environmental degradation and ecological footprint

sections.heading: Unit 7: International Relations and the Environment

content.text: This unit focuses on environmental issues that involve multiple countries. Students examine international environmental challenges, trade policies, intellectual property rights and the role of international cooperation in conservation.
Important topics:

items: International environmental issues and transboundary pollution
Amazon rainforest deforestation
International wildlife trade and the ivory trade
Ozone layer depletion and the ozone hole
Chapman's cycle and ozone-depleting substances
National sovereignty and international environmental politics
International trade and environmental protection
Free trade, protectionism and import barriers
Trade between developed and developing countries
World Trade Organization and General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights
Trade-Related Investment Measures
Agreement on Agriculture
Patents, copyrights, trademarks and geographical indications
International aid, tied aid and untied aid
Self-reliance and environmental sustainability

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Environmental Science Practical and Project Work 2026-27

content.text: The practical and project component carries 30 marks. CISCE permits students to complete one project from the prescribed categories under the supervision of their teacher. The project must demonstrate environmental understanding, research skills and appropriate methods of data collection or analysis.

rows: Study of a Current Environmental Problem
Investigate an environmental issue using available information and primary data, and propose possible solutions.
Design and carry out an environmental impact assessment, including relevant data collection and analysis.
Monitor a selected environmental issue for at least six months using scientific methods and numerical data.
Complete at least one month of fieldwork or training with a relevant environmental organisation and prepare a report.
Study plant population and density in a selected area using the quadrat method.

content.text: The 30-mark practical/project component is evaluated through the prescribed project work. Students complete their projects under their teacher's guidance, and a visiting examiner appointed locally with CISCE approval evaluates the work.
CISCE will not set a separate question paper for practical work. Students should follow the project requirements provided in the official syllabus and their school's instructions.

detail.title: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Exam Pattern 2027 - Overview
detail.short_info: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) has published the examination pattern and syllabus for ISC Class 12 Accountancy (Subject Code 858) for the 2026-27 academic session. The examination carries 100 marks, including an 80-mark theory paper and 20 marks for project work. The written examination will be conducted for three hours.

content.text: According to the official ISC Accountancy syllabus, the theory paper is divided into three sections: Section A (60 marks), Section B (20 marks) and Section C (20 marks). Section A is compulsory for every candidate, while students must attempt either Section B (Management Accounting) or Section C (Computerised Accounting). Candidates are not required to attempt both optional sections.

The ISC Class 12 Accountancy examination is scheduled for 26 February 2027, from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Students preparing for the board examination can check the section-wise marks distribution, topic-wise weightage, question paper structure, project assessment scheme and official syllabus PDF below.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Exam Pattern 2027 - Overview

rows: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Marks Distribution 2027

content.text: The Accountancy assessment is divided into theory and project work.
The theory paper examines accounting concepts and numerical problem-solving skills. Project work assesses students' ability to apply accounting principles, prepare records and explain their findings.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Section-Wise Weightage 2027

content.text: The 80-mark theory examination contains three sections, but students need to attempt only two of them.

rows: Partnership Accounts and Joint Stock Company Accounts
Section A + Either B or C

content.text: Important: Students must attempt Section A and one of the two optional sections. Section B and Section C are alternatives, so their marks should not be added together when calculating the maximum marks of the paper.

sections.heading: ISC Accountancy Section A Marking Scheme 2027

content.text: Section A is compulsory and carries 60 marks. It covers Partnership Accounts and Joint Stock Company Accounts.
The official syllabus provides the following topic-wise distribution.
The syllabus includes Admission, Retirement and Death of a Partner under Partnership Reconstitution. Students should prepare these topics together with goodwill accounting and related adjustments.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Partnership Accounts Weightage 2027

content.text: Partnership Accounts represents 34 marks of the compulsory Section A.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Joint Stock Company Accounts Weightage 2027

content.text: Joint Stock Company Accounts carries 26 marks in the compulsory Section A.
Students should focus on the prescribed treatment of shares and debentures, accounting entries and company financial statements.
Correct presentation of calculations and final accounts is important for numerical questions.

sections.heading: ISC Accountancy Section B Exam Pattern 2027

content.text: Section B covers Management Accounting and carries 20 marks.
Students choosing this section should prepare the three units listed in the official syllabus.
Section B assesses the ability to analyse financial statements and interpret financial performance.

sections.heading: Financial Statement Analysis - 4 Marks

content.text: This topic includes the prescribed analysis and interpretation of company financial statements.
Students should understand the purpose of financial statement analysis and practise the relevant comparative and common-size statement formats.

sections.heading: Cash Flow Statement - 8 Marks

content.text: Students should practise preparing Cash Flow Statements according to the methods and classifications prescribed in the ISC syllabus.
They should understand operating, investing and financing activities and accurately show the supporting workings.

sections.heading: Ratio Analysis - 8 Marks

content.text: Ratio Analysis assesses the calculation and interpretation of the financial ratios prescribed by CISCE.
Students should prepare the relevant liquidity, solvency, activity and profitability ratios and understand the significance of the results.

sections.heading: ISC Accountancy Section C Exam Pattern 2027

content.text: Section C provides an alternative to Management Accounting. It covers Computerised Accounting and carries 20 marks.

sections.heading: Electronic Spreadsheet - 10 Marks

content.text: The syllabus includes practical understanding of spreadsheet applications used in accounting.
Students should prepare the prescribed spreadsheet calculations, functions, formatting and data presentation methods.

sections.heading: Database Management System - 10 Marks

content.text: The DBMS unit includes:

items: Meaning and Features of a Database Management System
Database Tables and Fields
Data Storage and Retrieval
Basic Database Queries
Relevant SQL Commands and Functions
Business Applications of Databases

content.text: The official syllabus covers basic SQL commands such as SELECT, WHERE, AND, OR, UPDATE and DELETE, along with functions including AVG, COUNT, MAX, MIN and SUM.

sections.heading: ISC Accountancy Section B vs Section C

content.text: Students should understand the optional-section structure before preparing for the examination.

rows: Financial Statement Analysis, Cash Flow Statement, Ratio Analysis

content.text: Students should prepare the optional section taught by their school and refer to the official question paper instructions.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Question Paper Structure 2027

content.text: The official syllabus confirms that the 80-mark Accountancy theory examination consists of three sections.
Students must answer compulsory Section A and either Section B or Section C.
The specimen paper for the previous examination year provides useful examples of multiple-choice, short-answer and structured numerical questions.
However, candidates should check the latest official specimen paper applicable to Examination Year 2027 for the exact question numbering, subparts and internal-choice arrangements.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Project Work 2027

content.text: Paper II consists of project work carrying 20 marks.
According to the official ISC Accountancy syllabus, candidates are expected to complete two projects from topics covered in the theory syllabus.
The projects are assessed by the subject teacher and a visiting examiner appointed locally and approved by CISCE.

sections.heading: ISC Accountancy Project Marking Scheme 2027

content.text: Each project is evaluated out of 10 marks using the following criteria.
The subject teacher and visiting examiner separately evaluate the seven marks allocated to format, content and findings. Their marks are averaged according to CISCE guidelines.
The visiting examiner conducts the three-mark viva-voce for each project. The final total is calculated in accordance with the official project assessment procedure.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Project Topics 2027

content.text: The official syllabus provides suggested project activities based on accounting concepts and practical business situations.
Examples include:

items: Prepare journal entries, ledger accounts, a trial balance and financial statements for a partnership business based on a case study.
Prepare a Cash Flow Statement using the financial statements of a company for two consecutive accounting periods, along with the prescribed additional information.
Prepare comparative and common-size Income Statements and Balance Sheets for a selected company.
Prepare and interpret financial ratios using company financial statements.

content.text: Students should complete two projects according to their school's instructions and the detailed requirements specified in the ISC syllabus.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Exam Date 2027

content.text: According to the ISC Class 12 Date Sheet 2027, the Accountancy theory examination will be held on Friday, 26 February 2027.
Students should report according to their school's examination instructions and verify the final date and timing through the official CISCE timetable and admission card.

sections.heading: ISC Class 12 Accountancy Passing Marks 2027

content.text: The official ISC Examination Year 2027 regulations specify 35% as the minimum subject pass-mark standard.
Accountancy carries a total of 100 marks, comprising 80 marks for the theory paper and 20 marks for project work.

The reviewed Accountancy syllabus does not separately establish compulsory minimum marks of 28 out of 80 in theory and 7 out of 20 in projects. Students should follow the applicable CISCE regulations rather than assuming separate thresholds.
For the ISC Examination Year 2027, candidates must also satisfy the broader requirements for qualifying the examination, including the prescribed number of subjects and SUPW and Community Service.

Select the syllabus for ISC Examination Year 2027.
Find Accountancy (858) in the subject list.

content.text: Students should balance numerical practice with theoretical understanding and project preparation.

items: Study the complete official Accountancy syllabus for Examination Year 2027.

Practise goodwill valuation, admission and retirement adjustments.

detail.title: CBSE Class 11 Maths Exam Pattern 2027 - Overview
detail.short_info: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has published the Mathematics (Subject Code 041) curriculum and examination pattern for the academic session 2026-27. According to the official syllabus, Class 11 Mathematics carries a total of 100 marks, consisting of an 80-mark theory examination and 20 marks for internal assessment. The written examination has a duration of three hours.

content.text: The CBSE Class 11 Mathematics syllabus contains five major units: Sets and Functions, Algebra, Coordinate Geometry, Calculus, and Statistics and Probability. The published course structure assigns 25 marks to Algebra, 23 marks to Sets and Functions, 12 marks each to Coordinate Geometry and Statistics and Probability, and 8 marks to Calculus. Students should also prepare for application-based and analytical questions as specified in the official question paper design.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Exam Pattern 2027 - Overview
CBSE Class 11 Maths Marks Distribution 2027

content.text: The Class 11 Mathematics assessment is divided into two components: written theory and internal assessment.
Internal assessment marks are earned through periodic tests and Mathematics activities conducted during the academic session.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Unit-Wise Weightage 2026-27

content.text: The official CBSE Class 11 Mathematics course structure provides the following unit-level marks distribution.

Important clarification: Although the CBSE curriculum publishes these unit-level figures, the accompanying note cautions against assuming fixed chapter or unit-wise weightage. The question paper design separately confirms that there is no prescribed chapter-wise weightage. Students should cover all chapters, and the published figures should not be treated as a guarantee of an identical distribution in every school examination.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Question Paper Design 2027

content.text: The official Mathematics question paper design allocates marks according to the cognitive skills being assessed.
The three categories represent types of learning outcomes rather than three separately numbered examination sections. The actual question paper may contain different question formats.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Remembering and Understanding Questions

content.text: The official design allocates 44 marks, or 55% of the theory assessment, to remembering and understanding mathematical concepts.
These questions assess a student's ability to:

items: Recall Mathematical Definitions
Identify Relevant Formulas
Understand Mathematical Properties
Interpret Mathematical Notation
Explain Concepts and Relationships
Apply Fundamental Procedures in Familiar Situations

content.text: Students should revise textbook explanations, solved examples and fundamental identities before attempting more advanced problems.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Application-Based Questions

content.text: The application category carries 20 marks, or 25% of the theory question paper design.
Students may be required to use mathematical formulas or methods in unfamiliar situations, interpret numerical information or solve multi-step problems.
Preparation should include a variety of exercises rather than only repeating previously solved examples.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Higher-Order Thinking Questions

content.text: The official question paper design allocates 16 marks, or 20% to analysing, evaluating and creating.
These questions assess the ability to:

items: Analyse Different Parts of a Mathematical Problem
Identify Patterns and Relationships
Compare Alternative Solution Methods
Evaluate the Correctness of an Argument
Draw Logical Conclusions
Develop an Appropriate Solution Strategy

content.text: Students should practise challenging NCERT exercises and questions requiring detailed reasoning.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Internal Choice 2027

content.text: The official CBSE question paper design specifies that there will be no overall choice in the Mathematics question paper.
However, it provides for 33% internal choices across the sections.
Internal choice allows a student to answer one of the alternative questions provided within the paper. It does not allow the candidate to skip an entire compulsory section.
CBSE also permits suitable variations in question paper templates while retaining the overall weightage given to different question types.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Internal Assessment 2026-27

content.text: The internal assessment carries 20 marks and comprises two components.

rows: Periodic Tests - Best Two Out of Three

content.text: The curriculum provides detailed assessment guidance under the Mathematics syllabus for Classes XI and XII.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Periodic Test Marking Scheme

content.text: Periodic tests are pen-and-paper assessments conducted by schools during the academic session.
According to the CBSE guidelines, schools may conduct three periodic tests and use the best two performances for the final 10-mark periodic assessment.
Each test's marks are converted to a 10-mark scale. The best two scores are averaged to calculate the periodic-test assessment out of 10.
The months listed above are suggestive. Schools may adjust their test schedules according to their academic calendars.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Activities Marking Scheme

content.text: The Mathematics activity component carries 10 marks and encourages practical understanding of concepts.

rows: Activities Performed Throughout the Year and Record Keeping

content.text: CBSE recommends completing 10 Mathematics activities during the year using the NCERT Mathematics Laboratory Manual for Class XI.
Students should maintain their activity records and participate in the year-end assessment and viva-voce.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 11 Maths Syllabus 2026-27 Chapter-Wise

content.text: The prescribed Class 11 Mathematics syllabus is organised into five units containing 14 main chapters.

rows: Sets; Relations and Functions; Trigonometric Functions
Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations; Linear Inequalities; Permutations and Combinations; Binomial Theorem; Sequence and Series
Straight Lines; Conic Sections; Introduction to Three-Dimensional Geometry

content.text: The curriculum includes a separate list of topics intended only for formative assessment. Students should distinguish these from the content prescribed for summative examinations.

detail.title: ICSE Class 10 Economics Exam Pattern 2026-27 - Overview
detail.short_info: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) has prescribed the examination structure for Economics (Subject Code 64) for the ICSE Class 10 Board Examination 2027. The subject carries 100 marks, including an 80-mark written theory examination and 20 marks for internal assessment. The written examination has a duration of two hours, with an additional 15 minutes provided for reading the question paper.

content.text: According to the Economics question-paper blueprint, the theory examination consists of two sections: Section A (40 marks), which is compulsory, and Section B (40 marks), which offers internal choice. Candidates are required to answer four out of six structured questions in Section B. The paper assesses economic concepts, definitions, comparisons, interpretation of demand and supply, and the application of economic principles to practical situations.

Students preparing for the 2026-27 academic session should understand the marking scheme, question format, internal project requirements and passing criteria before beginning their final revision. The official CISCE syllabus for Examination Year 2027 is available at Official Website.

Candidates who appeared for the screening examination held on 31 October 2026 can now check their marks and qualifying status through the result PDF available on the official website at natboard.edu.in. The result was announced on 10 November 2026.

content.text: According to the published FMGE October 2026 result, 9,354 candidates qualified, while 31,539 candidates did not secure the required passing marks. The common result PDF contains candidates' application sequence numbers, examination roll numbers, marks and result status. Candidates can download this document without logging in. However, individual FMGE October 2026 scorecards will be available from 20 November 2026. Qualified candidates must also complete the prescribed identity and credential verification process to obtain their FMGE Pass Certificate.

detail.title: ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026 Direct Link
detail.short_info: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has declared the ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026 on 6 November 2026 for the September 2026 examination session. The official ICAI result website confirms that the Foundation result and merit list were announced on 6 November. Candidates who appeared in the examinations held on 2, 5, 7 and 9 September 2026 can check their results and scorecards through the direct official result page at caresults.icai.org/caresult/.

content.text: The CA Foundation September 2026 Result is available through the official result portal using the candidate's registration number and roll number. Candidates can check their paper-wise marks, aggregate marks and result status, and access the Foundation merit-list facility. To pass CA Foundation, candidates must obtain at least 40% marks in each paper and 50% marks in aggregate.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026 Direct Link

content.text: ICAI has activated the September 2026 Foundation result and merit-list entries on its official examination result portal. Candidates should use the authorised website to access their individual results.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026 Overview

content.text: The CA Foundation examination is the entry-level examination in the Chartered Accountancy course conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. The September 2026 examination consisted of four papers covering accounting, business laws, quantitative aptitude and business economics.

rows: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)

sections.heading: CA Foundation Result September 2026 Release Date

content.text: ICAI issued a result-date announcement on 1 November 2026. The result was subsequently declared on 6 November 2026, as confirmed by the September 2026 Foundation entry on the official results website.
The official results website confirms the announcement date. Candidates should use the result portal for individual marks and the published Foundation merit-list facility.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026 Important Dates

content.text: The September 2026 Foundation examination was conducted over four dates. ICAI announced the result date on 1 November and published the result on 6 November 2026.

sections.heading: How to Check ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026?

content.text: Candidates can check their Foundation examination results through the official ICAI result portal, which now lists the September 2026 Foundation result.

items: Visit the official result website at caresults.icai.org.
Click the Foundation - September 2026 entry under Check Results.
Open the Foundation result login page.
Enter your ICAI registration number.
Enter your examination roll number.
Complete any additional verification displayed by the portal.
Click the submit or check-result button.
View your CA Foundation September 2026 result.
Verify the paper-wise marks, total marks and result status.
Download or print the available scorecard for future reference.

content.text: ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026 - Official Scorecard Portal

links.text: ICAI CA Foundation Result 2026 - Official Scorecard Portal

sections.heading: CA Foundation Result 2026 Login Details

content.text: ICAI's official announcement specifically requires candidates to enter their registration number along with their roll number to access the result.

rows: If Displayed on the Result Portal

content.text: Candidates should keep their registration and roll numbers ready before accessing the result. They should not share their login details on unverified third-party websites.

sections.heading: Details Mentioned on CA Foundation Scorecard 2026

content.text: Candidates should check the marks and examination details displayed on their September 2026 scorecards.

items: Candidate Name
Registration Number
Examination Roll Number
Examination Session
Paper Names
Marks Obtained in Each Paper
Total Marks
Qualifying or Result Status
Other Information Displayed by ICAI

content.text: If a candidate finds any discrepancy, they should follow ICAI's official examination help and clarification procedure.

sections.heading: CA Foundation Passing Marks 2026

content.text: To pass the CA Foundation examination, candidates must score at least 40 marks out of 100 in each of the four papers and at least 200 marks out of 400 in aggregate.
Both conditions must be satisfied. Obtaining 200 or more marks in total is not sufficient if a candidate fails to secure the prescribed minimum marks in an individual paper.

sections.heading: CA Foundation September 2026 Result - Paper-Wise Marks

content.text: The Foundation examination consists of four papers, each carrying 100 marks.
Candidates should review their scorecards to understand their performance in each paper and whether they have satisfied both the paper-wise and aggregate qualifying requirements.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Foundation Pass Percentage September 2026

content.text: ICAI has declared the Foundation result. Candidates should refer to ICAI’s official examination statistics for the number of candidates who appeared, the number who passed and the pass percentage when these figures are published or verified.
The statistics may include the number of candidates who appeared, the number who passed and the overall pass percentage.
An official September 2026 Foundation pass-percentage figure has not been independently verified for this article. Figures from earlier sessions should not be presented as September 2026 statistics.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Foundation Toppers List 2026

content.text: The official result portal now lists a Foundation September 2026 merit-list entry. Candidates can use that facility to check available merit-list information. Individual topper names and ranks have not been independently verified for this article.
Rank-holder names and marks should be published only when supported by the official merit list or a verified ICAI announcement.

sections.heading: CA Foundation Result 2026 - Is There a Separate Cut Off?

content.text: The primary qualifying requirements for the CA Foundation examination are the prescribed minimum marks in each paper and the overall aggregate.

These requirements are different from a competitive recruitment examination in which selection may depend on a vacancy-based cut-off. Candidates should refer to ICAI's examination rules for the applicable passing standard rather than relying on speculative cut-off predictions.

sections.heading: What Happens After CA Foundation Result 2026?

content.text: Candidates who pass the September 2026 CA Foundation examination can proceed towards the Chartered Accountancy Intermediate course, subject to ICAI's applicable course-registration and training requirements.
Candidates who do not qualify may consider appearing in a subsequent Foundation examination session, following the Institute's registration and examination-application rules.
All candidates should retain their result information and follow the official ICAI Student Services Portal for further course-related instructions.

sections.heading: CA Foundation January 2027 Examination

content.text: ICAI's next Foundation examination session is scheduled for January 2027. Candidates planning to appear in that session should follow the official examination application schedule and eligibility instructions.
The January 2027 examination application window opened on 3 November 2026, with the regular application deadline reported as 16 November 2026 and the late-fee deadline as 19 November 2026.
These dates relate to the next examination session, not the September 2026 result declaration.

sections.heading: What to Do If CA Foundation Result 2026 Is Not Opening?

content.text: If the ICAI result portal temporarily fails to load or a candidate cannot access their result, they should verify their details and retry through the official website.

items: Open caresults.icai.org.
Select the Foundation - September 2026 result entry.
Verify your registration number and examination roll number.
Complete any additional portal verification correctly.
Try opening the page again if there is a temporary technical error.
Check the official ICAI announcements for updates.
Contact ICAI through its official examination-support channels if the issue continues.

detail.title: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 Overview
detail.short_info: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 covers six main units: The Productive Mechanism, Theory of Demand and Supply, Market, Banking in India, Inflation and Consumer Awareness. Students preparing for the ICSE 2027 examination should study the prescribed concepts, diagrams, banking functions, public finance and consumer protection measures. Economics carries 80 marks for the two-hour theory examination and 20 marks for internal assessment

content.text: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 covers six major units for students preparing for the ICSE 2027 board examination. The syllabus includes The Productive Mechanism, Theory of Demand and Supply, Market, Banking in India, Inflation and Consumer Awareness. The Economics examination carries 80 marks in theory and 20 marks in internal assessment, with a two-hour written paper.

Students should prepare the complete chapter-wise syllabus, including important economic concepts, demand and supply curves, banking functions, inflation and consumer rights. The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) publishes its official syllabuses through cisce.org. Candidates should select the syllabus labelled Examination Year 2027.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 Chapter-Wise

content.text: The Economics syllabus for the ICSE Class 10 examination covers six major units. Each unit contains several concepts and subtopics that students should prepare.

rows: Land, Labour, Capital, Entrepreneur and Factors of Production
Demand, Supply, Curves, Laws, Elasticity and Determinants
Perfect Competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly
Money, Commercial Banks, Central Bank, Monetary Policy and Public Finance
Stages, Types, Causes and Effects of Inflation
Consumer Rights, Consumer Protection, RTI, PDS and Quality Certification

sections.heading: Unit 1: The Productive Mechanism

content.text: This unit introduces the four major factors of production and explains their contribution to economic activities.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning and characteristics of land as a factor of production.
Productivity of land and factors affecting land productivity.
Meaning and characteristics of labour.
Division of labour, its types and advantages.
Efficiency of labour and reasons for low labour efficiency in India.
Meaning and characteristics of capital.
Physical and financial capital with examples.
Capital formation, its process and importance.
Meaning of entrepreneur.
Functions of an entrepreneur and contribution to economic development.

content.text: Students should understand the differences among land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship and explain how each contributes to production.

sections.heading: Unit 2: Theory of Demand and Supply

content.text: This unit examines how consumer demand and market supply are related to price and other economic factors.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning and concept of demand and supply.
Types of demand.
Law of demand and law of supply.
Individual and market demand schedules.
Individual and market supply schedules.
Demand and supply curves.
Movement along demand and supply curves.
Shift in demand and supply curves.
Determinants of demand and supply.
Exceptions to the law of demand.
Meaning and types of elasticity of demand.
Meaning and types of elasticity of supply.
Percentage method of measuring price elasticity.
Factors affecting elasticity of demand and supply.

content.text: Students should practise drawing and interpreting demand and supply curves and clearly distinguish a movement along a curve from a shift of the entire curve.

Important: The accessible CISCE Economics syllabus reference specifies that numerical problems on elasticity are not for testing. Students should follow the corresponding instructions in their Examination Year 2027 document when preparing.

sections.heading: Unit 3: Market

content.text: The Market unit covers the meaning of a market and the different types of market structures.

rows: A Market with Many Buyers and Sellers
A Market with a Single Seller
Competition Among Sellers Offering Differentiated Products
A Market Dominated by a Small Number of Sellers

sections.heading: Unit 4: Banking in India

content.text: Banking in India is a broad unit that includes money, commercial banks, central banking, monetary policy and public finance.

sections.heading: Money

items: Barter system and its limitations.
Evolution and legal meaning of money.
Money as a medium of exchange.
Money as a measure of value.
Money as a store of value.
Money as a standard of deferred payment.

sections.heading: Commercial Banks

items: Meaning and functions of commercial banks.
Types of bank deposits.
Types of loans and methods of advancing loans.
Basic process of credit creation.
Primary and derivative deposits.

sections.heading: Central Bank and Monetary Policy

items: Meaning and functions of the central bank.
Issue of currency notes.
Banker's bank and lender of last resort.
Banker, agent and adviser to the government.
Custodian of foreign exchange.
Qualitative credit control methods, including moral suasion, margin requirements and credit rationing.
Quantitative credit control methods, including Bank Rate, Open Market Operations, Cash Reserve Ratio and Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
Basic understanding of demonetisation.

sections.heading: Public Finance

items: Meaning of public finance.
Sources of public revenue.
Direct and indirect taxes and their differences.
Meaning and objectives of Goods and Services Tax (GST).
Progressive, proportional, regressive and degressive taxes.
Non-tax revenue with examples.
Public expenditure and its classification.
Revenue expenditure and capital expenditure.
Reasons for increasing public expenditure.
Meaning and types of public debt.

content.text: Students should particularly practise comparison questions covering commercial banks and central banks, qualitative and quantitative credit controls, and direct and indirect taxation.

sections.heading: Unit 5: Inflation

content.text: This unit focuses on the meaning, categories, causes and economic effects of inflation.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning of inflation.
Creeping inflation.
Walking inflation.
Running inflation.
Hyperinflation.
Demand-pull inflation.
Cost-push inflation.
Causes of demand-pull and cost-push inflation.
Differences between the two main types of inflation.
Negative effects of inflation on production.
Effects of inflation on fixed-income earners and business-income groups.

content.text: Students should understand the differences among inflation types and explain their effects using simple examples.

sections.heading: Unit 6: Consumer Awareness

content.text: The final unit deals with consumer exploitation, rights, duties and protection mechanisms.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning of consumer exploitation.
Forms and reasons for consumer exploitation.
Meaning and importance of consumer awareness.
Consumer rights and consumer duties.
Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Right to Information (RTI).
Food adulteration and its harmful effects.
Public Distribution System (PDS).
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).
AGMARK certification.
ECOMARK certification.

content.text: Students should be able to explain how consumer rights, consumer protection laws and standardisation marks help protect buyers.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Exam Pattern 2027

content.text: The Economics examination combines a written theory paper with an internal project or assignment.

The official subject syllabus specifies the overall assessment division. Students should refer to the specimen question paper for the question format, section-wise choices and applicable marking instructions.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Chapter-Wise Marks Distribution

content.text: The syllabus establishes the six required units but does not provide a confirmed fixed marks allocation for each individual chapter.
Students should not assume that every unit carries equal marks or rely on unofficial chapter-wise weightage tables as guaranteed examination allocations.
Prepare all six units and use the official specimen papers and previous examination papers to understand the expected question format.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Internal Assessment 2026-27

content.text: Students must complete at least one Economics project or assignment prescribed by their teacher.
The internal assessment carries 20 marks. The subject teacher and an external examiner assess the project independently.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Project Topics

content.text: The published syllabus provides project and assignment examples related to factors of production, taxation and GST.

sections.heading: Project 1: Factors of Production

content.text: Visit a local industrial unit and study how land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship are combined in the production process.

sections.heading: Project 2: Survey on Taxes

content.text: Conduct a survey of 15 people in the neighbourhood to study the types of taxes they pay. Analyse which type of tax respondents find easier to pay and explain the conclusion.

sections.heading: Project 3: Impact of GST

content.text: Visit a nearby store and select five commonly purchased products. Examine the impact of GST on their prices or demand and discuss the benefits or implications for producers, consumers and the government.
The final project topic, submission format and assessment requirements should be confirmed with the school's Economics teacher.

sections.heading: How to Download ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27?

items: Visit the official CISCE website at cisce.org.
Open the syllabus or regulations and syllabuses section.
Select the ICSE examination.
Choose the syllabus corresponding to Examination Year 2027.
Find Economics under the Group II subjects.
Open the Economics (64) syllabus document.
Verify that its cover or page headings refer to Examination Year 2027.
Download and save the PDF for examination preparation.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics 2026-27 Preparation Tips

items: Begin preparation with the six units listed in the syllabus.
Learn important definitions and distinguish closely related economic concepts.
Practise demand and supply schedules and curves.
Prepare comparison tables for different market structures.
Understand banking functions, GST and monetary policy terminology.
Revise inflation types, their causes and effects.
Learn consumer rights, duties and important consumer protection measures.
Complete the Economics project according to the teacher's instructions.
Use official specimen and past examination papers for revision.
Revise the complete syllabus instead of relying on unverified chapter weightage.

sections.heading: Difference Between ICSE Economics and Economic Applications

content.text: ICSE Economics and Economic Applications are separate subjects with different subject codes and syllabus requirements.

Mock Test Paper Series I will begin on 1 December 2026, while Series II will start on 14 December 2026. Students preparing for the January 2027 Foundation examination can participate in physical or virtual mode and download the official timetable from icai.org.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Foundation January 2027 Mock Test Schedule Released

content.text: The Board of Studies (Academic) of ICAI has announced two Mock Test Paper series for students preparing for the CA Foundation January 2027 examination.
The official announcement, dated 21 October 2026, states that Series I will commence on 1 December and Series II will commence on 14 December.
Students can attempt these mock tests virtually or through physical sessions organised by ICAI branches and regional offices.
The tests are designed to help candidates practise answering examination papers within the prescribed duration and assess their preparation before the January 2027 examination.

content.text: The first mock test series will run from 1 to 9 December 2026, with four papers on separate dates.
Accounting and Business Laws have a three-hour duration each. Quantitative Aptitude and Business Economics have a two-hour duration each.

sections.heading: CA Foundation January 2027 Mock Test Series 2 Schedule

content.text: The second mock test series will be conducted from 14 to 21 December 2026, providing another opportunity to practise all four CA Foundation subjects.

content.text: ICAI has announced that answer keys will be uploaded within 48 hours of the scheduled commencement of the respective mock test paper.

Students can use the mock papers as a preparation resource and check with their local branch about the physical test facility.

The December mock test series is separate from the actual CA Foundation examination. Students should consult ICAI's examination notification and admit card for confirmed paper-wise examination details.

content.text: AACCC permits only one counselling registration application per candidate. Multiple applications can lead to debarment or other action under the counselling rules.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Eligibility Criteria

content.text: Candidates seeking AACCC postgraduate counselling must have qualified in AIAPGET 2026 and satisfy the applicable academic and institutional admission conditions.
The counselling covers eligible MD/MS postgraduate programmes in Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy.
Admission is subject to the relevant entrance examination merit, qualifying degree, internship requirements, institutional eligibility and applicable regulatory provisions.
Final eligibility is verified by the allotted institution. Merely registering for counselling does not guarantee a postgraduate seat.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Choice Filling and Locking

content.text: Round 1 choice filling begins on 27 October and ends on 1 November 2026 at 11:55 PM.
Choice locking will be available on 1 November from 2 PM to 11:55 PM.
Candidates should check the available college and course options, confirm the applicable fees and arrange preferences according to their actual admission choices.
Once choices are locked, AACCC does not allow candidates to modify them. Students should therefore review the college, course and preference order carefully.
Earlier-round choices do not automatically remain valid for all subsequent counselling rounds. Candidates must submit fresh choices where required under the counselling scheme.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Round 1 Seat Allotment Result

content.text: AACCC will process the first-round seat allotment on 2 November 2026 and publish the result on 3 November 2026.
The allotment will be determined according to the applicable candidate merit, eligibility, preferences, category and available seats.
Candidates who receive seats should download the individual allotment information through the official portal and complete the prescribed joining formalities between 4 and 13 November.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Reporting and Admission Confirmation

content.text: After seat allotment, eligible candidates must report to the allotted institution within the scheduled reporting period.
The college will verify the candidate's academic qualifications, examination result, internship and category-related documents, where applicable.
AACCC instructs students to obtain an online-generated provisional admission letter after completing physical reporting.
Admission confirmation and any subsequent relieving or withdrawal must be processed through the official AACCC system. Offline changes are not recognised under the counselling scheme.

content.text: The final document checklist depends on the candidate's course, category and allotted institution. Students must follow the current official information bulletin and college-specific instructions.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Security Deposit Refund and Forfeiture Rules

content.text: The registration fee is non-refundable. The security deposit may be refunded after completion of the counselling process if the candidate satisfies the refund conditions.

AACCC states that security money can be forfeited if a candidate does not join an allotted seat in Round 2 or later rounds, withdraws contrary to the counselling rules, or fails to comply with prescribed conditions.

There is no free exit from an allotted Round 3 or stray vacancy seat under the specified rules. Withdrawal or non-joining can also make a candidate ineligible for further AYUSH postgraduate counselling.
Candidates should read the official forfeiture and eligibility rules before deciding not to join an allotted seat.

items: BITSAT 2026 application number.
Password or date of birth used at registration.
Access to the registered email ID / mobile number in case you need to recover login details.

sections.heading: Details Printed on BITSAT 2026 Admit Card

content.text: Candidates must verify all the information printed on the BITSAT admit card and ensure it matches their application details.
Typical details include:

items: Candidate’s name, photograph and signature (if printed).
BITSAT 2026 application number / roll number.
Exam date and time slot allotted.
Test centre name, complete address and test city.
Reporting time and gate closing time.
Instructions regarding acceptable ID proofs and permitted items.
General exam-day rules and code of conduct.

content.text: If any detail is incorrect or unclear, candidates should contact the BITS admission office immediately.

sections.heading: BITSAT 2026 Exam Date, Slot and Centre Allotment

content.text: BITSAT 2026 Exam Schedule and Slot

BITSAT is usually conducted over multiple days and in several time slots. The specific date and slot allotted to each candidate will be mentioned clearly on the BITSAT 2026 admit card. Candidates must carefully note the slot printed on the admit card and appear for the test only at that date and time.
BITSAT 2026 Test Centre Allotment

Test centres are allotted based on the preferences filled in the BITSAT application form and the availability of seats at each centre. Once a test centre is allotted and mentioned on the admit card, change of centre is normally not allowed, so candidates must plan travel and reporting time accordingly.

sections.heading: Documents to Carry with BITSAT 2026 Admit Card

content.text: Bringing the correct documents to the test centre is essential to avoid rejection at the entry gate.
Mandatory Documents on Exam Day

items: Printed BITSAT 2026 admit card (preferably in colour, though black-and-white is usually accepted unless otherwise specified).
A valid photo ID proof such as Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, Driving Licence, or School/College ID as per the latest instructions.
Recent passport-size photographs if mentioned in the exam instructions.

content.text: Items Not Allowed Inside BITSAT Exam Centre

items: Mobile phones, smart watches, Bluetooth devices, earphones or any form of electronic gadget.
Calculators, digital diaries, programmable watches or any calculation device (unless specifically allowed).
Books, notes, written slips and any other study material.

sections.heading: Important Instructions on BITSAT 2026 Admit Card

content.text: The BITSAT admit card will contain essential instructions that candidates must follow strictly.
Key instructions typically include:

items: Reach the exam centre at least 60 minutes before the reporting time to complete security checks and registration.
Carry the admit card and photo ID in original; photocopies of ID may not be accepted.
Do not carry prohibited items to the exam lab; there may not be any facility for safe-keeping of personal belongings.
Follow the invigilator’s guidelines for logging in to the computer, navigating between questions and submitting the test.
Any kind of malpractice or misconduct can lead to cancellation of candidature and further disciplinary action.

sections.heading: What to Do If There Is an Error or Download Issue

content.text: Incorrect Details / Photo on BITSAT 2026 Admit Card
If you notice mistakes such as wrong name spelling, incorrect date, wrong centre or unclear photograph, you should:

items: Immediately contact the BITS admission office using the helpline number or email given in the information brochure.
Provide your application number, registered email ID and a detailed description of the error.
Follow the instructions given by the authorities and complete any required correction process before the exam day.

content.text: Unable to Download BITSAT Admit Card 2026
If the website is not opening or the admit card is not downloading:

items: Check your internet connection and browser; try clearing cache or using a different browser/device.
Ensure that you are entering the correct application number and password/date of birth.
If the problem persists, reach out to the admission helpline with your registration details and screenshot of the issue, if possible.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Gujarat NEET UG Counselling 2026 Round 2

items: Visit the official website, medadmgujarat.org.
Click on the link for "UG Medical / Dental / Ayurvedic & Homoeopathy Admission."
Select "Purchase PIN" (skip this step if you already hold a valid PIN from Round 1).
Enter your NEET UG 2026 roll number, name, email address, and mobile number, and complete the PIN payment.
Log in using the PIN and your NEET UG/Class 12 details.
Fill in personal details - name, category, domicile status, contact information - and upload the required documents.
Set a password (typically 6–12 alphanumeric characters) for future logins.
Review and confirm all entered details, since registration details generally cannot be edited after confirmation.
Print the Registration Details/Slip, selecting a preferred Help Centre along with an available date and time slot for document verification.
Visit the chosen Help Centre in person with original documents and self-attested photocopies to complete verification and collect the signed Registration Acknowledgement Slip.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Complete both online registration and in-person document verification within the notified deadlines - registration alone does not confirm participation in seat allotment.
Safely preserve the PIN and password until the entire admission process, including any final fee refund, is complete. Do not share the PIN with anyone.
Choice filling is compulsory in every counselling round for candidates who wish to be considered for seat allotment.
Help Centres generally remain closed on Sundays and public holidays; plan verification visits accordingly.
Keep checking the official website regularly for updates on the merit list, choice filling, and seat allotment schedule for Round 2, as some dates were not available at the time of writing.

content.text: Candidates can follow the steps below to download the Haryana nursing Round 1 merit list.

items: Visit the official counselling portal at nursing.online-counselling.co.in.
Find the Round 1 provisional merit list notice or link.
Select the applicable course: ANM, GNM or MPHW (Male).
Open the course-wise provisional or revised merit list PDF.
Use the PDF search function to locate the candidate's Application ID or name.
Check the merit number, qualifying stream and aggregate marks.
Download and save the merit list PDF for future reference.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Admission is by Class 12 merit only. There is no entrance exam. Admission is based on Class 12 merit through centralised counselling. Pt. B.D. Sharma University of Health Sciences, Rohtak, conducts the combined online counselling.

Only registered candidates are on the list. Admission is made through online centralised counselling from the list of registered candidates, as per merit in the qualifying exam. If you missed the October 26 to 28 registration window, you won’t appear in Round 1.

Check your name, marks and category. In case of a tie in marks, a tie-breaking rule applies. Check that the marks, category and the 5% relaxation for GNM are right if you claim them. SC, SC (Deprived), BC-A, BC-B and PwBD candidates get a 5% relaxation in merit for GNM.

Fill choices carefully and on time. Choice filling opens before the merit list is out, so fill your preferences carefully and on time. Seats are allotted by merit and your choices, so lock them before the deadline. Check the seat split before you choose. All government institution seats are State Quota, while private institutions offer 50% State Quota and 50% Management Quota. Also, a candidate who is found ineligible or who gives false information can be debarred for three years. Keep your documents ready for verification.

detail.short_info: Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026 registration and choice filling are open from September 28 to October 10. Check important dates, registration steps, seat allotment and joining deadline.

content.text: Pt. B. D. Sharma University of Health Sciences (UHSR), Rohtak has released the schedule for Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026. Registration, editing, choice filling and choice locking run from September 28, 2026 to October 10, 2026 (till 11:59 PM). The provisional seat allotment will be released on October 12, 2026.

This counselling is for eligible NEET UG 2026 candidates seeking MBBS or BDS admission in government, government-aided, private medical and private dental colleges, and specified private and minority universities in Haryana. Always confirm details on the official counselling website, uhsrugcounselling.com, before acting.

rows: Pt. B. D. Sharma University of Health Sciences (UHSR), Rohtak

sections.heading: Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026 Important Dates

content.text: Every step in Round 3 has a fixed deadline. Missing one can cost you your chance in this round.

rows: Registration, Editing, Choice Filling and Locking

sections.heading: How to Register for Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026

content.text: The whole process is online. Follow these steps:

items: Visit the official counselling website, uhsrugcounselling.com.
Click the Round 3 registration link.
Enter your NEET UG 2026 roll number and the other required details.
Upload the required documents in the prescribed format.
Pay the required security amount online.
Select your preferred MBBS and BDS colleges and courses.
Arrange the colleges in the order you prefer.
Lock your choices before the October 10 deadline.
Download the confirmation page and keep it for future use.

sections.heading: Choice Filling Is Fresh for Round 3

content.text: You must submit new choices in Round 3. Choices filled in Round 1 or Round 2 will not be considered. If you want an upgrade, plan your preference list carefully before you lock it.

sections.heading: Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Seat Allotment 2026

content.text: The provisional seat allotment will be released on October 12, 2026. If you find a problem with your allotment, you can submit a grievance on the same day. Candidates who receive a seat must then pay the provisional tuition fee between October 12 and October 14, 2026 (till 11:00 PM).
The source does not give the seat matrix, previous-year cut-offs, or tuition fee amounts. These details are not available in the official source used for this article.

sections.heading: Important Rules for Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026

items: Round 1 or Round 2 candidates who did not get a seat do not need to register again.
Fresh candidates must register within the Round 3 window.
Fresh choices are mandatory because old choices will not be considered.
Candidates who want an upgrade must submit their willingness online.
Paying the security deposit is compulsory.
If you do not join after being allotted a seat, your security deposit is forfeited and you cannot take part in the stray vacancy round.
Check the official UHSR counselling website regularly for updates and notices.

items: Check the merit list on the official site. Use hpbose.org, as the board publishes the merit list there with topper names, marks, ranks and percentages. The top-ranked student is Anmol from Kangra, who scored 699 out of 700, or 99.86%. The overall pass percentage was 83.87%.

The re-evaluation window is closed. One source puts the re-evaluation and re-checking application window at May 10 to 25, 2026. Don’t rely on that, because I didn’t see an official HPBOSE notice for it. Improvement exams count towards later merit. One source says a second opportunity examination was set for June 2026 for students wishing to improve their scores, and its results are considered for the final merit list and Class 11 admission. sections.heading: HPBOSE D.El.Ed Counselling 2026: Seat-Allotment Procedure

content.text: As per the official prospectus, counselling works as follows:

items: HPBOSE prepares a merit list based purely on total marks scored in the CET (no interview is conducted).
Candidates are called for counselling strictly in order of merit, category-wise, as per the reservation roster.
The date, time and venue for each counselling round is announced only on the official HPBOSE website - no individual letters, faxes or phone calls are sent to candidates.
At counselling, eligibility is finally verified against original documents.

Seats are allotted according to the candidate's stated institution preference and the seats available at that candidate's turn. This preference can be exercised only once - once a seat is accepted, it is final, and the candidate cannot request a change of institution.
A candidate who accepts a seat in one round cannot participate in later rounds for re-allotment.
Unfilled or vacated seats are carried forward to the next round strictly by merit.
There is no migration allowed between institutions after admission - neither between DIETs nor between private colleges.

sections.heading: How to Apply / Register for HPBOSE D.El.Ed CET and Counselling

items: Visit the official HPBOSE website: hpbose.org.
Click on the "CET / Vacancy" section, then select the D.El.Ed (CET) 2026 link.
Register and fill in personal, educational, category and exam-centre preference details in capital letters exactly as per your Matriculation certificate.
Upload a scanned photograph (JPG, under 20 KB, 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm) and signature (JPG, under 15 KB, 3.5 cm x 1.5 cm).
Pay the application fee online via net banking, debit card or credit card.
Submit the declaration and download/print the confirmation page for your records.
After the result and merit list are announced, regularly check hpbose.org for your counselling call - no separate communication is sent by post or courier.
Attend counselling in person on the notified date with all original documents, and exercise your institution preference to get your seat allotted.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: The information provided in the online application (name, date of birth, category, etc.) is treated as final and generally cannot be changed once the correction window closes.
No separate letter, fax, email or phone call is sent for any round of counselling - candidates must track hpbose.org themselves.
There is no job guarantee from the Government of Himachal Pradesh after completing the D.El.Ed course.

sections.heading: What Is HPCET 2026 Counselling?

content.text: This section explains the basic purpose of HPCET counselling for readers who are new to the process.

HPCET counselling is the centralised admission process conducted by HPTU, Hamirpur, for candidates who have qualified the Himachal Pradesh Common Entrance Test. Through this process, qualified candidates register online, fill their course and college preferences, and get seats allotted based on their rank, category, and seat availability. The counselling applies to admissions across HPTU's affiliated government and private institutes in Himachal Pradesh.

content.text: This section walks candidates through the step-by-step process to complete counselling registration at himtu.ac.in.

Pay the applicable counselling fee through net banking, debit card, or credit card.
Fill course and college preferences in order of priority from the available seat matrix.
Lock your choices before the deadline; unlocked choices may be auto-considered as locked once the window closes.
Submit the form and save/print the confirmation page for future reference.

content.text: This section breaks down the complete counselling journey from registration to admission confirmation.
The HPCET 2026 counselling procedure includes the following stages:

items: Online Registration: Candidates register at himtu.ac.in and pay the counselling fee within the notified window.
Choice Filling: Candidates select course and college preferences from the published seat matrix, in order of priority.
Locking of Choices: Preferences must be locked before the deadline; any choices left unlocked may be treated as locked automatically.
Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on HPCET 2026 rank, category, preferences submitted, and seat availability.
Document Verification: Allotted candidates upload or present documents for verification.
Admission Fee Payment: Candidates confirm their allotted seat by paying the admission fee.
Reporting to Institute: Candidates report to the allotted institute with original documents within the specified timeline.

Once a seat is allotted, candidates must confirm admission within the notified deadline through document verification and fee payment. Candidates who fail to confirm admission by the deadline risk cancellation of their allotted seat. HPTU typically conducts multiple counselling rounds including a mop-up/stray vacancy round to fill any seats that remain vacant after the initial rounds.

content.text: The HP PAT 2026 merit list is published alongside the result on hptechboard.com. It ranks all qualified candidates based on their total marks obtained in the entrance examination. Understanding how ties are resolved helps candidates know exactly where they stand.
In cases where two or more candidates score identical marks, the board applies a tie-breaking formula in the following order of priority:

items: Marks in Chemistry - The candidate with higher Chemistry marks ranks higher.

Age - In case of a further tie, the older candidate is given the higher rank.
