sections.heading: How to Calculate Marks Using HPCET 2026 Answer Key

content.text: Once the tentative answer key is downloaded, candidates can estimate their HPCET 2026 score by applying the marking scheme to their responses. The marking scheme for each paper is given in the official HPCET 2026 information brochure, and candidates must follow that pattern only.
The general process is as follows:

items: Note down the total number of questions and marks per question for your paper as mentioned in the HPCET 2026 exam pattern.
For every correct answer that matches the option given in the answer key, add the full marks allotted per question.
For every wrong answer, deduct marks as per the negative marking specified in the brochure.
No marks are added or deducted for questions which were left unanswered.
After going through all questions, total your marks to get your approximate score in HPCET 2026 for that specific course.

content.text: For example, if a paper carries 100 questions with 2 marks each and 0.5 marks negative per wrong answer, and a candidate gets 70 questions correct and 20 wrong, the estimated score will be: Correct: 70 × 2 = 140 Wrong: 20 × 0.5 = 10 (to be deducted) Estimated score = 140 − 10 = 130
This calculated score is only indicative; the final result will be based on the University’s evaluation and the final answer key.

items: For B.Tech and B.Pharmacy: Candidates must have passed 10+2 or equivalent examination from a recognised board with the required combination of subjects and minimum aggregate marks stipulated by HPTU.

HPCET 2026 Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
HPCET is conducted in offline mode as a pen‑and‑paper OMR based test. The exam pattern varies slightly from course to course, but some common features are:

items: The question paper consists of objective type multiple-choice questions.
The medium of the question paper is generally English.
Each question carries equal marks and there is negative marking for incorrect answers as per the official scheme for that particular programme.

detail.title: Ladakh MBBS BDS Admission 2026 - Overview
detail.short_info: Ladakh's Health & Medical Education Department has revised the Central Pool MBBS and BDS admission guidelines for 2026-27, replacing the old category-wise roster with a single NEET merit list.

content.text: The Health & Medical Education (H&ME) Department, Union Territory of Ladakh, issued revised guidelines on September 22, 2026, for admission to MBBS and BDS seats under the Central Pool. The revision replaces the existing category-wise roster system with a single merit list based purely on NEET ranking. The change was made following the creation of seven new districts in Ladakh and was approved by Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena. For the 2026-27 academic session, the Centre has allotted 7 MBBS seats and 2 BDS seats to Ladakh under the Central Pool.

content.text: Jharkhand NEET UG Counselling 2026 has been started by the Jharkhand Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (JCECEB) for admission to MBBS and BDS courses under the 85% state quota in government and private medical and dental colleges of Jharkhand. Online registration is open from August 7 to August 11, 2026 (up to 3:00 PM), the state merit list will be published on August 12, 2026, and Round 1 online counselling will begin from August 13, 2026. This article explains the complete Jharkhand NEET UG Counselling 2026 schedule, eligibility, security deposit/fee details, required documents, and the step-by-step application process, based on the official JCECEB notification.

content.text: Candidates participating in Jharkhand NEET UG Counselling 2026 are required to pay a refundable security deposit at the time of registration/choice filling. The amount varies by category and type of college:

rows: SC, ST, OBC and PwD candidates (Government colleges)

content.text: As per JCECEB, the security deposit is refundable within three months after the completion of the last round of counselling, subject to prescribed conditions.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Jharkhand NEET UG Counselling 2026

items: Visit the official JCECEB website at jceceb.jharkhand.gov.in.
Click on the Jharkhand NEET UG Counselling 2026 registration link.
Register using your NEET UG 2026 roll number and required basic details to create a login.
Fill in the online application form with personal, academic, and category details.
Upload the required scanned documents and photographs as per the specified format.
Pay the applicable registration/security deposit amount online.
Submit the form and download/save the confirmation page for future reference.
After the merit list is published, log in again to complete online choice filling within the specified window.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Complete registration before the deadline of August 11, 2026 (3:00 PM); late submissions are typically not accepted.
Ensure all uploaded documents are clear, valid, and match the details in the NEET UG 2026 application.
Keep a valid, active mobile number and email ID linked to the counselling registration for OTPs and official communication.
Regularly check the official JCECEB website for updates on merit list corrections, seat matrix release, and round-wise schedules.
Candidates who wish to withdraw from the state quota process should carefully review the applicable withdrawal and refund rules before doing so.

sections.heading: Who Can Check This Result

content.text: This result applies to UG students enrolled under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 structure who appeared for the Semester 1 examination under the 2025-2029 admission session, as well as students appearing for the backlog (re-appear/failed) papers of Semester 1. SKMU's result portal also lists Semester 1 results for other NEP batches (2022-26, 2023-27, 2024-28) on the same page, so make sure you select the correct batch and exam year before searching.

content.text: The provisional merit list is an initial rank list prepared by DET Jharkhand based on the marks candidates scored in their qualifying Class 8th or Class 10th examination. items: Open the official SKMU result portal: https://exam.skmu.ac.in/resultskmu/result

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Choose an option when the allotment comes out. In Round 1, KEA warned that candidates who don’t select a choice within the deadline are treated as not interested in the seat and moved to choice-4. Don’t miss the window.

Choice-1 means fee, slip and reporting. Choice-1 candidates must download the seat confirmation slip and report to the allotted college by the stated deadline. Pay the fee online before that, because the allotment is cancelled if you skip any of these steps.

Surrendering a seat may need an in-person visit. For Round 1, KEA required that candidates surrendering a choice 1 or 2 seat do so in person at the KEA office in Bengaluru by a fixed time. Check whether Round 4 uses the same rule.

Later rounds may have fewer choices. In Round 1 candidates had all four choice options available. In later UGCET rounds, KEA said choices 2 and 3 would not be available. NEET Round 4 may be similarly restricted, so read the choice rules in the notice carefully.

Keep your documents and the official schedule at hand. Carry your NEET UG 2026 scorecard and admit card, along with the allotment letter and fee receipt. KEA often extends deadlines, but don’t count on it. Follow only kea.kar.nic.in for dates.

Home State (Tamil Nadu) quota: One report puts the Round 5 closing rank at 4,015 for home state and 1,373 for other state. Round 4 CSE is listed at 1034 to 3812. Home State ranks are much more relaxed than OS ranks.

Rank and percentile: CSE at OS generally needs a General rank under about 1,500. This is a rough guide, since the final cutoff is only set by the round-wise counselling outcome.

Verify on the official portal: Third-party reporting of final-round figures has been inconsistent, so verify them on the JoSAA OR-CR portal at josaa.nic.in. I couldn’t confirm an official 2026 final-round figure, and some sites mix 2025 and 2026 data.

How to Apply for CEE Kerala DNB Post MBBS 2026?

content.text: CEE Kerala has specified five mandatory application steps.

items: Visit the official DNB Post MBBS 2026 application portal.
Click Registration and enter the required mobile number and email address.
Create a password and save the system-generated application number.
Log in using the application number and password.
Complete the application form with personal, educational, NEET PG and applicable Government service details.
Pay the prescribed application fee of Rs. 1,000 plus gateway charges.
Upload the required images and certificates.
Complete option registration by selecting the applicable course, speciality and institution preferences.
Review the completed application and option details.
Download or print the acknowledgement page for future reference.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Eligibility is limited. All the State quota seats are earmarked for In-Service candidates (Medical Education, Health Service or Insurance Medical Service of the Govt. of Kerala), and you must hold an MBBS degree.

Apply online only, on the CEE website. The 2025 round let candidates apply online through the CEE website until 06.11.2025, 12.00 PM. The 2026 deadline will be in the new notification, and no late submissions are accepted.
The fee is Rs 1,000, paid online. In earlier rounds, it was non-refundable. The 2026 Post Diploma notice says payment is by credit card, debit card or net banking.

Upload your documents with the application. After paying, you must upload your photo, signature and the required certificates, such as proof of nativity. Nothing can be submitted after the last date, so have all of it scanned in advance.

Register your options and skip the printout. You must select and order your options (speciality and institution combinations) as part of the online application, and the application is complete only after options are registered. There is no need to send a printout of the acknowledgement page or any documents to the CEE office. Still, save the acknowledgement page for your records.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 1 Seat Allotment Result 2026 Released

content.text: The Directorate of Medical Education, Madhya Pradesh, has announced the first-round provisional seat allotment result for NEET PG 2026 counselling. The result was released on 29 October 2026 for candidates who completed the required registration and choice filling procedures.
The allotment has been prepared based on candidates' state merit positions, submitted college and course preferences, applicable reservation categories and available postgraduate medical seats.

Candidates can check the published allotment list to identify their allotted institution, postgraduate course and relevant seat category. The result is provisional, and admission remains subject to verification of documents and completion of the prescribed formalities.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Counselling 2026 Round 1 Important Dates

content.text: DME Madhya Pradesh has announced the Round 1 result and the subsequent reporting, upgradation and resignation schedule. Candidates should carefully note that the reporting and upgradation deadlines have different closing times.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Counselling 2026 Round 1 Result Download Link

content.text: Candidates can access the Round 1 provisional allotment list through the official DME MPOnline counselling website. The allotment list is published in PDF format, while individual provisional allotment letters are available through candidate login.

rows: Round 1 Opening and Closing Rank PDF

content.text: The two direct PDF addresses above were publicly shared as official-domain result links but could not be independently opened during verification. Candidates should use the main counselling portal if either direct link is unavailable.

sections.heading: How to Download MP NEET PG Round 1 Result 2026?

content.text: Candidates can follow these steps to check the MP NEET PG 2026 Round 1 provisional seat allotment result.

items: Visit the official counselling portal at dme.mponline.gov.in.
Open the PG Medical Counselling section for MD/MS admissions.
Find the First Round Allotment List for MP State Combined NEET PG Counselling 2026.
Open the provisional allotment result PDF.
Use the PDF search option to find the candidate's NEET PG roll number or name.
Check the allotted college, course and applicable seat category.
Download the PDF for future reference.
Log in to the candidate account to download the individual provisional allotment letter if a seat has been allotted.

content.text: The individual allotment letter is required for the subsequent admission process. Candidates should not rely only on a screenshot or the general allotment list when reporting to their allotted institution.

sections.heading: Details to Check in MP NEET PG Round 1 Allotment List 2026

content.text: The Round 1 allotment list provides information about candidates and the postgraduate medical seats allotted through state counselling.
Candidates should check the following details, wherever shown in the official result document:

items: Candidate's Name
NEET PG Roll Number
State Common Merit Rank
NEET PG All India Rank
Candidate Category
Allotted Medical College
Allotted Course and Speciality
Allotted Seat Category or Quota

content.text: Candidates should verify that their allotted course and institution match the information in their individual allotment letter. Any discrepancy should be through the official counselling or allotted college authorities.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG 2026 Provisional Allotment Letter

content.text: Candidates who have received a seat in the first round must download their provisional allotment letters through the official DME MPOnline candidate login.

The allotment letter contains the admission details required for reporting to the allotted medical institution. It must be presented along with the applicable original documents during the verification process.

Downloading the allotment letter does not by itself complete the admission process. Candidates must satisfy the document verification, fee payment and reporting requirements within the prescribed schedule.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 1 Reporting Dates 2026

content.text: Physical reporting and admission at allotted medical colleges will take place between 30 October and 10 November 2026, up to 6:00 PM.
Candidates who have been allotted a postgraduate medical seat must report in person to their respective institutions for the prescribed verification and admission procedures.

rows: Document Verification, Fee Payment and Admission

content.text: The allotted institution will verify the candidate's eligibility and original academic records. Candidates should follow the official admission instructions and confirm the applicable tuition fees with their allotted colleges.

sections.heading: Documents Required for MP NEET PG Counselling 2026 Round 1 Reporting

content.text: According to the admission instructions, allotted candidates must carry their original documents along with two sets of self-attested photocopies for verification.

items: MP NEET PG 2026 Provisional Allotment Letter
NEET PG 2026 Admit Card
NEET PG 2026 Scorecard or Rank Letter
MBBS Degree Certificate or Provisional Passing Certificate
MBBS Mark Sheets of All Professional Examinations
Compulsory Rotatory Internship Completion Certificate
Permanent or Provisional Medical Registration Certificate
Valid Government Photo Identity Proof
Madhya Pradesh Domicile Certificate, if applicable
SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD Certificate, if applicable
In-Service Experience or Sponsorship Certificate, if applicable

content.text: Candidates should verify the complete document requirements with their allotted college and the latest official counselling instructions before reporting.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 2 Upgradation 2026

content.text: DME Madhya Pradesh has provided an option for eligible Round 1 allotted candidates to express willingness for upgradation in Round 2.
The upgradation willingness window is scheduled from 30 October to 10 November 2026, closing at 11:59 PM.

Candidates considering upgradation should review the official counselling rules before submitting their willingness. The implications for retaining or changing the Round 1 allotted seat are governed by the applicable counselling instructions.
The detailed Round 2 choice filling and seat allotment dates were not provided in the supplied Round 1 result announcement.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 1 Resignation and Admission Cancellation 2026

content.text: Candidates who wish to resign from or cancel a Round 1 admission can use the prescribed online resignation or admission cancellation process.

Candidates should carefully review the official admission and resignation rules before taking any action. The consequences of cancellation and eligibility for later counselling rounds depend on the applicable DME regulations.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG 2026 Round 1 Opening and Closing Rank

content.text: In addition to the provisional allotment list, an opening and closing rank document for the first round has been publicly linked on the DME MPOnline domain.
The document is intended to provide course-wise and college-wise allotment rank information. Candidates may use it to understand the ranks at which seats were allotted in the first round.
These opening and closing ranks describe completed Round 1 allotments. They should not be treated as guaranteed admission thresholds for subsequent counselling rounds.

items: The Round 1 provisional seat allotment result was released on 29 October 2026.
Allotted candidates must download their individual provisional allotment letters.
Physical reporting begins on 30 October 2026.
The reporting and document verification deadline is 10 November 2026 at 6:00 PM.
Candidates must carry the required original documents and photocopies.
Applicable admission and tuition fees must be paid according to the allotted college's instructions.
Willingness for Round 2 upgradation can be submitted until 10 November 2026 at 11:59 PM.
The resignation and admission cancellation deadline is 10 November 2026 at 6:00 PM.

sections.heading: How to Correct Errors in MP Board Dummy Admit Card 2027?

items: Download or obtain the MPBSE Dummy Admit Card 2027.
Check the personal and examination details against school records.
Identify any incorrect or missing information.
Inform the school principal or authorised school staff.
Provide the relevant details or supporting documents requested by the school.
Ask the school to complete the correction through the prescribed MPBSE process.
Verify the corrected information once it is available.

sections.heading: MPBSE Class 10th and 12th Exam Dates 2027

content.text: The Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education has published the annual main examination timetable for 2027. Class 12 examinations will begin on 17 February 2027, followed by Class 10 examinations on 24 February 2027.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Check every detail on the dummy card. A dummy admit card is a draft for correcting errors before the final one is issued. Verify your name, parents’ names, date of birth, photo, signature, subjects and medium. Don’t treat it as the exam ticket.

Get corrections made through your school. In the 2025 case before the High Court, the board’s dummy admit card was issued and then the school’s documents were scrutinised. Errors are usually fixed by the school or principal, not by individual students. Tell your school quickly and keep proof of what you reported.
Mind the correction deadline. I don’t have the 2027 deadline yet. Last time the correction window was short, so don’t wait. Once the final admit card is issued, changes are much harder.

Don’t treat the dummy card as the final one. The admit card is released later at the board’s website. Check what the board says at release, since the portal name has varied (mpbse.nic.in and mpbse.mponline.gov.in).

Note the exam-day timings. Theory exams run from 9 am to noon. Students must reach their centres by 8 am and be seated by 8.30 am, with entry closing at 8.45 am. Question papers are given out at 8.45 am.

Pay the fee and report on time. Pay the acceptance fee online within the deadline, then report to the allotted institute with your original documents. Missing the deadline can cancel your seat.

Keep documents ready. Carry your MHT-CET/NEET scorecard, 10th and 12th marksheets, domicile, caste and validity certificates (if applicable), and ID proof. Follow the exact dates in the official schedule.

sections.heading: Courses Offered Under FYUGP 2026

content.text: Applicants often want to know exactly which subjects and programme formats are available before applying. Here is what Nagaland University is offering this year.

The admissions are conducted by the University's Multi-Disciplinary Research Centre (MDRC) in accordance with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 framework. sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria for Nagaland University UG Admission 2026

content.text: Before applying, candidates should understand how selection works, since Nagaland University does not rely on Class XII marks alone.

Admissions will be granted strictly on merit based on candidates' CUET-UG scores and Class XII examination performance, as per the eligibility criteria prescribed by the respective academic departments. This means:

content.text: Timing matters a great deal in this admission cycle, as the entire process from application to final seat allotment runs on a tight schedule. The section below lays out every key date candidates need to track.

Applications are open till 15th July 2026 for FYUGP B.Sc. Honours and Honours with Research programmes. The University will publish the list of shortlisted candidates on 16th July 2026, while admissions for selected candidates will be conducted from 17th July to 20th July 2026. Admissions from the waiting list are scheduled from 21st July to 23rd July 2026.
Candidates are advised to keep checking the official admission portal regularly, as revised or extended dates (if any) are typically notified there first.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026

content.text: Applicants naturally want a simple, step-by-step way to submit their application without missing any part of the process. Here's how it works.
Interested candidates can submit their applications through the University's admission portal at admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in. The general process is as follows:

items: Visit the official admission portal: admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in
Register with basic personal details to create a login.
Log in and select the FYUGP B.Sc. Honours/Honours with Research programme.
Choose your preferred discipline (Botany, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, or Zoology).
Fill in academic details, including Class X and Class XII information and CUET-UG scorecard details.
Upload the required documents (see checklist below).
Review the form carefully before final submission, as incomplete or incorrect forms may be rejected.
Submit the application within the deadline of 15th July 2026.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Application

content.text: Missing or incorrect documents are one of the most common reasons applications get delayed or rejected, so it's worth checking this list closely before starting the form.

Applicants are required to submit a recent passport-size photograph and signature, Class X admit card and marksheet, Class XII admit card and marksheet, CUET scorecard, transfer certificate, and other applicable documents such as caste, disability, backward tribe, or gap certificates, wherever relevant.

Seat allocation will be carried out in accordance with the norms and reservation guidelines of Nagaland University under categories including Scheduled Tribe (ST), Scheduled Caste (SC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), Persons with Disabilities (PwD), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Sports Quota, Employees' Quota, and Unreserved (UR).

content.text: Beyond academics, prospective students and parents often want to know what kind of campus life and support infrastructure to expect at Nagaland University.

Students admitted to the programme will have access to well-equipped laboratories, digital library resources, Wi-Fi-enabled campus facilities, e-learning support, sports infrastructure, career counselling and placement assistance, as well as on-campus cafeteria and health centre facilities.

content.text: University leadership statements often clarify the intent and vision behind a new admission cycle, which can help applicants understand what the programme is designed to deliver.

Welcoming applicants to the programme, Prof. Jagadish K Patnaik, Vice Chancellor of Nagaland University, invited students from across India to join the university, noting its status as the only Central University in the State of Nagaland and highlighting the implementation of FYUGP under NEP 2020 to provide a multidisciplinary, research-oriented, and student-centric learning environment. content.text: The IISER 2026 Round 2 seat allotment result was released on August 1, 2026, at the official counselling portal, iiseradmission.in. Candidates who registered for IISER Counselling 2026 through IAT 2026 can now log in to their dashboard to check their allotted institute and programme, choose between the "Freeze" or "Float" willingness options, and pay the Seat Acceptance Fee (SAF) within the stipulated deadline. This article explains everything about the IISER Round 2 result, including the direct check process, important dates, SAF structure by category, and what happens next in the counselling process.

sections.heading: IISER 2026 Round 2 Seat Allotment - Overview

rows: Joint Admissions Committee (JAC), organised by IISER Berhampur
IISER Counselling 2026 (based on IISER Aptitude Test / IAT 2026)

sections.heading: What Is IISER Counselling 2026?

content.text: IISER Counselling 2026 is the centralised online admission process conducted by the Joint Admissions Committee (JAC), with IISER Berhampur serving as the organising institute for this admission cycle. The process facilitates admission to BS-MS, BS, and B.Tech programmes offered by the seven participating IISER campuses, based on candidates' IAT 2026 ranks, categories, and the choices filled during registration. Depending on the availability of vacant seats, the admission process may continue through multiple rounds - up to 8 to 9 rounds - during August 2026.

rows: IISER Counselling 2026 registration and choice filling
Round 1 SAF payment and willingness submission deadline

items: Visit the official portal at iiseradmission.in.
Click on the IAT 2026 counselling login link.
Enter your application number and password.
Open the seat allotment or "Round 2 Result" tab on your dashboard.
View your allotted institute and programme, if allotted.
Download and save the allotment letter as a PDF for future reference.

sections.heading: Seat Acceptance Fee (SAF) - Category Wise

rows: General / EWS / OBC / OBC-NCL / PwD / Kashmiri Migrant / Kashmiri Pandit / Kashmiri Hindu Families (Non-Migrants)
₹25,000 (adjustable against first-semester fee) + ₹10,000 non-refundable administrative fee
₹12,500 (adjustable against first-semester fee) + ₹5,000 non-refundable administrative fee

sections.heading: Willingness Options: Freeze vs Float

content.text: Once a Round 2 offer appears, candidates must choose between two willingness options before paying the SAF.

rows: You accept the current seat as final and opt out of further allotment rounds.
Choose this if you are satisfied with the offer and do not want any further rank-based upgrade.
You keep the current seat safely while remaining eligible for a possible upgrade to a higher preference in later rounds. Float is generally activated by default once SAF is paid.
Choose this if you want a chance at a better-preference institute in Round 3 or later, while still holding your current seat.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Round 2 Candidates

items: Admission offers are provisional until candidates report in person at the allotted IISER and complete document verification.
Requests for extension of the seat acceptance deadline are not entertained under any circumstances; published deadlines are strictly enforced.
Candidates who fail to pay the SAF or submit willingness within the deadline lose the offer and are not considered in subsequent rounds.
Keep your login credentials (application number and password) secure and easily accessible during the entire counselling window.
Regularly check the official portal, as counselling schedules can shift slightly depending on how each round progresses.

sections.heading: What Happens After Round 2 Allotment

content.text: Candidates who float after Round 2 remain in contention for Round 3, expected around August 10, 2026, and any further rounds that follow depending on vacancies. Candidates who freeze proceed toward document verification and physical reporting at their allotted IISER. The counselling process may continue for up to 8-9 rounds in total, depending on how many seats remain vacant after each stage.

sections.heading: CENTAC UG NEET Admission Notification 2026-27

content.text: The admission notification for MBBS, BDS, BAMS, and BVSc & AH courses was issued on 30 July 2026 by the Directorate of Higher and Technical Education. Applications are accepted only through the CENTAC UG NEET dashboard at centacpuducherry.in/UgNeet_2026/, and the window closes on 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM. As of 4 August 2026, the portal showed more than 3,400 completed applications.

sections.heading: Puducherry UG Medical Counselling 2026: Application Fee

rows: NRI / NRI-Sponsored / OCI / OCI-Sponsored / Foreign National

content.text: Payment is accepted online only. A single candidate may submit only one application; submitting more than one leads to cancellation of both.

sections.heading: Documents and Certificate Dating Rules

content.text: Candidates claiming Puducherry residency must upload renewed certificates issued on or after 1 January 2026, including:

items: Residence certificate
Community certificate (Note: community certificates issued in the Central Educational Institutions format are not accepted)

content.text: For EWS and income certificates, the certificate must be issued on or after 1 April 2026.
Where applicable, candidates must also upload:

items: Regional reservation certificates (for Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam candidates)
Special reservation certificates: freedom fighter, PwBD, ex-servicemen, Meritorious Sports Person (MSP), and government school categories

sections.heading: Guidelines for MSP and PwBD Candidates

content.text: CENTAC published separate guidelines on 31 July 2026 for the Meritorious Sports Persons (MSP) quota and for assessment of Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) under the Government Quota.

items: MSP applicants from the Puducherry region must hand-deliver self-attested copies of sports certificates, along with a copy of the application, at the CENTAC office, Kamarajar Manimandapam, by 6 August 2026, 5:00 PM.
MSP candidates from Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam must upload a single self-attested PDF through their login dashboard by the same deadline.

sections.heading: Cross-State AYUSH Option for Puducherry Candidates

content.text: CENTAC has also invited applications from Puducherry candidates for BSMS, BUMS, and BHMS courses in government Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy colleges in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. The original notification was issued on 21 July 2026, and the last date was extended through a notice dated 31 July 2026. Candidates should check the revised deadline directly on the portal before applying, as the exact extended date was not specified in the source reviewed for this article (Not Available Officially).

sections.heading: Puducherry NEET UG 2026: Topper Details

content.text: Krishanth Abhinav M topped the Union Territory of Puducherry in the Re-NEET UG 2026 result, securing All India Rank (AIR) 553 with a percentile of 99.9721, as reported by exam-tracking sources including Aakash Institute and Daily Jagran.

Source conflict note: Moneycontrol has separately reported that the Puducherry topper scored 670 marks. This specific marks figure could not be independently cross-verified against a second source at the time of writing, so it is presented here as reported by Moneycontrol rather than as a confirmed official figure. Candidates should treat the AIR/percentile (cross-verified across two sources) as more reliable than the marks figure until the official NTA scorecard or CENTAC records are checked directly.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Applicants

items: Only one application per candidate is permitted; multiple applications result in cancellation.
Applications and objections must be submitted only through the official portals or email listed in this article.
Keep renewed residence, community, EWS/income, and category certificates ready with the correct issue dates before starting the application.
False nativity or residency claims across multiple states can lead to rejection and legal action.
Since the seat matrix and full counselling schedule are still awaited, candidates should check centacpuducherry.in regularly for updates rather than relying on unofficial estimates.

sections.heading: CENTAC Merit List 2026 - Draft UG Non-NEET Merit List Released

content.text: The Centralised Admission Committee (CENTAC), under the Directorate of Higher and Technical Education, Government of Puducherry, has released the draft merit list for UG Non-NEET admissions 2026-2027 on 17 June 2026. The list covers a wide range of undergraduate courses across colleges in the Union Territory of Puducherry, including Arts, Law, Agriculture & Horticulture, Biology-based courses, B.Tech, B.Pharm, Nursing, and Diploma programmes. Candidates can check their category-wise rank and submit objections, if any, through the official CENTAC dashboard before the deadline.
Click Here: CENTAC Merit List 2026

links.text: CENTAC Merit List 2026

sections.heading: What Is the CENTAC Draft Merit List 2026?

content.text: This section explains what the draft merit list is and why it matters to applicants.

The draft merit list is a preliminary ranking of candidates who applied for UG Non-NEET admission through CENTAC for the academic year 2026-2027. It is published before the final merit list so that candidates get an opportunity to verify their rank and details, and raise objections if there are discrepancies. The list has been published separately for each course and is further broken down by category: Overall, Puducherry (local), Other States, and NRI/NRI SP/OCI/FN (foreign nationals and related categories).

sections.heading: CENTAC Merit List 2026 - Key Dates

content.text: This section lists the important dates candidates need to know regarding the draft merit list and objection window.
Candidates who find any error in their rank, marks, or category in the draft list must raise an objection within this window, as no requests are typically considered after the deadline closes.

sections.heading: How to Submit Objections to the CENTAC Draft Merit List

content.text: This section explains the step-by-step process to raise an objection against the draft merit list.
If a candidate notices any discrepancy in the draft merit list, they can raise it directly through the CENTAC online portal. The process is as follows:

items: Visit the official CENTAC UG Degree admission portal.
Log in to your candidate dashboard using your registered credentials.
Locate the objection or grievance section on the dashboard.
Enter the details of the discrepancy you have identified.
Submit the objection before 20 June 2026, 11:00 AM.

content.text: Candidates should keep supporting documents ready in case they are asked to substantiate their objection.

sections.heading: Important Notes on Specific Courses

content.text: This section highlights special conditions that apply to certain courses in the merit list.
A few courses have additional conditions candidates should be aware of:

items: B.Sc. Nursing (Government Quota): The merit list will be published only after the Puducherry Nursing Entrance Test (PNET) 2026 result is declared.
B.Sc. Nursing (Self-Supporting Quota): This list depends on the UG-NEET 2026 result and will be released after that result is announced.
B.Tech. (Other State, based on H.Sc. Marks): This merit list will be operated only after the JEE-based merit list for the same category has been exhausted.
Ward of Farmer and Village Extension Worker categories: No candidates are listed (NIL) under these categories at present.
PWD and MSP categories: Lists for Persons with Disabilities and Meritorious Sports Persons are yet to be published.

sections.heading: How to Check Your CENTAC Merit List Rank

content.text: This section explains how candidates can view their rank in the draft merit list.
Candidates can check their rank in the draft merit list by following these steps:

items: Go to the official CENTAC website (centacpuducherry.in).
Open the UG Non-NEET 2026-2027 draft merit list page.
Select the relevant course and category (Overall, Puducherry, Other States, or NRI/OCI/FN).
Click on "View" against the corresponding course to open the list.
Use your application/roll number to locate your rank within the document.

sections.heading: Why the Draft Merit List Matters Before Final Counselling

content.text: This section explains the purpose of releasing a draft list before the final merit list and counselling process.

Publishing a draft list before finalising admissions ensures transparency and fairness in the selection process. It gives every applicant a chance to verify their marks, category, and rank, and to flag any clerical or technical errors before they affect final seat allotment. Once objections are reviewed, CENTAC will release the final merit list, which will then be used for the counselling and seat allotment process for UG Non-NEET admissions 2026-2027 in Puducherry colleges.

rows: Verifying that every answer has been evaluated, marks are correctly totalled and carried forward to the main sheet, and no question has been left unchecked. The actual answers are not re-assessed.
A detailed process in which the answer script is re-evaluated, typically by a different examiner, for accuracy of marking. Marks can increase, decrease, or remain unchanged as a result.

sections.heading: What Happens After You Apply

items: PSEB re-checks or re-evaluates the answer script as per the option chosen.

sections.heading: Punjab B.Ed Counselling Process 2026

content.text: The Punjab B.Ed 2026 counselling process is conducted entirely online and involves the following stages:

sections.heading: 1. Registration

items: Candidates who appeared for the Punjab B.Ed entrance exam must register for counselling on the official website.
After filling the counselling application form, candidates have to pay the applicable fee.
Details filled in the counselling form should be accurate, as admission will be considered only if the submitted details are correct.

sections.heading: 2. Choice Filling

items: Candidates must complete the choice-filling step by selecting their preferred programme/college options.
Candidates get multiple options and must arrange them in the order of their preference.
Preferences must be locked within the given time window.

sections.heading: 3. Seat Allotment

items: Seat allotment is released based on Punjab B.Ed CET entrance test results.
The Phase 2 seat allotment is scheduled for September 22, 2026.

sections.heading: 4. Reporting and Verification

items: Candidates allotted a seat must report to the allocated college within the dates specified in the schedule and complete document verification.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Keep track of all dates in the counselling schedule, as missing the upgrade or choice-locking window can affect seat allotment.
Ensure that qualifying degree marks are updated on the portal where applicable, especially for Phase 2 candidates who had not submitted them earlier.
Report to the allotted college within the specified reporting window with all required documents.
Cross-check personal and academic details submitted during registration, as incorrect details may affect admission.

sections.heading: How to Check PPMET 2026 Round 2 Seat Allotment Result

detail.title: RBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus 2026-27 - Overview
detail.short_info: The Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan (RBSE) has published the RBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus 2026-27 for students preparing for the 2027 board examination. The syllabus covers 15 chapters divided into two parts: Contemporary World Politics and Politics in India Since Independence.

content.text: Political Science (Subject Code 11) carries a total of 100 marks, including 80 marks for the written examination and 20 marks for sessional assessment. The theory examination lasts 3 hours and 15 minutes. Students can check the chapter-wise syllabus, marks distribution and PDF download details below.
Direct Link to RBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus 2026-27 PDF

sections.heading: RBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus 2026-27 - Overview
RBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus 2026-27 PDF Download

content.text: The Rajasthan Board provides the Class 12 syllabus for the 2026-27 academic session through its official website. The Political Science syllabus contains the prescribed chapters, topics and marks distribution for the 2027 board examination.
Official Syllabus PDF: Direct Link to RBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus 2026-27 PDF
The official Class 12 syllabus PDF contains multiple subjects. Students should locate Political Science (Subject Code 11) in the document.

sections.heading: RBSE Class 12 Political Science Exam Pattern 2026-27

content.text: The RBSE Class 12 Political Science examination carries 100 marks. The written examination accounts for 80 marks, while the remaining 20 marks are allotted to sessional assessment. The theory syllabus is divided equally between two parts.

rows: Part B: Politics in India Since Independence

content.text: Both parts carry equal weightage in the theory examination. However, individual chapters are assigned different marks, so students should prepare according to the prescribed chapter-wise distribution.

sections.heading: RBSE Class 12 Political Science Chapter-Wise Marks Distribution 2026-27

content.text: The syllabus includes seven chapters in Contemporary World Politics and eight chapters in Politics in India Since Independence.

sections.heading: Part A: Contemporary World Politics - 40 Marks
Part B: Politics in India Since Independence - 40 Marks

rows: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System
The Crisis of the Democratic Order

sections.heading: Part A: Contemporary World Politics Syllabus

content.text: Part A covers important political developments across the world, including the end of the Cold War, the emergence of new centres of power, international organisations, security challenges and globalisation.

sections.heading: Chapter 1: The End of Bipolarity (6 Marks)

content.text: This chapter explains the Soviet political system, the dissolution of the Soviet Union and its effects on international relations.

items: The Soviet System
Mikhail Gorbachev and the disintegration of the Soviet Union
Causes and consequences of the Soviet Union's disintegration
Shock Therapy in post-communist countries and its consequences
Tensions and conflicts following the Cold War
India's relations with post-communist countries and the USSR

sections.heading: Chapter 2: Contemporary Centres of Power (6 Marks)

content.text: This chapter discusses the emergence of major economic and political powers after the Cold War and their influence on international relations.

items: European Union
Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)
Rise of the Chinese economy
India-China relations
Japan and South Korea as centres of power

sections.heading: Chapter 3: Contemporary South Asia (6 Marks)

content.text: Students study the political developments of South Asian countries and the challenges involved in maintaining peace and cooperation within the region.

items: Political developments in South Asia
Military rule and democracy in Pakistan
Democracy in Bangladesh
Monarchy and democracy in Nepal
Ethnic conflict and democracy in Sri Lanka
India-Pakistan conflicts
India's relations with neighbouring countries
Regional peace and cooperation

sections.heading: Chapter 4: International Organisations (6 Marks)

content.text: This chapter explains why international organisations are necessary and examines their structure, functions and role in resolving global problems.

items: Importance of international organisations
Evolution of the United Nations
Reforms of the UN after the Cold War
Reforms in UN structures, processes and jurisdiction
India and UN reforms
United Nations in a unipolar world
International Monetary Fund, World Bank and WTO
International Atomic Energy Agency
Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch

sections.heading: Chapter 5: Security in the Contemporary World (6 Marks)

content.text: This chapter examines traditional and non-traditional security concerns and explains how nations respond to different threats.

items: Meaning and concept of security
Traditional notions of external and internal security
Traditional security and international cooperation
Non-traditional notions of security
Cooperative security
New sources of threats
Human rights
India's security strategy

sections.heading: Chapter 6: Environment and Natural Resources (6 Marks)

content.text: Students learn about global environmental challenges, resource management and the relationship between politics and environmental protection.

items: Environmental concerns in global politics
Protection of global commons
Common but Differentiated Responsibilities
Common property resources
India's position on environmental issues
Environmental movements
Resource geopolitics
Indigenous peoples and their rights
Sacred groves in India
Antarctica and global environmental governance

sections.heading: Chapter 7: Globalisation (4 Marks)

content.text: This chapter covers the meaning, causes and consequences of globalisation, particularly its impact on political, economic and cultural life.

items: Concept and causes of globalisation
Political consequences of globalisation
Economic consequences of globalisation
Cultural consequences of globalisation
India and globalisation
Resistance to globalisation
India and resistance to globalisation

sections.heading: Part B: Politics in India Since Independence Syllabus

content.text: Part B focuses on India's political development since Independence. It includes nation-building, electoral politics, economic planning, foreign policy, the Emergency, regional movements and recent political developments.

sections.heading: Chapter 1: Challenges of Nation Building (6 Marks)

content.text: This chapter examines the major challenges faced by India after Independence and the measures adopted to establish national unity and democratic governance.

items: Challenges facing the newly independent nation
Three major challenges of nation-building
Partition, displacement and rehabilitation
Process and consequences of Partition
Mahatma Gandhi's sacrifice
Integration of princely states
Hyderabad and Manipur
Government's approach to national integration
Reorganisation of states
Creation of new states

sections.heading: Chapter 2: Era of One-Party Dominance (4 Marks)

content.text: This chapter explains the dominance of the Indian National Congress in the early general elections and the development of opposition politics.

items: Challenge of building democracy
Congress dominance in the first three general elections
Nature of Congress dominance
Emergence of opposition parties
Socialist Party
Communist Party of India
Bharatiya Jana Sangh
Changing voting patterns

sections.heading: Chapter 3: Politics of Planned Development (2 Marks)

content.text: This chapter discusses India's approach to economic development after Independence and the political debates surrounding planning.

items: Political contestation and conflicts
Different ideas of development
Economic planning and early initiatives
First Five-Year Plan
Rapid industrialisation
Decentralised planning
Planning Commission
NITI Aayog

sections.heading: Chapter 4: India's External Relations (6 Marks)

content.text: This chapter examines the principles of Indian foreign policy and India's relations with major countries and neighbouring nations after Independence.

items: International context after Independence
Policy of Non-Alignment
Jawaharlal Nehru's role in foreign policy
Maintaining distance from rival power blocs
Afro-Asian unity
India-China relations and the 1962 conflict
Tibet issue
India-Pakistan wars and peace efforts
Bangladesh War of 1971
Kargil confrontation
India's nuclear policy and nuclear programme
Changing equations of world politics

sections.heading: Chapter 5: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System (4 Marks)

content.text: This chapter explains the political challenges faced by the Congress party during the late 1960s and early 1970s, including electoral changes and internal divisions.

items: Challenge of political succession
Fourth General Election of 1967
Electoral verdict and non-Congressism
Coalition governments
Defection in Indian politics
Split in the Congress party
Indira Gandhi and the Syndicate
Presidential Election of 1969
General Election of 1971 and restoration of Congress dominance
Abolition of Privy Purses

sections.heading: Chapter 6: The Crisis of the Democratic Order (4 Marks)

content.text: This chapter covers the circumstances leading to the Emergency in India, its consequences and the political developments that followed.

items: Background to the Emergency
Gujarat and Bihar movements
Conflict between the government and judiciary
Declaration of Emergency
Lessons of the Emergency
Politics after the Emergency
Lok Sabha Election of 1977
Janata Government

sections.heading: Chapter 7: Regional Aspirations (6 Marks)

content.text: Students examine the political aspirations of different regions and how India has addressed demands for autonomy, identity and national integration.

items: Relationship between region and nation
Indian approach to regional aspirations
Areas of regional tension
Jammu and Kashmir
External and internal disputes
Political developments in Punjab
Cycle of violence and efforts toward peace
Autonomy demands in Northeast India
Secessionist movements
Movements against outsiders
Accommodation and national integration
Sikkim's merger with India
Goa's liberation
Dravidian movement

sections.heading: Chapter 8: Recent Developments in Indian Politics (8 Marks)

content.text: This chapter carries the highest individual chapter weightage in the Political Science theory syllabus. It examines major political changes since the 1990s, including coalition governments, caste-based mobilisation and changing party politics.

items: Political developments of the 1990s
Era of coalition governments
Decline of Congress dominance
Alliance politics
Political rise of Other Backward Classes
Mandal Commission and its political consequences
Communalism and secularism
Democracy and changing political debates
Ayodhya dispute and subsequent developments
Emergence of a new political consensus

sections.heading: RBSE Class 12 Political Science Important Chapters 2026-27

content.text: The highest-weightage chapter is Recent Developments in Indian Politics, carrying 8 marks. Several other chapters carry 6 marks each. Students can use this distribution to allocate revision time without leaving out the lower-weightage chapters.

sections.heading: RBSE Class 12 Political Science Question Paper Pattern 2027

content.text: The theory examination is worth 80 marks and lasts 3 hours and 15 minutes. According to the supplied syllabus guide, students should prepare for different question formats, including objective and descriptive questions.

items: Multiple-choice questions
Very short-answer questions
Short-answer questions
Long-answer questions
Descriptive questions

content.text: The exact number of questions, section-wise marks and internal choices should be checked against the official model question paper issued for the 2027 examination.

sections.heading: How to Download RBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus 2026-27 PDF?

content.text: Students can download the Rajasthan Board Class 12 Political Science syllabus by following these steps:

items: Visit the official Rajasthan Board website at rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in.
Open the syllabus section.
Select the syllabus for examination year 2027.
Choose the Class 12 syllabus PDF.
Find Political Science (Subject Code 11) in the document.
Review the chapter-wise topics and marks distribution.
Download and save the PDF for reference.

sections.heading: How to Prepare for RBSE Class 12 Political Science Exam 2027?

content.text: Students should plan their preparation according to the prescribed chapters and chapter-wise weightage. Both parts of the syllabus carry 40 marks, making balanced preparation important.

items: Complete all 15 prescribed chapters.
Prepare separate notes for Contemporary World Politics and Politics in India Since Independence.
Allocate additional revision time to the 8-mark and 6-mark chapters.
Understand important political events, constitutional developments and international relations.
Prepare timelines for major historical and political events.
Practise short-answer and long-answer questions.
Solve available RBSE previous-year question papers.
Use the latest official model paper to practise examination-style questions.
Revise both parts regularly before the examination.

For example, a candidate may have a particular NEET All India Rank but a different position in the Rajasthan stray vacancy merit list because only the applicable counselling participants are included in that list.

sections.heading: Rajasthan NEET UG 2026 Stray Round Seat Allotment Date

content.text: The Rajasthan NEET UG stray vacancy provisional seat allotment is scheduled for 22 October 2026.
The counselling board will allot available MBBS and BDS seats according to applicable merit, eligibility, category, seat availability and the fresh choices submitted by candidates.
Candidates must use the official counselling portal to check whether a seat has been allotted.
The publication of the provisional merit list does not mean that the seat allotment result has also been released.

items: Download the provisional combined merit list PDF.

Confirm that mandatory verification and deposition formalities were completed.
Check that fresh college choices were submitted before the applicable deadline.
Monitor the official website for the provisional stray vacancy allotment result.
If allotted, download the allotment letter and follow the tuition fee payment instructions.
Complete the prescribed college reporting and admission formalities before the deadline.

sections.heading: Rajasthan NEET UG Stray Vacancy Round Eligibility 2026

content.text: The counselling board has listed several categories of candidates eligible for the stray vacancy round, subject to the official rules and mandatory verification.

items: Registered candidates who did not receive a seat in Rounds 1, 2 or 3.
Eligible candidates who exited or resigned from earlier allotments within the prescribed conditions and were not allotted a seat in Round 3.
Specified candidates allotted in Round 2 who did not join and were not allotted in Round 3 after completing the required re-registration.
Newly registered candidates meeting the stray round requirements.
Re-registered candidates satisfying the applicable rules.
Eligible candidates covered under the special non-domicile provision, subject to the priority rules stated by the counselling board.

content.text: Eligibility cannot be determined solely from previous counselling participation. Candidates must satisfy the precise clause applicable to their allotment and reporting history.

sections.heading: Rajasthan NEET UG 2026 Stray Vacancy Document Verification

content.text: The stray round required eligible participants to complete document verification and prescribed deposition formalities.
The official counselling portal states that candidates must report personally for verification and submission of the documents and bonds required for stray vacancy participation.
Choice filling is enabled only after the prescribed documents and bond have been deposited according to the applicable schedule.
Verification was scheduled from 18 to 20 October 2026 at the Academic Block, SMS Medical College, Jaipur.

The official counselling website explains that candidates participating in the round must submit fresh choices even if they filled choices in previous counselling rounds.

Candidates seeking admission to B.Tech programmes at the university can complete their application forms through the official website, aeee.amrita.edu. The registration process commenced on 7 November 2026 and is currently open.

content.text: According to the university's official admission schedule, AEEE 2027 will be conducted from 15 April to 7 May 2027 in computer-based test (CBT) mode at examination centres across India. Candidates who have passed Class 12 or are appearing for an equivalent examination in 2027 can apply, provided they meet the prescribed Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics eligibility criteria.

The university has provided an online registration facility through which applicants can enter their personal and academic details, upload required documents, select their preferred examination cities and pay the application fee. The official website lists an application fee of ₹1,300 for the AEEE route. Candidates can also seek B.Tech admission through their JEE Main 2027 percentile. detail.short_info: The Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) has opened the application correction facility for the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) 2027. Candidates who have already submitted their application forms can make permitted changes through the GATE Online Application Processing System (GOAPS). The correction window opened on 10 November 2026 and will close on 14 November 2026.

content.text: The GATE 2027 application data correction facility allows registered candidates to modify specified details, including their name, date of birth, gender, category, examination city choices and existing test paper, by paying the applicable fee. According to the official IIT Madras fee schedule, most permitted changes cost ₹500 per paper, while certain changes affecting fee-concession eligibility cost ₹1,500 per paper.

IIT Madras has also provided a separate free application defect rectification facility until 30 November 2026. This facility is intended for candidates whose applications have been flagged during official scrutiny. The two correction processes have different purposes and deadlines. Candidates should complete the process applicable to their application status through the official GOAPS portal.

The Selection Committee has published separate provisional MBBS/BDS allotment lists for Government Quota, Management Quota and the 7.5% reservation for government school students at tnmedicalselection.net.

content.text: Candidates who receive a stray vacancy seat must access the official UG counselling portal to download their individual provisional allotment order.

sections.heading: Tamil Nadu NEET UG 2026 Reporting Last Date

content.text: The last date to report to the allotted medical or dental institution is 26 October 2026 at 5 PM.
Candidates must appear in person with the required original certificates and scanned copies for verification at the selected institution.
The college will check academic eligibility, community and reservation documents, and other applicable admission details.
Allotted candidates should verify the reporting location, applicable fees and document requirements before travelling.

sections.heading: Important Rule: Downloading the Allotment Order Counts as Joining

content.text: The Tamil Nadu Selection Committee has issued a specific instruction for candidates allotted seats during the stray vacancy round.
Downloading the provisional allotment order is considered joining the allotted seat under the official stray-round counselling provisions.
However, candidates must still physically report to their allotted colleges within the prescribed deadline.
If a candidate downloads the allotment order but does not report, the Selection Committee may treat the case as discontinuation and apply the prescribed fee and counselling penalties.
Candidates should therefore read the complete admission conditions before downloading the order or deciding not to join the allotted institution.

sections.heading: Tamil Nadu NEET UG 2026 Stray Round Additional Security Deposit

content.text: The Selection Committee requires an additional security deposit for applicable candidates participating in the general stray vacancy counselling category.
The additional security deposit is liable to forfeiture if an allotted candidate fails to join the course, subject to the official counselling rules.

Eligible SC, SCA, ST and SCC candidates meeting the prescribed annual parental or guardian income limit of less than Rs. 2.5 lakh and the income-certificate submission requirements are exempt from the additional security deposit.
The 7.5% special reservation for Tamil Nadu government school students has separate fee exemptions.

sections.heading: Tamil Nadu NEET UG 2026 Stray Round Registration Fee

content.text: The Selection Committee's general stray vacancy notification specifies the following non-refundable registration fees for candidates who had not previously registered for online choice filling but had already applied and appeared in the published merit list.
These registration charges are different from the additional security deposit and applicable tuition fee.

sections.heading: Tamil Nadu NEET UG 2026 Government School Students 7.5% Quota

content.text: The Selection Committee has published a separate stray vacancy provisional allotment list for candidates under the 7.5% special reservation for eligible Tamil Nadu government school students.
The official allotment PDF dated 22 October 2026 contains seven candidate entries, all allotted to BDS institutions.

The separate counselling schedule for this special-reservation category specifies that no processing fee, security deposit or tuition fee is applicable to eligible candidates under the 7.5% reservation.
Students must still download their provisional allotment orders and physically report to their allotted colleges within the prescribed dates.

sections.heading: Tamil Nadu NEET UG 2026 Stray Round Eligibility

content.text: The Selection Committee's stray vacancy counselling schedule specifies that only eligible candidates who are not holding an MBBS or BDS seat under the All India Quota or State Quota can participate.
The following candidates are not eligible:

items: Candidates who have already joined MBBS or BDS seats through All India Quota or State Quota counselling.
Candidates holding seats under Government, Management or NRI quotas covered by the stated restrictions.
Candidates who received a seat in Tamil Nadu State Counselling Round 3 but failed to join it.

content.text: Eligibility also depends on the applicable merit list, candidate category, registration status and counselling instructions.

sections.heading: What Happens If a Candidate Does Not Join the Stray Round Seat?

content.text: The Selection Committee has notified penalties for candidates who receive stray vacancy allotments but fail to join or discontinue their allotted courses.
Under the applicable general counselling rules, candidates may lose their security deposit, additional security deposit and tuition fee, and may be required to pay the prescribed discontinuation fee.
The Selection Committee also specifies that affected candidates will not be allowed to participate in Tamil Nadu UG medical counselling for the subsequent one academic year.
Students should refer to the applicable Government Quota or Management Quota prospectus for the precise discontinuation conditions.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Tamil Nadu NEET UG Stray Round Reporting

content.text: The official counselling notice requires candidates to report in person with original certificates and scanned copies of the original records.
Candidates should arrange the following documents where applicable:

items: Provisional allotment order issued by the Selection Committee.
NEET UG 2026 scorecard and admit card.
Class 10 and Class 12 academic certificates.
Valid photo identity proof.
Community and reservation certificates where applicable.
Nativity or domicile-related certificates where required.
Documents supporting 7.5% government school reservation eligibility, where applicable.
Income certificate where required for fee exemption.
Fee payment acknowledgement, where applicable.
Other original certificates specified in the relevant prospectus and college instructions.

content.text: The list is a preparatory checklist. Candidates must follow the complete document requirements published by the Selection Committee and allotted institution.

items.name: VITEEE 2027 Revised Exam Pattern Overview

detail.title: VITEEE 2027 Revised Exam Pattern Overview
detail.short_info: Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) has revised the VITEEE 2027 examination pattern for B.Tech admissions. The computer-based entrance test will last 120 minutes instead of 150 minutes, with 100 multiple-choice questions carrying 400 marks. Fixed time limits have been introduced for Mathematics/Biology, Physics, Chemistry and the combined English–Aptitude section. Candidates receive four marks for a correct answer and lose one mark for an incorrect response. The examination is tentatively scheduled from 27 April to 2 May 2027.

content.text: VITEEE 2027 Exam Pattern Revised: Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) has reduced the B.Tech entrance examination duration from 2 hours 30 minutes to 2 hours (120 minutes). The revised examination will contain 100 multiple-choice questions carrying 400 marks. VIT has introduced fixed sectional timers, with 50 minutes for Mathematics/Biology, 30 minutes each for Physics and Chemistry, and 10 minutes for English and Aptitude combined.

Candidates will receive four marks for each correct answer, while one mark will be deducted for every incorrect response. The computer-based examination is tentatively scheduled from 27 April to 2 May 2027. Registration is open at viteee.vit.ac.in until 31 March 2027.

links.text: viteee.vit.ac.in

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Revised Exam Pattern Overview
VITEEE 2027 Exam Pattern Revised: What Has Changed?

content.text: VIT has introduced several changes to the examination structure for the 2027 admission cycle. The important revisions concern overall duration, total questions, marks and time management.

The comparison describes the previous examination format and the new 2027 structure. Candidates preparing for VITEEE 2027 should follow the latest official pattern instead of relying on older mock tests or preparation guides.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Subject-Wise Exam Pattern and Marks Distribution

content.text: The revised question paper has five subjects but four timed sections, because English and Aptitude share one ten-minute block.
Mathematics or Biology carries the highest weightage, contributing 160 of the total 400 marks. Physics and Chemistry carry 100 marks each, while English and Aptitude together carry 40 marks.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Sectional Timers Explained

content.text: One of the most important changes in VITEEE 2027 is the introduction of fixed sectional time limits.
Each subject block has a defined duration. Candidates must attempt the questions within the available time instead of freely distributing the full 120 minutes across the entire paper.
The published examination update states that responses are saved and locked when a sectional timer expires, preventing candidates from returning to earlier questions after the section closes.

The official VIT website independently confirms the fixed time allocation for each block. Candidates should follow the instructions displayed during the examination for the precise navigation and section-locking procedure.

sections.heading: Can Candidates Return to Previous Sections in VITEEE 2027?

content.text: According to the published revised-pattern explanation, candidates cannot revisit a completed section after its allotted time expires.
This means students should carefully review their attempted answers while the relevant section remains active.

VIT's official portal confirms the use of sectional timers. However, the full computer-based test navigation rules should be checked through the official examination instructions and mock test once available.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Mathematics and Biology Section

content.text: The Mathematics or Biology section contains 40 multiple-choice questions worth 160 marks.
Candidates receive 50 minutes to complete this section, making it the largest and longest timed block in the examination.
Candidates should select the correct MPCEA or BPCEA examination stream according to their Class 12 subjects and intended B.Tech programmes.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Physics and Chemistry Exam Pattern

content.text: Physics and Chemistry each contain 25 multiple-choice questions.
Each subject carries 100 marks and has a separate 30-minute sectional timer.
The average available time is approximately 72 seconds per question in each of these sections.
Students should practise calculations and concept-based questions under timed conditions to become familiar with the revised format.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 English and Aptitude Section

content.text: The combined English and Aptitude section carries ten questions and 40 marks.
Important: VIT provides only ten minutes for English and Aptitude together. The university does not list separate ten-minute timers for each subject.
Candidates should practise both sections together within a single ten-minute limit.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Negative Marking and Marking Scheme

content.text: VITEEE 2027 has negative marking for incorrect answers under its revised examination pattern.
For example, a candidate answering 60 questions correctly and 20 incorrectly, while leaving the remaining 20 unanswered, would receive 220 marks.
The score is calculated as 60 multiplied by four, minus 20 marks for incorrect responses.
Since wrong answers reduce the score, candidates should avoid unsupported guessing and manage their time carefully.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 MPCEA and BPCEA Exam Patterns

content.text: VITEEE 2027 has two examination streams based on the Mathematics or Biology subject selected by the candidate.

sections.heading: MPCEA Exam Pattern
BPCEA Exam Pattern

content.text: Candidates taking MPCEA and meeting the relevant academic eligibility requirements may apply for all B.Tech programmes.
BPCEA candidates are eligible only for specified B.Tech programmes, including applicable Biotechnology, Bioengineering, Bioinformatics and health-related programmes.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Exam Date and Registration Schedule

content.text: The official VITEEE 2027 website lists the following admission and examination schedule.
The exam dates are tentative. VIT states that the number of examination days may vary across test cities, and candidates will receive details of their allotted examination session.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Application Fee and Registration

content.text: VITEEE 2027 registration is open through the official university examination portal.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Eligibility Criteria

content.text: VIT's official admission guidelines specify the following Class 12 eligibility requirements.

rows: 60% Aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, with at Least 50% in Mathematics
60% Aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Biology, with at Least 50% in Biology
50% Aggregate in PCM/PCB, Subject to Official Conditions

content.text: Candidates who passed Class 12 in 2024 or earlier are not eligible for VITEEE 2027 under the currently published admission rules.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Preparation Strategy for Revised Pattern

content.text: Students should adjust their preparation to the shorter duration and fixed sectional limits.

items: Practise full-length mock tests containing 100 questions in 120 minutes.
Allocate 50 minutes to Mathematics or Biology during practice.
Attempt Physics and Chemistry using separate 30-minute timers.
Complete English and Aptitude together within ten minutes.
Practise accurate answering because wrong responses carry a one-mark penalty.
Review errors after each practice test and improve time management.
Use the official syllabus and VIT's mock test when available.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Important Instructions

items: The revised exam duration is two hours instead of two hours and 30 minutes.
The examination has 100 questions carrying 400 marks.
Fixed sectional timers apply to Mathematics/Biology, Physics, Chemistry and combined English–Aptitude.
Each correct answer earns four marks, while each incorrect answer carries a one-mark penalty.

How to Check NIT Trichy CSE Cutoff 2026 on JoSAA?

content.text: The Joint Seat Allocation Authority provides the official opening and closing ranks for engineering admissions. Candidates can check the NIT Trichy Computer Science and Engineering cutoff using the JoSAA 2026 rank portal.

items: Visit the official website at josaa.nic.in.
Open the Opening and Closing Ranks 2026 section.
Select the required counselling round.
Choose NIT as the institute type.
Select National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli.
Choose Computer Science and Engineering (4 Years, Bachelor of Technology).
Select the applicable quota, category and gender pool.
Check the opening and closing ranks displayed in the result.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Other State (OS) quota: For General-category OS, Round 1 of 2026 (13 June) closed at rank 1,317, and the final-round 2025 closing rank was 1,449. That makes it one of the toughest NIT CSE seats.

Home State (Tamil Nadu) quota: One report puts the Round 5 closing rank at 4,015 for home state and 1,373 for other state. Round 4 CSE is listed at 1034 to 3812. Home State ranks are much more relaxed than OS ranks.

Check the quota and category: The cutoff differs by quota (HS or OS), category (General, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, EWS) and gender seat type. JoSAA publishes separate opening and closing ranks for each category, so compare yourself against the right row.
Rank and percentile: CSE at OS generally needs a General rank under about 1,500. This is a rough guide, since the final cutoff is only set by the round-wise counselling outcome.

Verify on the official portal: Third-party reporting of final-round figures has been inconsistent, so verify them on the JoSAA OR-CR portal at josaa.nic.in. I couldn’t confirm an official 2026 final-round figure, and some sites mix 2025 and 2026 data.

sections.heading: IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Admission 2027 - Overview
IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Admission 2027 - Important Dates
How to Apply for IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Admission 2027?

items: Visit the official Ph.D. admission website at iith.ac.in/phdadmissions.
Read the general eligibility criteria for the January 2027 session.
Choose the department or interdisciplinary research programme relevant to your academic background.
Download and review its departmental brochure.
Click the Apply Here link to open the online admissions portal.
Register or sign in according to the portal instructions.
Select the appropriate Ph.D. admission category and department.
Fill in the required personal and academic information.
Provide the qualification, entrance-test and experience details applicable to your admission category.
Upload the required documents in the prescribed format.
Review the completed application and pay any fee displayed by the portal.
Submit the application before 10 November 2026 at 5 PM IST.
Save the submitted application and acknowledgement for reference.

sections.heading: IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Departments 2027
Important Instructions

items: Check the criteria for the cycle. The next cycle is for the semester beginning Jan 2027. The eligibility criteria and brochure from the July 2026 round are only a reference and might change.

Apply only through the right channel. IIT Hyderabad has a centralized online application portal for Ph.D admission, and candidates must apply through it. The exception is QIP: for QIP admissions you must apply through the AICTE website, not the IITH portal.

Meet the eligibility before applying. In the July 2026 round, Regular Ph.D needed an ME/M.Tech/MS or equivalent with First Class without GATE. An M.Sc. with First Class needed GATE/CSIR/UGC/DST-Inspire or equivalent. Direct Ph.D needed a BE/B.Tech or equivalent from CFIs with a minimum CGPA of 8.0 without GATE. First class means 60% or CGPA 6.0, with 10% relaxation for OBC and 15% for SC/ST. Requirements vary by department.

Expect shortlisting, then a test or interview. For the January round, shortlisted candidates may be invited directly to one or more rounds of online interviews. The written test is typically held in the July round. Departments can also set their own cut-offs.

Keep your funding and documents ready. Students are funded by IITH through Ministry of Education funding. Candidates with INSPIRE or CSIR-UGC NET JRF funding can also apply. Candidates must upload all necessary documents through the online portal at the time of admission. Admissions are provisional until all documents are provided
