content_sections.heading: About WCD Bidar
content_sections.text: The Office of the Deputy Director, Department of Women and Child Development, on Mailur Road, Bidar, runs the Anganwadi centres in the district through five Child Development Projects (Bidar, Bhalki, Basavakalyan, Humnabad and Santhpur (B)) that cover eight taluks. The recruitment follows Government Order No. ಮಮಇ 154 ಐಸಿಡಿ 2020 dated 03/12/2022 and the amendment order dated 18-11-2024 on the selection of Anganwadi Workers and Helpers. The Deputy Commissioner of Bidar approved it on 04-11-2026. The office can be reached at 08482-233146 and 08482-234237, or by email at [email protected] .

content_sections.heading: WCD Bidar Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: There is a single deadline for the online form and the documents. Every document has to be uploaded with the online application, and documents submitted afterwards will not be considered.

content_sections.heading: Vacancies by Project / Block
content_sections.text: The notice lists 441 vacant posts across eight taluks of Bidar district: 110 Anganwadi Workers and 331 Anganwadi Helpers. Bidar taluk has the most posts (27 Workers and 103 Helpers), followed by Aurad (27 Workers and 56 Helpers). The notice also gives a centre-wise list for each taluk. For every vacant post, the list shows the gram panchayat or urban ward, the name of the Anganwadi centre and the reservation fixed for that centre: SC, ST or Others.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Only women and transgender women can apply for the Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Girls and women, and transgender women, aged 19-35 years can apply for both posts. Persons with disabilities get an age relaxation of 10 years. The notice does not print a date as on which age is counted. Rural Anganwadi centre: the candidate must reside in the revenue village of that centre. A candidate from a local hamlet (majire), tanda or hadi must get a residence certificate from the competent authority and submit it with the application. Urban Anganwadi centre: the candidate must reside in the revenue ward of that centre and submit a residence certificate from the competent authority. To prove local residence, submit the residence verification for three years from the Tahsildar or Deputy Tahsildar. Submit Aadhaar card, ration card or voter ID card with it as supporting documents. Other qualification rules in the notice: Anganwadi Worker: certain courses from government-recognised institutions get first preference and +5 bonus marks. These are the ECCE diploma course from D.S.E.R.T, the JOC course, NTT courses, and, for Anganwadi activities, Diploma Nutrition, the Home Science certificate course, and one-year nursery or pre-primary training. Open school SSLC from the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board: the candidate must have compulsorily studied Kannada as first or second language, General Mathematics and Social Science/Social Studies. The certificate or marks card must show maximum 625 and minimum 219 marks. Only such candidates will be considered. Studies in another state: candidates who studied in another state with Kannada as first or second language are covered by a separate rule. If the maximum and minimum SSLC marks fixed in that state differ, only candidates who studied in Karnataka will be considered. Anganwadi Helper: candidates whose mother tongue is not Kannada may be interviewed by the selection committee at the time of selection. If needed, they will be asked to read and write so that their Kannada can be tested. The district-level selection committee will decide on their selection. Some Anganwadi centres are in areas where more than 25% of the population is from minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Jains, Buddhists, Parsis and Sikhs). In those centres, candidates who know that community's language along with Kannada will be selected. For each vacant centre, only applications from candidates of the category for which that post is reserved on a population basis will be considered. Persons with other physical disability not exceeding 40% may apply. They must attach a certificate from the authorised District Medical Board or a UDID card. Candidates should check the official notification for the centre-wise reservation of each vacant post.

Widows are selected directly on third preference, without considering the other accepted applications. Acid attack victims and residents of department institutions come before them. Women who became widows after submitting the application will not be considered under this rule. Among widows, the widow of a farmer who committed suicide gets first preference. The place where a widow currently lives, as shown in her residence verification, is taken as her residence. If more than one candidate has equal marks, the older candidate is considered. content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: The Anganwadi Worker and Helper posts are honorary service posts. Government reservation principles for government posts do not apply to them. A post is reserved for a scheduled category when more than 40% of the population covered by the centre belongs to scheduled categories. In that case, the post goes to the category with the highest population, and only members of that category will be selected. The posts are temporary and based on honorarium. Selected candidates must be ready to work on an honorarium basis. The selection process is subject to the advice, instructions, guidelines and orders issued by the Government or Directorate from time to time.

content_sections.heading: RRC NR Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: Eligible candidates can submit the RRC NR Apprentice online application form from 11 November to 11 December 2026. The merit list is expected to be displayed in February 2027.

content_sections.heading: RRC NR Apprentice Vacancy 2026 – Cluster-Wise Details
content_sections.text: Northern Railway has announced 4,651 Act Apprentice training slots across six clusters. Candidates can check the cluster-wise vacancy distribution below. Candidates must check the trade-wise and unit-wise training slots in Annexure-A of the official notification before selecting a cluster. Applications submitted for units where the candidate's ITI trade is not notified may be rejected.

content_sections.heading: RRC NR Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates applying for Northern Railway Apprentice Recruitment 2026 must meet the educational qualification and age requirements specified in the notification. Must have passed Class 10 (Matriculation) or equivalent under the 10+2 examination system from a recognised board. Must have secured at least 50% aggregate marks in Class 10. Must possess an ITI qualification in the relevant trade recognised by NCVT/SCVT. Both Class 10 and ITI qualifications must have been completed on or before 06 November 2026. Note: Candidates awaiting their Class 10 or ITI results as of the notification date are not eligible to apply.

content_sections.heading: RRC NR Apprentice Age Limit 2026
content_sections.text: The age limit for RRC NR Apprentice Recruitment 2026 is calculated as on 11 December 2026. SC/ST: 5 Years OBC: 3 Years PwBD: 10 Years Ex-Servicemen: As per the conditions mentioned in the official notification

content_sections.heading: RRC NR Apprentice Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The application fee must be paid online while submitting the RRC NR Apprentice application form. The application fee is non-refundable. Applicable online transaction charges, if any, must be paid by the candidate.

content_sections.heading: RRC NR Apprentice Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection for RRC NR Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026 will be based on merit calculated from Class 10 and ITI marks. There will be no written examination or interview. Screening and scrutiny of online applications. Preparation of merit lists based on the average percentage of Class 10 and ITI marks, with equal weightage. Document verification of shortlisted candidates. Fulfilment of prescribed medical fitness requirements. Merit Calculation: (Class 10 Percentage + ITI Percentage) / 2 If two candidates receive the same merit score, preference will be given to the older candidate. If their dates of birth are also the same, the candidate who passed Matriculation earlier will be preferred.

content_sections.heading: RRC NR Apprentice Stipend 2026
content_sections.text: Selected apprentices will receive a stipend during their training according to the applicable Apprenticeship Rules. The official RRC NR notification does not specify a fixed monthly stipend amount for each trade. Apprenticeship training does not guarantee permanent employment in Northern Railway after completion of the training period.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for RRC NR Apprentice Recruitment 2026?
content_sections.text: Eligible candidates can apply online for RRC NR Apprentice Recruitment 2026 through the official website before 11 December 2026. Visit the official Northern Railway RRC website at www.rrcnr.org . Find the Engagement of Act Apprentice 2026 online application link. Complete registration using your personal details, mobile number and email ID. Log in using the registration credentials. Enter the required personal, educational and ITI qualification details. Select the appropriate cluster and unit based on the available slots for your ITI trade. Upload the required photograph, signature, thumb impression and certificates. Pay the application fee online, if applicable. Review the details and submit the application form. Download and print the submitted application and fee receipt for future reference. Important: Only one application is permitted per candidate. Multiple applications may lead to rejection, and changes are not allowed after final submission.

Selection runs through scrutiny of applications
document verification
a written examination
a trade test where applicable
and a merit list.

All applications are scrutinised against the eligibility criteria and required documents. Admit cards or call letters are then issued to shortlisted candidates for document verification and the written examination. Shortlisted candidates bring their original documents
including the original admit card or call letter
and two sets of self-attested Xerox copies
as directed in the admit card.

Thumb impression and photograph are captured and verified at document verification or before entering the examination hall. Candidates whose biometric does not match at any stage are not allowed for the written examination
and refusal to take part may lead to cancellation of candidature. ICG reserves the right to capture or verify biometric data at other stages
and the Headquarters reserves the right to exempt biometric verification at any stage.
The written examination is pen-paper based and lasts one hour. The bilingual question paper has 80 objective type questions with one mark for each correct answer
and there is no negative marking. The syllabus follows the educational qualification and the relevant trade.
The qualifying mark in the written exam is 50%

and 45% for SC and ST candidates. No relaxation in qualifying marks is admissible to OBC and EWS candidates. Candidates who qualify the written test are shortlisted for the trade test (where applicable). SC/ST candidates are entitled to 2nd class rail / bus fare by shortest route as per Govt. rules, reimbursed at the written examination venue on submission of tickets. This is not admissible to SC/ST candidates already in Central/State Govt. service. Appearing or qualifying in the written examination does not give a right to claim appointment unless the candidate meets the eligibility criteria. Candidates selected for a Group 'C' post are liable for posting initially at any unit / establishment under Coast Guard Region (East), with All India transfer liability. Updates on this recruitment will appear on the ICG website, indiancoastguard.gov.in.

content_sections.heading: About Bokaro Home Guard Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: The notice states that the Home Guard is a voluntary organisation and Home Guards are its volunteer members. They are paid an allowance at the rate fixed by the government only for the working days on which they are deployed on duty as required. The notice clearly says that this is not a salaried government job or a means of livelihood, and applications are expected from candidates ready to serve the nation selflessly. The enrolment is conducted by the Home Guard New Enrolment Committee, Bokaro, chaired by the Deputy Commissioner, with the Superintendent of Police as senior member and the District Commandant as member. Under the Jharkhand Home Guard (Volunteer) Rules, 2014, Home Guards are enrolled for 4 years.

content_sections.heading: Bokaro Home Guard Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: The application fee must also be paid online within the application period, as the application is treated as accepted only after payment. All certificates uploaded must have been issued before the last date of application.

content_sections.heading: Vacancies by Project / Block
content_sections.text: The notice states that the vacancies may decrease or increase. Of the 199 posts, 111 are for Rural Home Guards and 88 for Urban Home Guards. Chas block has the most rural vacancies (40), followed by Chandankiyari (23). In both categories, 50 percent of the posts are earmarked for women, as shown in the tables above. Of the posts earmarked for women, 5 percent are reserved for qualified divorced, abandoned or widowed women. If such candidates are not available, these posts merge back into the women's share. 50 percent of the Urban Home Guard vacancies are for technically skilled candidates. If suitable candidates are not found, the non-technical and technically skilled vacancies will be filled from each other. Government servants can be enrolled as Urban Home Guards up to a limit of 10 percent of the total urban vacancies.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Rural Home Guard: the candidate must be a permanent resident of the block of Bokaro district from which the application for Rural Home Guard is made. Urban Home Guard: the candidate must be an ordinary resident of the urban area of Bokaro district. Both must attach a self-attested copy of the online residence certificate issued by the competent authority authorised by the State Government. Candidates may apply only from their own block or urban area. The age limit for both posts is 19 to 40 years as on 01-01-2026. A self-attested copy of the date of birth certificate issued by the competent authority is required. The notice does not mention any age relaxation. SC/ST candidates must attach a self-attested copy of the online caste certificate issued by the competent authority to get the relaxation in physical measurement. The candidate should be skilled in a technical field and working in a related office, self-employed or technically knowledgeable. The following are generally treated as technically qualified: doctor, engineer, advocate, lecturer (prādhyāpak), nurse, computer operator, typist, licensed driver (HMV/LMV), cook, carpenter, cobbler, washerman, barber, electrician, gardener, plumber, fireman and others. A self-attested copy of the certificate issued by the competent authority is required. Government servants may be enrolled as Urban Home Guards up to 10 percent of the total urban vacancies. They must attach a self-attested copy of a No Objection Certificate issued by their head of office. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of each post.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection follows the procedure fixed by the selection committee in light of the Home Department, Government of Jharkhand, Ranchi notification no. 5442 dated 20.10.2014. The stages are: physical test, Hindi writing ability test, technical proficiency test (technically skilled urban candidates only), merit list, medical examination and police character verification, and basic training. The physical test includes a 1 mile run, high jump, long jump and shot put. Candidates who pass the physical test take the Hindi writing ability test, set at the class 7 level for Rural Home Guards and the class 10 level for Urban Home Guards. It is qualifying, with full marks 100 and pass marks 30. Only technically skilled Urban Home Guard candidates who pass the physical test and the Hindi writing test take this test. It is qualifying, with full marks 100 and pass marks 30. Candidates awarded in national or state-level sports get these additional marks on attaching the award certificate. Government servants applying for Urban Home Guard get marks for education: Postgraduate 10, Graduate 8, Intermediate 6, Matric 4. After all tests, a merit list is prepared under the provisions of the above notification and selection is made against the vacancies. Selected candidates undergo a medical examination and police character verification. If found suitable, they receive basic Home Guard training on the order of the Headquarters, Jharkhand Home Guard, Ranchi. On completing the training, they are enrolled as Home Guards and given an enrolment certificate.

content_sections.heading: DSSSB Recruitment 2026 Age Limit
content_sections.text: The ordinary age limit is 18 to 27 years for most vacancies. The NDMC Junior Engineer (Electric) post has an age limit of 18 to 32 years . Age eligibility is determined as on 11 December 2026. Important: OBC reservation and age relaxation are available only to candidates meeting DSSSB's notified OBC (Delhi) requirements. OBC candidates from outside Delhi are generally considered under the unreserved category for these benefits. For specified NDMC, MCD, DUSIB and Directorate of Education positions, eligible contractual employees of the same department may receive one-time upper-age relaxation up to the actual period of contractual service, subject to a maximum of five years and the prescribed requirement of at least 180 working days in the relevant year. This concession does not automatically apply to every applicant or department.

content_sections.heading: DSSSB Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: DSSSB will conduct separate combined examinations for Junior Engineer and MTS under their respective post codes. The recruitment also involves online e-dossier submission, document verification and department/post allocation based on merit, eligibility, reservation and preferences. Skill, endurance, driving or trade tests may be conducted where required by the job.

content_sections.heading: DSSSB Junior Engineer Electrical Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: Junior Engineer candidates will appear in a Two-Tier Technical Examination . Tier-I is used for shortlisting, while Tier-II marks determine the final examination merit. Tier-I Qualification: Minimum qualifying marks apply separately to Section B (Domain Subject) and to the combined marks of Sections A and B. There is no separate minimum qualifying requirement for Section A alone. Tier-I marks are used only for shortlisting to Tier-II. Tier-II Merit: Candidates must meet the applicable minimum qualifying marks separately in Part-I and Part-II. The combined Tier-II score is used for preparing the final merit list.

content_sections.heading: DSSSB Recruitment 2026 Post Preference and Department Allocation
content_sections.text: The notification provides a combined examination framework for each post code. Candidates who are shortlisted must submit their eligible department/post preferences when DSSSB opens the online e-dossier process. At least one department/post preference must be submitted. Preference submission takes place at the online e-dossier stage. Only departments for which the candidate meets all essential conditions should be selected. Preferences become final after confirmation. Candidates who fail to submit preferences within the notified period will not be considered for nomination/selection. Department allocation is based on merit, available vacancies, reservation and submitted preferences. No waiting panel will be maintained under the combined examination scheme. Important: Candidates cannot claim another department after being allocated their first available preference according to merit. The department preferences should therefore be selected carefully.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection process includes physical fitness, academic and technical assessments, document verification and medical examination. Online Application Submission. RFID-Based Physical Standard Test (PST). Physical Efficiency Test (PET). Initial Document Verification. Computer Based Test (CBT). Trade Skill Test. Detailed Document Verification. Detailed Medical Examination (DME). Review Medical Examination (RME), Where Applicable. Final Merit List and Training Call. Important: Candidates must qualify at each applicable stage to remain eligible for further consideration. Merely passing the physical tests or CBT does not guarantee selection.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Physical Standard Test (PST) 2026
content_sections.text: The physical standards depend on the candidate's category and the applicable regional relaxation. Specified regional categories include candidates belonging to the communities and regions mentioned in the notification, such as Garhwalis, Kumaonis, Dogras, Marathas and eligible candidates from designated northeastern, Himalayan and other regions. Weight must be proportionate to height and age according to the applicable medical standards. Important: Candidates claiming relaxed physical measurements must produce the appropriate supporting certificates.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Physical Efficiency Test (PET) 2026
content_sections.text: Male candidates who qualify the initial physical and document checks must complete the prescribed running test. Candidates must complete the required run within the prescribed time to qualify for further recruitment stages. The RFID-based PST/PET will be conducted at Jorhat or Diphu in Assam . The exact reporting date and further instructions will be published through the official Assam Rifles website.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Computer Based Test (CBT) 2026
content_sections.text: The Computer Based Test carries 100 marks . Candidates who qualify the physical and applicable verification stages will be considered for the written examination. Meeting the minimum qualifying marks does not guarantee shortlisting for the Trade Skill Test. Candidates are shortlisted according to their merit in CBT and the number of vacancies in their respective trades and categories.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Trade Skill Test 2026

The notification specifies that the Trade Skill Test consists of a Computer-Based Practical Skill Test and a Trade-Specific Practical Skill Test , as applicable. The test is qualifying in nature, and no marks are awarded for the Trade Skill Test in the final merit calculation. Shortlisting is based on CBT merit in the relevant trade and category. Candidates who qualify the Trade Skill Test proceed to the applicable document verification and medical examination. The notification specifies shortlisting of approximately four candidates per vacancy for the subsequent document verification and medical assessment process, subject to the applicable trade and category provisions.

content_sections.heading: Assam Rifles Medical Examination 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates qualifying in the recruitment stages must undergo a Detailed Medical Examination (DME). Medical examinations will be conducted according to the Uniform Guidelines for Recruitment Medical Examination prescribed for Central Armed Police Forces and Assam Rifles. Where permitted, candidates declared unfit may undergo a Review Medical Examination (RME) under the relevant medical procedures. Important: Candidates must satisfy the prescribed medical requirements. Passing the written examination and Trade Skill Test does not remove the medical-fitness requirement.

faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for SAC Recruitment 2026?

faq.question: Q2. Which positions are covered by SAC Advertisement No. SAC: 03:2026?
faq.answer: The notice covers 26 position codes: 9 Graduate Apprentice (01 to 09), 5 Technician Apprentice (10 to 14) and 12 Trade Apprentice (15 to 26) positions.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for SAC Graduate Apprentice?
faq.answer: Posts 01 to 06 need B.E. / B.Tech. or equivalent in the respective field, and posts 07 to 09 need graduation in the respective field, both with minimum 60% aggregate marks from a Government recognized University/Board/Institute.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification for SAC Technician and Trade Apprentice?
faq.answer: Technician Apprentice needs a Diploma in Engineering / Technology in the respective field with first class from a recognized State Board of Technical Education. Trade Apprentice needs ITI (NTC/STC) from a recognized institute of Gujarat State; posts 15 to 18 also list SSC/Matriculation/10th.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for SAC apprentice positions?
faq.answer: Posts 01 to 09 have minimum 18 and maximum 28 years; posts 10 to 26 have minimum 18 and maximum 35 years, as on 02-12-2026. OBC (NCL) get 3 years and SC/ST 5 years relaxation in the upper limit.

faq.question: Q6. What is the stipend for SAC apprentices?
faq.answer: Graduate Apprentices get ₹12,300 and Technician Apprentices ₹10,900 per month. Trade Apprentices get ₹10,560 (posts 15 to 16) or ₹11,040 (posts 17 to 26) per month.

faq.question: Q7. How do I apply for SAC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Apply online only through https://www.sac.gov.in or https://careers.sac.gov.in. Register with a valid e-mail ID, upload the qualification certificates as .pdf files of maximum 1MB, and submit once.

faq.question: Q8. How are candidates selected for SAC apprenticeship?
faq.answer: Candidates are shortlisted or empaneled on the percentage of the qualifying exam entered in the online application, with due weightage to reservation categories. Shortlisted candidates are then called for document verification, subject to vacancies.

faq.question: Q9. Is the SAC apprenticeship a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. The training lasts one year under the Apprentices Act, 1961, and apprentices have no claim for employment in SAC or any other ISRO/Department of Space Centre or Unit after the training.

faq.question: Q10. Who is not eligible for SAC apprenticeship?
faq.answer: Those already undergoing or who have undergone apprenticeship training, those with one year or more of job experience, and those who completed three years after qualifying on the date of joining are not eligible.

content_sections.heading: JMI Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: All non-teaching positions will be filled as per the Recruitment Rules of Jamia Millia Islamia. Selection will be based on the candidates' performance in the written / skill / trade test / interview, etc. Screening and shortlisting: The University may constitute a Screening Committee to scrutinise applications and shortlist candidates. It reserves the right to limit the number of candidates called for interview, using qualifications and experience higher than the minimum or any other condition it deems fit. Assistant Registrar: Appointment under direct recruitment will be made through an All India open competition by conducting a Written Test and Interview. Call letters: Call letters for the written/skill/trade test/interview will be sent only to shortlisted candidates, at the e-mail address given in the application form. There will be no correspondence with applicants who are not shortlisted. Provisional acceptance: Eligibility may not be scrutinised at the time of the Recruitment Examination, so applications are accepted provisionally. A candidature will be cancelled at any stage if a claim is not substantiated, including during the University's scrutiny of documents. No TA/DA will be paid for appearing in any written/skill/trade test/interview for any post.

content_sections.heading: AIFF Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: The notice prints a role overview and key responsibilities for most posts. The Deputy Manager and Manager posts in Player's Status and Registration have key responsibilities only. The Manager will manage and oversee the day-to-day accounting, finance, taxation, banking, payroll and statutory compliance functions of the Federation. Supervise day-to-day accounting operations; review and verify payment vouchers, journal entries and supporting documents; monitor accounts payable and general ledger. Handle direct and indirect taxation, including GST and Income Tax; ensure timely preparation and filing of TDS returns and other statutory returns. Manage day-to-day banking operations; supervise bank reconciliations; handle foreign payments, international remittances and related documentation, ensuring compliance with FEMA, RBI and banking regulations. Supervise monthly payroll processing and salary disbursement, including salaries, deductions, TDS and statutory contributions. Ensure timely reconciliation of bank accounts, ledger accounts, vendor accounts and other balances. Coordinate and facilitate statutory audits and internal audits; liaise with statutory auditors, internal auditors and tax auditors; monitor closure of audit objections. The Deputy Manager will manage the organisation's accounting, taxation, payroll, financial reporting, audit and compliance functions. Oversee day-to-day accounting, general ledger and books of accounts; manage monthly, quarterly and annual books closure; prepare and review Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account and financial statements. Conduct budget versus actual analysis, variance analysis and financial MIS. Manage GST, TDS and Income Tax compliance; handle GST/TDS assessments, notices, appeals and departmental proceedings. Supervise monthly payroll, employee remuneration, incentives, reimbursements and deductions; coordinate with HR. Manage vendor payments, invoice verification, advances and expense settlements; monitor receivables, club billing and outstanding balances. Lead and coordinate Statutory Audit, Internal Audit, Event Audit, FIFA/AFC Audit and Forensic Audit. Oversee event-wise, tournament-wise and project-wise accounting, including utilisation reporting for FIFA Forward, AFC grants and other funded projects. The role overview in the notice describes the position as providing legal and regulatory support across relevant functions and helping maintain effective legal and regulatory frameworks. Administer, implement and periodically audit applicable regulations, operational policies, guidelines and statutory legal frameworks. Provide legal, regulatory and risk-management guidance to internal departments and external stakeholders; provide briefs and coordinate with external legal counsels. Draft, negotiate and review contracts, agreements, legal notices, official correspondence and binding instruments. Manage and resolve ongoing disputes, contractual claims, complaints and regulatory proceedings. Assist AIFF

Weightage of marks obtained in the minimum educational qualification 70

Permanent caste certificate issued by the competent authority (only permanent caste and residence certificates are accepted). Self-attested copies of all certificates and mark sheets. Experience certificate, if claiming experience: only experience in government rural development schemes on a post of at least equal pay is accepted. No Objection Certificate from the appointing officer and experience certificate, if currently working on such a post; without them, the experience benefit cannot be given.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is on merit out of 100 marks, worked out as follows: Among candidates with equal marks, the older candidate is selected first. Where no eligible application is received from a Gram Panchayat, a candidate of the same category from the same Janpad Panchayat is selected on merit. If PwD (Divyang) candidates are not available, candidates from other categories may be taken; if SC/ST women candidates are not available, men of the same category will be taken. After scrutiny as per the prescribed norms, the list of candidates will be pasted on the Janpad Panchayat notice board for claims and objections.

rows.basis: Weightage of marks obtained in the minimum educational qualification
Experience in government rural development schemes on at least equal honorarium: 05 marks for 06 months, then 01 mark for every further 06 months
One-year diploma/certificate (PGDCA/DCA/ITI) from a recognised institution, OR at least six months' experience as Panchayat-cum-Data Entry Operator

rows.event: Last Date to Apply (receipt at office)

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: The appointment is for one year, fully temporary, from 01 January to 31 December. After that, if needed, continuing for one more year may be considered with the consent of both sides, based on suitability, efficiency, annual work appraisal and conduct, as per government instructions. Either side may end the appointment during the contract by giving one month's notice or one month's pay in lieu of it. Contract appointees are governed by the Chhattisgarh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965. The posts are for field work, so 100 percent disabled candidates will not be accepted. Applications without self-attested copies will not be accepted; incomplete, unclear or faulty applications will not be considered and no information will be sent about them. Not eligible: those earlier removed from any post by Chhattisgarh Ajeevika Samvardhan Samiti or any government department for indiscipline, misconduct, arbitrariness or irregularity; giving false information cancels the candidature. Not eligible: an applicant who married before the minimum age prescribed for marriage; a candidate who married a person already having a living spouse (the Government may exempt if satisfied there is sufficient reason); a candidate with more than two living children, one of whom was born on or after 26 January 2001. Candidature may be cancelled if an applicant directly or indirectly disrupts or tries to influence the recruitment process. The District Collector has the right to take the final decision on any dispute or problem arising during the recruitment.

faq.answer: Fill the prescribed form (available on the Janpad Panchayat Bhairamgarh notice board or www.bijapur.gov.in), attach self-attested documents and submit it in person or by post at the Janpad Panchayat Bhairamgarh office during office hours.

faq.answer: Native residents of that Gram Panchayat; the selected candidate must be a resident of the same Gram Panchayat. If no eligible application comes from a Gram Panchayat, a same-category candidate from the same Janpad Panchayat may be selected on merit.

basic_details.job_title: DLSA Nuapada Para Legal Volunteers Recruitment 2026 – Apply Offline
basic_details.short_information: The District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), Nuapada is selecting Para-Legal Volunteers (PLVs) for DLSA Nuapada and the Taluk Legal Services Committees (TLSCs) of Khadial, Sinapali and Boden under Notification No. 01/2026, dated 03.11.2026. Only local residents of Nuapada District may apply. Applicants from Nuapada and Komna Blocks send the application to DLSA, ADR Building, District Court Complex, Nuapada, PIN-766 105. Applicants from Khadial, Sinapali and Boden blocks send it to their own TLSC. The application must reach the office on or before 15 December 2026 (05:00 pm). The notice states

qualification.details: Applications are invited only from individual local residents of Nuapada District. To apply for selection as a Para Legal Volunteer, an applicant should meet these conditions: | He/she must be a citizen of India. He/she shall be literate, preferably a Matriculate or its equivalent, with a capacity for overall comprehension. He/she should bear a good moral character. | The notice does not mention an age limit. Candidates should check the official notification for any further eligibility details of the scheme. | Teachers (including retired teachers) Ex-Servicemen Retired Government servants/Forest Officials and Senior Citizens M.S.W students and teachers Anganwadi Workers Transgenders Doctors/Physicians Students & Law Students (till they enroll as lawyers) Members of non-political, service-oriented NGOs and Clubs Members of Women Neighbourhood Groups, Maithri Sanghams and other Self-Help Groups, including those of marginalized/vulnerable groups Educated prisoners with good behaviour, serving long term sentences in prisons Any other person whom the District Legal Services Authority or Taluk Legal Services Committee deems fit to be identified as PLVs | The notice states: "The appointment of PLV is not a job and it does not carry any salary, remuneration or wages except honorarium fixed by OSLSA from time to time." The notice does not print the amount of the honorarium. In the application pledge, the applicant promises to work voluntarily as a Para Legal Volunteer.

selection_process: The PLVs will be selected by a Committee headed by the Chairman of the District Legal Services Authority
Nuapada. The selection works as follows:
The Selection Committee may use its discretion to shortlist candidates for interview

depending on the number of applications received. The Selection Committee will decide the basis of screening and elimination after receiving the applications. Women will be given preference while selecting PLVs. Representation from suitable applicants belonging to S.C/S.T./Minorities and Other Backward Classes must be ensured. Preferably
PLVs will be selected from persons who do not look up to the income from their services as PLVs. They should have the mindset to assist the needy in society
with compassion
empathy and concern for the upliftment of marginalized and weaker sections.
The interview date has not been announced in the notice.
important_instructions: Incomplete applications shall be rejected without assigning any reason. No application will be entertained after the last date fixed. No T.A/D.A will be provided to applicants for appearing in the interview. Under the declaration, an applicant's enrolment is liable to be cancelled or terminated instantly in any of these cases: false information is found at any stage; the applicant fails to show interest in the scheme; the applicant is adjudged insolvent or is accused of any offence; the applicant becomes physically or mentally incapable of acting as a PLV; the applicant abuses the position by misconduct; the applicant affiliates to any political party, partially or fully. The notice has also been sent for display to the Collector-cum-D.M, Nuapada, the Registrar, Civil Courts, Nuapada, the TLSCs, Bar Associations and colleges of Nuapada district.

content_sections.heading: About DLSA Nuapada
content_sections.text: The District Legal Services Authority, Nuapada works from the ADR Centre Building, District Court Complex, Nuapada- 766 105 (Tel. No. 06678-225336, e-mail: [email protected] ). The PLVs are selected under the Scheme for Para-Legal Volunteers (Revised), 2009, which was framed by the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The notice says a copy of the scheme is enclosed with it. The selected volunteers will serve under DLSA Nuapada and the TLSCs at Khadial, Sinapali and Boden.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: The office you send your application to depends on your block. The application must reach that office on or before 15 December 2026 (05:00 pm). The notice does not name a postal mode. It also does not say what to write on the envelope. The application form is printed with the notice. It is titled "Application for engagement of PLV at DLSA, Nuapada/TLSC, Khadial/Sinapali/Boden". The notice gives these steps: Fill up the form in capital letters, ticking the options that apply. Affix a self-attested recent colour passport size photograph in the box on the form. Give the details the form asks for: name and father's or husband's name; gender and marital status; permanent address and present address; date of birth; contact number and e-mail ID; category (General/SC/ST/OBC); educational qualifications, other skills and work experience; place of preference to work at (name of Block/Panchayat/NAC); computer knowledge (Typing (MS Word)/Excel/Video editing/Graphic Designing/other); achievements in the fields of law or social work. Complete the "Express Willingness to work as a PLV" pledge and sign the Declaration, with date and place. Attach the self-attested copies listed under Enclosures. Send the application to the office for your block so that it reaches by 15.12.2026 (05:00 pm).

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: Applications are invited only from individual local residents of Nuapada District. To apply for selection as a Para Legal Volunteer, an applicant should meet these conditions: He/she must be a citizen of India. He/she shall be literate, preferably a Matriculate or its equivalent, with a capacity for overall comprehension. He/she should bear a good moral character. The notice does not mention an age limit. Candidates should check the official notification for any further eligibility details of the scheme. Teachers (including retired teachers) Ex-Servicemen Retired Government servants/Forest Officials and Senior Citizens M.S.W students and teachers Anganwadi Workers Transgenders Doctors/Physicians Students & Law Students (till they enroll as lawyers) Members of non-political, service-oriented NGOs and Clubs Members of Women Neighbourhood Groups, Maithri Sanghams and other Self-Help Groups, including those of marginalized/vulnerable groups Educated prisoners with good behaviour, serving long term sentences in prisons Any other person whom the District Legal Services Authority or Taluk Legal Services Committee deems fit to be identified as PLVs The notice states: "The appointment of PLV is not a job and it does not carry any salary, remuneration or wages except honorarium fixed by OSLSA from time to time." The notice does not print the amount of the honorarium. In the application pledge, the applicant promises to work voluntarily as a Para Legal Volunteer.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Self-attested copy of the certificate of age (date of birth) Self-attested copy of the caste certificate (category) Self-attested copies of qualification certificates Self-attested proof of residence Self-attested work experience certificates, if any Supporting documents for other skills, computer knowledge and achievements in law or social work, if claimed in the form Self-attested recent colour passport size photograph affixed on the form

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The PLVs will be selected by a Committee headed by the Chairman of the District Legal Services Authority, Nuapada. The selection works as follows: The Selection Committee may use its discretion to shortlist candidates for interview, depending on the number of applications received. The Selection Committee will decide the basis of screening and elimination after receiving the applications. Women will be given preference while selecting PLVs. Representation from suitable applicants belonging to S.C/S.T./Minorities and Other Backward Classes must be ensured. Preferably, PLVs will be selected from persons who do not look up to the income from their services as PLVs. They should have the mindset to assist the needy in society, with compassion, empathy and concern for the upliftment of marginalized and weaker sections. The interview date has not been announced in the notice.

content_sections.heading: About Nuh District Court Stenographer Grade-III
content_sections.text: The notice is issued by the Office of District and Sessions Judge, Nuh, Haryana, which handles the courts of Nuh Sessions Division. The posts are filled for a period of six months or till regular appointments are made by the Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana, Chandigarh, whichever is earlier. Selection is made strictly under Rule 7 of the Haryana Subordinate Courts Establishment (Recruitment and General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1997.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Address the application to "The District and Sessions Judge, Nuh" and send it to the office of The District and Sessions Judge, Nuh, either by registered post or by hand. It must reach the office by 25 November 2026 up to 5:00 P.M. No advance copy will be entertained, and applications sent through e-mail will not be accepted in any case. The form's subject line reads: "Application for the post of Stenographer on adhoc basis."

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: All 08 posts are of Stenographer Grade-III on adhoc basis, at a consolidated pay of Rs. 25,500/-. The category-wise break-up is as printed in the notice: The number of vacancies may increase or decrease. If candidates of a reserved category are not available, the posts may be filled from candidates in the unreserved category, subject to their availability, in terms of the explanation to Rule 7 of the Haryana Subordinate Court Establishment (Recruitment and General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1997. A degree of Bachelor of Arts or Science or equivalent thereto from a recognized University. Passed matriculation examination with Hindi as one of the subjects. Proficiency in operation of Computers. The minimum age is 18 years. The upper age limit is in accordance with the latest instructions of the Haryana Government, calculated as on 01.01.2026. For candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste and Backward Class-A and B of Haryana State, and persons already in Government employment, the upper age limit is such as may be fixed by the Haryana Government from time to time. Applications of underage or overage candidates will be deemed to be rejected. The posts carry a consolidated pay of Rs. 25,500/-. The appointment is purely adhoc, initially for a period of six months or till regular appointments are made, whichever is earlier. For any other eligibility detail, candidates should check the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: One latest passport size photograph affixed on top of the application. Attested copies of relevant certificates/testimonials. Attested copy of the category certificate issued by the Competent Authority, if a category is claimed.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Candidates must qualify the English Shorthand Test and its Transcription, and a Computer Proficiency Test. The English Shorthand Test and its Transcription are at a speed of 80 w.p.m. and 20 w.p.m. respectively, on Computer. The stenography test will be held on 30 November 2026, and candidates must report sharp at 10:00 AM with their own shorthand note book and pencil. Candidates also have to qualify a Computer Proficiency Test. The notice also refers to a computer typing test. The place of examination will be informed on the website http://districts.ecourts.gov.in/mewat , and no separate letter or call letter will be issued. Candidates should watch the public notice on the notice board of the Court of the District and Sessions Judge, Nuh, and the same website. Original testimonials and identity proof must be brought at the time of the tests. No TA/DA will be given for appearing in the tests.

content_sections.heading: About the Recruiting Office
content_sections.text: The recruitment is conducted by the District Programme Officer, Hardoi, whose office (Child Development Department) is in Vikas Bhawan, Hardoi. The posts are in the Child Development Projects run in the urban and rural areas of Hardoi district. The direct recruitment follows the arrangement laid down in Government Order No. 1/1092245/2025/3313/58-1-2025 (1917687) dated 17 September 2025, and a copy of the notice has been sent to the Director, Child Development Services and Nutrition (Bal Vikas Seva Evam Pushtahar), Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow.

content_sections.heading: Hardoi Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: Applications are accepted only within this period; the notice gives no separate date for submitting documents.

content_sections.heading: Vacancies by Project / Block
content_sections.text: The 20 Child Development Projects of Hardoi district have 329 Anganwadi Worker and 333 Anganwadi Helper vacancies, a total of 662 posts. Kothawan has the most posts (29 Worker and 47 Helper), followed by Shahabad (21 Worker and 46 Helper); Hardoi City is the only urban project. The Gram Sabha/ward-wise details of these posts, with reservation and full eligibility details, will be pasted on the notice boards of the Collectorate, Vikas Bhawan, Tehsil and Development Block offices of the district and uploaded on http://upanganwadibharti.in . The number of vacant posts may decrease or increase in special circumstances.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The same eligibility rules apply to both Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Gender: Only women candidates are eligible for the posts in this notification. Residence: The applicant must be a permanent resident of the same Gram Sabha or ward (urban) as the vacant post. Applications from another Gram Sabha or ward will not be valid. Qualification: The minimum educational qualification is Intermediate. The online merit will be prepared on the basis of the maximum educational qualification of postgraduate. Age: Minimum 18 years and not more than 35 years on the cut-off date 01.07.2026. Proof of age: Only the date of birth recorded in the High School marksheet and certificate is accepted. Income limit: Rs. 46,080.00 annual in rural areas and Rs. 56,460.00 annual in urban areas, as per Government Order No. 22/2015/2123/26-2-2015 dated 14 September 2015 of Samaj Kalyan Anubhag-2, Uttar Pradesh Government. Income certificate: only a certificate issued online from the tehsil with a digital signature, issued at the competent level under Revenue Section-9 Government Order No. 3959/1-9-11-Raj-9 dated 30.09.2011 (as amended), that can be verified online. Caste and residence certificates: only certificates issued online from the tehsil with a digital signature that can be verified online. Widow: only a certificate issued by the Gram Panchayat Officer or the concerned urban local body, together with a certified copy of the family register (Parivar Register). Divorced or abandoned woman: only a legal or court order. The notice does not state the age relaxation or the honorarium; the full eligibility and application details are on http://upanganwadibharti.in . Candidates should check the official notification and the Gram Sabha/ward-wise list for the eligibility of each post.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: An online merit is prepared on the basis of educational qualification, from the minimum of Intermediate up to the maximum of postgraduate. Selection for the Anganwadi Helper and Worker posts then follows this order of preference, always within the same Gram Sabha or ward (urban area): Widow BPL candidate Divorced/abandoned BPL candidate BPL candidate Widow APL candidate Divorced/abandoned APL candidate APL candidate on the basis of merit The widow and divorced/abandoned status is accepted only on the certificates listed above.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for Hardoi Anganwadi Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Go to the departmental website http://upanganwadibharti.in , where the detailed form and information on the qualification and application process are available. Fill in the online application between 6 November 2026 and 26 November 2026, up to 12:00 midnight. Apply for a vacant post in your own Gram Sabha or ward only. Check every entry, especially the marks obtained and maximum marks; no offline request for correcting an error will be considered. Offline applications will not be accepted in any case. basic_details.short_information: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) has released the ONGC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 notification for 3,047 apprenticeship seats across various trades and disciplines. Eligible candidates with Class 10, Class 12, ITI, Diploma or Graduation qualifications, depending on the trade, can apply online through the NAPS or NATS apprenticeship portals.

application_fee.details: The official ONGC Apprentice notification does not specify an application fee. Candidates must apply through the respective government apprenticeship portal and follow the instructions displayed there.

age_limit.age_details: 18 to 24 Years
age_limit.details: The age limit for ONGC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 is 18 to 24 years as on 29 November 2026. Candidates' dates of birth should fall between 29 November 2002 and 29 November 2008, subject to applicable relaxation.

qualification.education_qualification: 10th, 12th, ITI, Diploma or Graduation, as applicable
qualification.details: Candidates are eligible for a particular ONGC work centre only if they are residents of an eligible district or have obtained their prescribed educational qualification from an eligible district. | For example, the Chennai work centre covers all districts of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, while the Hazira work centre specifies Surat, Navsari, Tapi, Dang and Valsad districts. Other locations have their own eligibility conditions. | Applicants should consult Annexure I of the official notification before choosing a work centre. A candidate should apply for one trade at one work centre, as directed in the application instructions.

salary_details.details: Selected apprentices will receive a monthly stipend ranging from Rs. 8,200 to Rs. 12,300, depending on their educational qualification and apprenticeship category. | The apprenticeship training period is 12 months for all trades. ONGC will not provide transportation, boarding or lodging expenses. Apprenticeship engagement does not guarantee regular employment with ONGC.

selection_process: Selection for ONGC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 will be based on the marks obtained in the prescribed qualifying examination. A provisional merit list will be prepared separately for the relevant trades
disciplines and work centres.
Application Scrutiny: Verification of eligibility
academic qualifications

age and other requirements. Provisional Merit List: Prepared based on marks in the qualifying examination. Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates and required supporting documents. Final Merit List: Prepared after eligibility and document verification
considering applicable reservation provisions. Engagement Formalities: Selected candidates must complete the required registration
document and medical fitness formalities.
If two candidates have equal merit marks
the older candidate will receive preference. The notification does not prescribe a separate written recruitment examination.
how_to_apply: Candidates can apply online through the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) or National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) portal, depending on their chosen trade. Offline applications are not accepted.
Read the official ONGC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 advertisement and verify your eligibility.
Check the required educational qualification and eligible districts for the chosen work centre.
For NAPS trades, visit apprenticeshipindia.gov.in.
For NATS trades, visit nats.education.gov.in.
Complete the required portal registration or sign in to your existing account.
Find the relevant ONGC apprenticeship opportunity for your eligible trade and work centre.
Fill in the required details and complete the application according to the portal instructions.
Submit the application before 20 November 2026 and retain your registration and application details for future reference.
Important: Applications submitted by post, by hand or through any other offline mode will not be accepted. Ensure that the correct apprenticeship scheme and eligible work centre are selected.

content_sections.heading: ONGC Apprentice Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The official ONGC Apprentice notification does not specify an application fee. Candidates must apply through the respective government apprenticeship portal and follow the instructions displayed there.

content_sections.heading: ONGC Apprentice Stipend 2026
content_sections.text: Selected apprentices will receive a monthly stipend ranging from Rs. 8,200 to Rs. 12,300 , depending on their educational qualification and apprenticeship category. The apprenticeship training period is 12 months for all trades. ONGC will not provide transportation, boarding or lodging expenses. Apprenticeship engagement does not guarantee regular employment with ONGC.

content_sections.heading: ONGC Apprentice Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection for ONGC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 will be based on the marks obtained in the prescribed qualifying examination. A provisional merit list will be prepared separately for the relevant trades, disciplines and work centres. Application Scrutiny: Verification of eligibility, academic qualifications, age and other requirements. Provisional Merit List: Prepared based on marks in the qualifying examination. Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates and required supporting documents. Final Merit List: Prepared after eligibility and document verification, considering applicable reservation provisions. Engagement Formalities: Selected candidates must complete the required registration, document and medical fitness formalities. If two candidates have equal merit marks, the older candidate will receive preference. The notification does not prescribe a separate written recruitment examination.

content_sections.heading: ONGC Apprentice Work Centre Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates are eligible for a particular ONGC work centre only if they are residents of an eligible district or have obtained their prescribed educational qualification from an eligible district. For example, the Chennai work centre covers all districts of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, while the Hazira work centre specifies Surat, Navsari, Tapi, Dang and Valsad districts. Other locations have their own eligibility conditions. Applicants should consult Annexure I of the official notification before choosing a work centre. A candidate should apply for one trade at one work centre, as directed in the application instructions.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for ONGC Apprentice Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates can apply online through the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) or National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) portal, depending on their chosen trade. Offline applications are not accepted. Important: Applications submitted by post, by hand or through any other offline mode will not be accepted. Ensure that the correct apprenticeship scheme and eligible work centre are selected.

content_sections.heading: ONGC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Apply Online
content_sections.text: The online application process is open from 29 October to 20 November 2026. Eligible candidates should apply through the appropriate portal: NAPS Apprentices: Apply through NAPS Portal NATS Apprentices: Apply through NATS Portal Candidates can check recruitment updates, selection lists and other notifications through the official ONGC apprenticeship website.

content_sections.heading: About RRC CR
content_sections.text: The Railway Recruitment Cell (RRC) of Central Railway works under the Ministry of Railways and has its office at CPM Conversion Office Building, P D Mello Road, Wadibunder, Mumbai – 400 010. This notice is its Cultural Quota recruitment for 2026-27. RRC only recommends the names of successful candidates; the appointment process is handled by the Principal Chief Personnel Officer of Central Railway.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice offers 2 posts at Level-2 in two cultural disciplines. The posts are open to all; there is no reservation for any caste. If no suitable candidate is available for one of the two disciplines, a suitable candidate of the other discipline will be selected instead, irrespective of gender. The number of vacancies is tentative and may be reduced or even become nil according to the actual needs of the railway administration.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: A candidate must be a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 to settle permanently, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, the East African countries of Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia or Vietnam to settle permanently in India. Candidates other than Indian citizens need a certificate of eligibility from the Government of India; they may be admitted to the exam provisionally but must produce it at document verification. 12th (+2 stage) or equivalent from a recognised board with at least 50% aggregate marks. The 50% condition does not apply to SC/ST/Ex-Servicemen/PwBD candidates or to candidates with a qualification higher than 12th; OR Matriculation from a recognised board and Course Completed Act Apprenticeship; OR Matriculation from a recognised board and ITI approved by NCVT/SCVT. Persons appointed as Clerk-cum-Typist must pass a typing test at 30 words per minute in English or 25 words per minute in Hindi within two years of appointment; their appointment stays temporary until then. Candidates must also upload a certificate from the institution confirming that it is recognised by the Central or State Government, or run by a Government body set up under an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature. A candidate who cannot upload it will be treated as provisionally eligible and allowed to sit the written exam, but must submit it on the day of document verification, failing which the candidature will be cancelled. Candidates without the professional qualification need not apply. Preference to candidates proficient in script writing and direction. Three years' experience in Acting/Script Writing/Direction; preference to experience with Doordarshan/All India Radio/a reputed or national television channel/a reputed theatre group (documentary proof required). Certificate of an individual award in Acting/Script Writing/Direction at state/national level competitions. Certificates of participation in state/national/international theatre festivals. Knowledge of light designing/light operating/set designing gives an additional advantage. Three years' experience of playing harmonium with Doordarshan/All India Radio/a reputed television musical group or channel (documentary proof required). An individual award or certificate for harmonium playing at state or national level competitions/programmes. Experience or mastery in playing 'Lehra' or accompanying classical/instrumental solo performances gives an additional advantage. Proficiency in playing Hindi songs (film/semi-classical) on keyboard, with a certificate from a reputed music group. A "reputed" theatre or musical group means one that has performed on various stages with national-level artists, or includes artists who have worked in All India Radio, television or the film industry. The railway reserves the right to reject any application. In the onli

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection consists of a Written Examination/CBT/Tab Mode, then Document Verification, then a Practical Demonstration. There will be no interview. RRC may, at its discretion, hold the written exam for all or a limited number of candidates. The date, time and venue of the written exam, practical demonstration and document verification will be fixed by RRC and told to eligible candidates in due course; requests for postponement will not be accepted. Eligibility status will be shown on the RRC website, and the e-call letter will be available there about seven days before the written exam; no admit card is sent by post.

content_sections.heading: About JIPMER
content_sections.text: The Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER) is a medical education and research institute with its letterhead address at Dhanwantri Nagar, Puducherry-6, and a campus at Karaikal. These posts are in an externally funded research project run by the Department of Community Medicine, JIPMER Karaikal. The Project Investigator is Dr L. Karthik Balajee, Additional Professor, and the PREVENT-D Study looks at drowning events and emergency response in Puducherry through multi-source surveillance.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: JIPMER has advertised 5 posts in total in the PREVENT-D Study.

rows.consolidated_pay: Rs 18,000 per person per month plus HRA

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Each post has its own essential qualification, desirable skills and maximum age. The age limit for every post is counted as on the last date of receipt of applications. Qualification and experience should be in a relevant discipline/field and from a reputed institution/organization, and the experience should have been gained after acquiring the essential qualification. Ability to communicate in Tamil and English is desirable for all three posts. Age relaxation: up to 5 years for candidates with experience in a government research organisation, as per ICMR norms (this applies to all three posts). Essential qualification (any one route): Three years' graduate degree in a relevant Subject/field in Public Health, Epidemiology, Social Work, Sociology, Anthropology, Psychology, Nursing, Allied Health Sciences, Life Sciences, Statistics/Biostatistics, Data Science + three years post-qualification experience; or PG in relevant subjects /field; or For engineering /IT/CS: four years' graduate degree. Desirable: Experience coordinating public-health or community research. Experience in supervising field staff and monitoring data quality. Familiarity with spreadsheets, digital data collection and preparation of research reports. Essential qualification (any one route): 12th in Science + Diploma (MLT/DMLT / Engineering or equivalent) + Five years' experience in relevant subject/field; or Three years' graduate degree in relevant subject/field + two years' experience in relevant subject; or PG in relevant subjects /field (work experience is not required under this route). Desirable: Experience entering, checking and managing health-research data. Ability to use spreadsheets and digital data-collection applications. Experience matching records, identifying duplicates and resolving data queries. Familiarity with statistical or GIS software. Essential qualification (any one route): 10th + Diploma (MLT/DMLT /ITI or equivalent) + two years' experience in relevant subject/field; or Three years' graduate degree in relevant subject/field + One year experience in relevant subject; or PG in relevant subjects /field (work experience is not required under this route). Desirable: Experience in community surveys, hospital record review or field data collection. Ability to use a tablet or smartphone for data collection. Familiarity with GPS/location recording. Experience arranging field visits and maintaining study records. The notice states that qualification, experience, other terms and conditions may be relaxed/altered at the discretion of the Principal Investigator. Candidates should check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of each post.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: All three posts carry a consolidated remuneration plus HRA as admissible at the approved posting location; the notice states that no other allowances are payable. It also says the consolidated salary of the post may vary from time to time, and no other allowance or facility other than the consolidated salary shall be extended.

content_sections.heading: JIPMER Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Staff will be assigned duties in Puducherry and/or Karaikal according to project requirements. The work includes hospital and administrative record review, community visits, interviews, verification of drowning events, environmental site assessments and digital data collection. Travel between study sites may be required. Coordinate surveillance activities across the study locations. Maintain the site calendar, permission tracker and progress records. Supervise field staff and monitor completion of assigned work. Liaise with authorised hospital, police, rescue service, and community nodal persons. Coordinate resolution of missing or inconsistent information. Assist the investigators with progress reports and stakeholder meetings. Any other project-related work assigned by the PI from time to time. Data entry, cleaning and management of the study database; maintain Case Record Forms and study records. Maintain the multi-source surveillance database. Link records from approved hospital, police, medico-legal and other sources. Identify possible duplicates and maintain linkage records. Conduct completeness and consistency checks. Maintain data-query, correction and backup records. Any other project-related work assigned by the PI from time to time. Identify and document eligible events through authorised study sources. Extract approved information from records using standard study forms. Conduct verification visits and interview eligible adult participants, including adult parents or guardians of child cases, after obtaining informed consent in accordance with the approved protocol. Record locations and complete environmental-assessment forms. Coordinate with approved community informants and institutional nodal persons. Enter data promptly and resolve queries under supervision. Assist with arrangements and documentation for expert-led first-response sessions. Any other project-related work assigned by the PI from time to time. For all three posts, the notice says the duties are indicative and not exhaustive: project staff shall carry out any work assigned by the PI in the interest of the project, including shift duty, field visits and administrative tasks. Refusal to carry out assigned work will be treated as unsatisfactory performance and may lead to termination of the engagement without notice.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Applicants will be shortlisted based on the details furnished in the application, CV and documentary proof, and the list of eligible candidates will also be displayed on the JIPMER website. Only shortlisted candidates will be called for a written test and/or interview. The final selection will be based on the CV, application, and written test/interview. If the number of applications is very large, more stringent criteria than those specified may be used to determine eligibility. The decision of the Project Investigator will be final. Written test: project-related topics including surveillance, accurate record extraction, consent and confidentiality, digital data collection, data quality, basic interpretation of health information, general aptitude, computer skills and duties relevant to the post. Skill test: record extraction, Tamil interview demonstration, data entry/checking and study documentation, data entry in MS Excel/database software. Interview: subject knowledge, communication skills in Tamil and English, and suitability for the project. The written test and interview will be conducted in person at the Department of Community Medicine, Academic Building, JIPMER Karaikal, FCI Road, Kovilpathu, Karaikal - 609602. The date and time of the interview will be notified one week in advance. No TA/DA will be paid for attending the interview.

faq.question: Q1. How many Gram Rozgar Sahayak vacancies are there in Janpad Panchayat Bijapur?
faq.answer: There are 23 posts, one in each of 23 gram panchayats: ST 16, UR 3, OBC 3 and SC 1, with 11 posts reserved for women.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the Bijapur Gram Rozgar Sahayak posts?
faq.answer: Applications are accepted from 5 November 2026 to 30 November 2026, between 10.30 AM and 05 PM; applications received after the fixed date will not be considered.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for Gram Rozgar Sahayak in Bijapur?
faq.answer: 12th pass is required (10th pass for SC and ST). For the Bastar and Surguja divisions, the priority order is 12th pass, then 10th pass, then 8th pass.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: The applicant must be not less than 18 years and not more than 40 years as on 01.01.2026, with age relaxation for reserved categories as per rules.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of a Gram Rozgar Sahayak?
faq.answer: The honorarium is a fixed monthly consolidated amount of Rs. 9960 per month, and no other allowance is payable.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply?
faq.answer: Fill the prescribed form addressed to the Chief Executive Officer, Janpad Panchayat Bijapur, attach the self-attested documents, and submit it in person or by post at the Office of Janpad Panchayat Bijapur.

faq.question: Q7. How will candidates be selected?
faq.answer: Through a gram panchayat-wise merit list of 100 marks: 70 percent weightage for marks in the minimum qualification, 15 marks for a computer diploma/certificate (PGDCA/DCA/ITI), and up to 15 marks for experience.

faq.question: Q8. Can I apply for a gram panchayat where I do not live?
faq.answer: No. The applicant must be a resident of the gram panchayat applied for; a same-category candidate from a nearby gram panchayat may be selected only where no eligible applications are received.

faq.answer: No. It is a completely temporary honorarium appointment for 01 year, sanctioned up to 28.02.2027, and may be extended at the appointing officer's discretion.

content_sections.heading: ISRO SDSC SHAR Apprentice Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: A total of 400 apprenticeship positions are distributed across six training categories. Trade Apprentices account for the largest number of positions, followed by Non-Engineering Graduates and DCCP apprentices.
