content_sections.text: The circular advertises 26 posts across five posts. The pay of each post is shown below.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: All the posts are open to officers of the Central Government, State Governments, Union Territory Administrations, recognized universities, recognized research institutions, public sector undertakings and statutory or autonomous bodies or organisations. Officers of Semi Government organisations may also apply, but only for Research Officer (Language)/Linguist. The application proforma states that only officers under the Central or State Government are eligible for deputation, and that candidates of non-Government organisations are eligible only for short-term contract. Each post needs two things: (a) the service condition for that post in the parent cadre or department, and (b) the essential educational qualification and experience. The essential educational qualification for each post is shown below. Service: (i) holding analogous posts on regular basis in the parent cadre or department; or (ii) five years' service in the grade, rendered after appointment to the post on a regular basis, in Level-11 of the pay matrix (Rs.67700-208700) or equivalent in the parent cadre or department. Experience (essential): ten years' experience in Geographic Information System or Remote Sensing or Research in the field of Geography or Cartography from the Central Government or State Governments or Union territory Administrations or autonomous body or statutory organisation or public sector undertakings or recognised University or recognised research institution. Desirable: Doctorate Degree in Geography from a recognised University or institution. Service: (i) holding analogous posts on regular basis in the parent cadre or department; or (ii) two years' service in the grade, rendered after appointment on a regular basis, in posts in Level-9 of the pay matrix (Rs.53100-167800); or (iii) four years' service in Level-8 (Rs.47600-151100); or (iv) five years' service in Level-7 (Rs.44900-142400), or equivalent in the parent cadre or department. Experience (essential): three years' work or research or teaching experience in Geographic Information System or Remote Sensing in the field of Geography or Cartography from Central Government or State Governments or Union territories or Universities or recognised research institutions or public sector undertakings or statutory bodies or autonomous organisations. content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The pay of the selected officer will be regulated under the Department of Personnel and Training's O.M.No.16/8/2009-Estt.(Pay-II) dated 17 June 2010, as amended from time to time. Posts are filled by deputation (including short term contract) initially for 3 (three) years or until further orders, whichever is earlier. The period of deputation (including short-term contract) also counts any deputation in another ex-cadre post held immediately before this appointment, in the same or another organisation or department of the Central Government. For Research Officer (Map), Research Officer (Drawing), Research Officer (Language)/Linguist and Map Analyst, this total shall ordinarily not exceed three years. For Assistant Registrar General (Map), Annexure-I says it shall ordinarily not exceed four years.

content_sections.heading: ORGI Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Assist the Deputy Registrar General (Map) in administration, planning, programme monitoring, and reforms. Prepare implementation plans, monitor execution, and ensure timely completion of mapping programmes, application of cartographic techniques. Supervise Senior Research Officer(s) (Map) and provide technical guidance for Policy and Standards implementation. Monitor development, maintenance, and quality assurance of geospatial databases and map products. Coordinate Web/mobile application deployments, manpower allocation, capacity building, technical reviews, and institutional strengthening. Recommend technical standards, SOPs, manuals, and quality assurance protocols for geospatial data related work. Coordinate with Central Ministries, Government bodies, ORGI Divisions and Directorates, on technical and administrative matters. Review proposals for procurement and modernization of GIS software, hardware, and map printing infrastructure. Supervise preparation of reports, guidelines, official communications, and responses to Rajbhasha, Parliament and RTI matters (if any). Support budget planning, programme monitoring, and policy implementation for the Map Division. Perform other duties as assigned by the Deputy Registrar General (Map) or Competent Authority. Overall In-charge of the Map Section in DCO and report to SRO (Map/DD), as the case may be. Supervise, monitor, ensure compliance and timely completion of mapping activities as per technical standards/SOPs. Allocate work, mentor staff, and review performance for effective manpower use. Ensure quality practices; identify improvements and innovations in mapping. Oversee creation, updating, and maintenance of geospatial databases and administrative boundary changes. Coordinate with District/Sub-district authorities for collection and verification of administrative boundary and field data. Review and validate geospatial datasets, maps, charts, and publications in DCO before submission to Map Division HQs. Guide the subordinates in use of GIS, remote sensing, digital cartography, and emerging technologies for quality outputs. Preparation of Monthly Progress Reports (MPRs), official communications. Responses to Rajbhasha, Parliament and RTI matters (when posted in HQrs). Responsible for the overall maintenance and upkeep of infrastructure (Hardware & Software) in Map Section(s) in DCOs. Supervise the preparation of analytical maps and outputs for Census publications, and archiving of cartographic products. Maintain documentation, metadata, quality records, and provide training to subordinates. Perform any other duties as assigned by Senior Officers. Assist the Research Officer (Map) in technical review and quality assurance of geospatial databases and map products. Validate spatial and attribute data for accuracy and compliance with standards. content_sections.heading: About NDMA Intern
content_sections.text: The National Disaster Management Authority, Government of India, has instituted this exclusive internship program as part of its organizational structure. The initiative aims to engage young talent with various divisions of NDMA and leading organizations of India, providing research support and experiential learning in the domain of disaster management.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: At least ten interns will be inducted during a year across various divisions of NDMA. The engagement is based on the skills and interest areas of the interns across broad thematic verticals, including Governance and Institutional Strengthening for DM, Risk Analysis and Mitigation (Includes loss and damage assessment in the context of disaster vulnerability and resilience), Disaster Management Plans, Community Based Disaster Management, Information Knowledge Management System/s (IKMS) for Disaster Management, School Safety, Urban Risk Management, Disaster Risk Reduction, Climate Change Adaptation, and Risk Insurance in Disaster Management.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Candidates must be Indian nationals enrolled as postgraduate/research students in reputed University/Institute within India or abroad, or have recently graduated with a university degree in concerned subject. Essential Qualification: Be enrolled in postgraduate degree programme in Disaster Management or in an equivalent post graduate degree program such as Development Studies, Economics, Humanities, Sciences, Management, Engineering, Health Studies etc. or have recently graduated with a university degree in concerned subject. If the student pursues a different academic discipline, there should be a clear linkage with disaster management. Desired Qualifications: Excellent computer knowledge (Microsoft Office applications), excellent written and spoken English, and excellent interactive and interpersonal skills, and flexibility to work in a multicultural environment.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The interns will be paid a remuneration of 12,000/- per month. The duration of the internship shall be at least six to eight weeks and not exceeding two months. NDMA will provide working space, internet facility and other necessities deemed fit by the divisional head. The interns will be required to have their own laptops. Internship based out of remote locations/work from home will be considered.

content_sections.heading: NDMA Intern Job Description
content_sections.text: The intern will assist/collate research/analysis in the following fields: SOP and Guidance Notes Project Assignments Research Assignments Training/Capacity Building and Documentation Process Documentation Day to day assignment- On the job training Any other tasks as assigned by the Supervisor

content_sections.heading: GeM Assistant Risk Officer Job Profile
content_sections.text: The job profile includes working in a dynamic, data-driven work environment involving collaboration with employees from the Government and Private Sector. The role of the Assistant Risk Officer involves identifying, analysing, assessing, and mitigating operational, financial, and strategic risks. The indicative list of responsibilities includes: Assist the Risk/Vigilance Officer in day-to-day preventive, punitive, and participative vigilance functions relating to transactions on the GeM portal. Carry out bid-cycle analysis, short-duration bid analysis, and bid decryption checks to detect cartelisation, price manipulation, bid-rotation, and other irregular bidding patterns. Monitor and analyse participation of suspended, blacklisted, or debarred sellers on the platform, and flag violations or attempts at circumvention for further examination. Undertake seller-profile analytics and buyer/seller behaviour analysis to identify anomalous transaction patterns, unusual pricing, or related-party arrangements warranting scrutiny. Assist in preliminary scrutiny and fact-finding on complaints received through CPGRAMS, CVC, whistle-blower mechanisms, and other channels, and prepare notes for the Risk/Vigilance Officer. Maintain vigilance case records, complaint registers, and trackers, and compile periodic statistical returns for submission to the Risk/Vigilance Officer/CVO. Build and maintain analytical queries, scripts, and dashboards (e.g. Python, SQL, Power BI/Tableau) for continuous, rule-based, and statistical transaction monitoring. Assist in compiling inputs for the Annual Vigilance Report, the Agreed List, the List of Officers of Doubtful Integrity, and other periodic returns required under CVC guidelines. Coordinate with the IT/Product teams for implementation of system-level red flags and preventive vigilance controls on the portal. Any other responsibility as assigned by the Vigilance Officer/Chief Vigilance Officer from time to time.

The rules and regulations of National Law University Delhi apply to the selected candidate.

Sign the form and attach the required documents: degree certificates, experience certificates, research papers DOI and so on. Number the supporting documents serially as Annexures and refer to them in the form.
Merge everything into a single PDF file named ABI<< Applicant First Name >>22112026.pdf.

Scanned copies of certificates for university awards, medals or conference best presentation awards.

Research publications, best professional outputs in the last 10 years, highlights of contributions, books authored/edited, patents/IPR, technologies developed, licensed or commercialised. Dissertations supervised (Ph.D. and post-graduation) and a 1–2 page summary of vision as Leader of CSIR-CGCRI. content_sections.text: Mess Kitchen Visits: visit the mess kitchens of IIT Jammu as and when required to assess food preparation practices, hygiene, sanitation, food handling and general kitchen conditions from a nutritional and food-service perspective. content_sections.heading: About the Project
content_sections.text: The post is for the ICMR-funded project "Survive to Thrive- Implementation Research to Improve Developmental Outcomes of disadvantaged children in urban, rural, tribal areas of Madhya Pradesh- A Mixed Methods Intervention Study". The Principal Investigator is Dr Deepti Dabar, Additional Professor, Department of Community & Family Medicine, AIIMS Bhopal. The notice is signed by the Principal Investigator from Room No. 246, 2nd Floor, Medical College Building, All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Saket Nagar, Bhopal-462020 (MP).

content_sections.text: One post of Project Research Scientist I (Non-Medical) is advertised. All educational qualifications and certificates must be from a recognised Board/University. Post Graduate Degree, including the integrated PG degrees. For Engineering / IT / CS: Four Years Graduate Degree. Master's degree in Psychology / Child Development / Human Development or a related field (meeting Qualification Level B Development Assessments); M.Phil. / PDCP / M.A. Clinical Psychology with RCI registration preferred. Training / experience in administering standardised child developmental assessment tools. Community/caste certificates must be issued by the authorised officers of the Government. A valid driving licence for a two-wheeler (with gear) and a car is required. The employee must own or arrange a two-wheeler/car for travel related to the project. A valid email ID and mobile number are mandatory for communication.

content_sections.heading: AIIMS Bhopal Project Research Scientist I (Non-Medical) Job Description
content_sections.text: Project Research Scientists are to provide assistance in conducting the project in the form of: child development assessments, literature review, microplanning and data collection; quality assurance and supervision, qualitative interviews, data analysis; report writing and dissemination, selection of other staff; meeting and liaising with government officials; procurement and maintenance of tools and equipment, financial record-keeping; other tasks assigned by the PI. The place of work is Bhopal and Chhindwara Districts of Madhya Pradesh. Travel to other districts and states may be required as part of the project. Candidates may be posted at rural or field sites as per project needs.

basic_details.short_information: All India Institute of Medical Sciences Bhopal has invited applications for one Health Economist post (1 UR) on contract for the DHR project in the Resource Centre for Health Technology Assessment, advertisement No. AIIMS/BPL/RRC-HTA/2026/02. Applications go by email to [email protected] and must be received by 3 December 2026, 5:00 PM.

important_dates.interview_date: Third week of December 2026; exact date, time and mode to be sent by email

post_wise_qualification.essential_qualification: 1 (UR)

qualification.details: Qualification: Masters in Health Economics/ Economics/ Public Health/ Community Medicine with specialization in Healthcare Costing, Economic Evaluation. Experience: 2 years of experience in the field of health economics. Age limit: 40 years. Age relaxation: admissible for SC/ST/OBC candidates, retrenched government employees, departmental candidates (including project employees) and ex-servicemen, in accordance with Central Government instructions issued from time to time. Age concession to the extent of services rendered in research projects is also admissible for experienced and skilled persons. Cut-off date: the date of submission of the application form is the cut-off date for determining eligibility and experience. Educational qualifications and certificates must be from a recognized Board/University. Experience shall be preferably from Govt. Organisations and is counted after the date of completion of the Minimum Essential Qualification. Experience from reputed National / International Organisations is also considered. Experience must be from the relevant field/area, as required for the study of the Project concerned. | Remuneration is Rs 67,000 + 20% HRA; no other allowances are admissible. Leave is governed by the institutional policy for extramural research projects. Candidates should check the official notification for any further eligibility detail.

selection_process: Applications are scrutinized for eligibility on age
educational qualification and experience. Selection is through a written test and/or interview
and eligible candidates are told the date
time and mode by email.

A written test is held only if eligible candidates for the post exceed 30. Minimum qualifying score is 40% for UR/OBC/EWS and 35% for SC/ST. At most five candidates are shortlisted for the interview in descending order of written test scores. If fewer than five qualify
all qualifying candidates are shortlisted. A tie is broken in favour of the candidate with the earlier date of birth.
If eligible candidates number 30 or fewer
they may attend the interview online or offline
as communicated by email. If a written test is held
final selection is on the combined written test and interview scores. If no written test is held
selection is exclusively on interview scores.
The venue for the written test and/or interview is the CFM Board Room
Second Floor
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Bhavan (Medical College Building)
AIIMS Bhopal. The interview may be conducted online or offline
as applicable
according to the number of eligible candidates.
important_instructions: The post is on contract for an externally funded project, with no claim to a regular post at AIIMS Bhopal or the funding agency. Tenure is up to 31 March 2027. It may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and further approval of the project duration by the funding agency. The contract expires automatically at the end of the specified period unless mutually renewed. Either party can terminate it with 30 days' notice or salary in lieu. Incomplete or incorrect applications will be rejected. A valid email ID and mobile number are mandatory. Candidates employed in government or other funded research projects must provide a "No Objection Certificate" from their employer. Private practice is prohibited. Candidates may be posted at rural or field sites as per project needs. No TA/DA is provided for the test or interview, and the Institute will not provide accommodation. Candidates appearing in person must bring coloured passport photos, original documents and self-attested copies. For online interviews, original documents are verified at joining and selection stays provisional until then. Meeting the minimum qualifications does not guarantee selection, and stricter criteria may be applied if there are many applicants. Misinformation or canvassing leads to disqualification, and all disputes are subject to the courts in Bhopal.

content_sections.text: Applications are scrutinized for eligibility on age, educational qualification and experience. Selection is through a written test and/or interview, and eligible candidates are told the date, time and mode by email. A written test is held only if eligible candidates for the post exceed 30. Minimum qualifying score is 40% for UR/OBC/EWS and 35% for SC/ST. At most five candidates are shortlisted for the interview in descending order of written test scores. If fewer than five qualify, all qualifying candidates are shortlisted. A tie is broken in favour of the candidate with the earlier date of birth. If eligible candidates number 30 or fewer, they may attend the interview online or offline, as communicated by email. If a written test is held, final selection is on the combined written test and interview scores. If no written test is held, selection is exclusively on interview scores. The venue for the written test and/or interview is the CFM Board Room, Second Floor, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Bhavan (Medical College Building), AIIMS Bhopal. The interview may be conducted online or offline, as applicable, according to the number of eligible candidates.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: The post is on contract for an externally funded project, with no claim to a regular post at AIIMS Bhopal or the funding agency. Tenure is up to 31 March 2027. It may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and further approval of the project duration by the funding agency. The contract expires automatically at the end of the specified period unless mutually renewed. Either party can terminate it with 30 days' notice or salary in lieu. Incomplete or incorrect applications will be rejected. A valid email ID and mobile number are mandatory. Candidates employed in government or other funded research projects must provide a "No Objection Certificate" from their employer. Private practice is prohibited. Candidates may be posted at rural or field sites as per project needs. No TA/DA is provided for the test or interview, and the Institute will not provide accommodation. Candidates appearing in person must bring coloured passport photos, original documents and self-attested copies. For online interviews, original documents are verified at joining and selection stays provisional until then. Meeting the minimum qualifications does not guarantee selection, and stricter criteria may be applied if there are many applicants. Misinformation or canvassing leads to disqualification, and all disputes are subject to the courts in Bhopal.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for NCST Recruitment 2027 by Email
content_sections.text: Fill the application in the format given at the Annexure (Performa for Application for the Post of Deputy Director). Enclose attested photocopies of complete ACRs/APARs for the last five years, vigilance clearance, integrity certificate and statement of penalties of the last 10 years. Send the hard copy with all signed documents by post to Sh. Tajinder Singh Bal, Under Secretary, NCST Division, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, New Delhi-110001, to reach before the last date. Email it on or before 11 January 2027.

content_sections.text: Officers, once selected, will not be allowed to withdraw their candidature. Applications received after the last date or found incomplete will not be considered. content_sections.heading: Anna University CARCA Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: The notice lists these duties for the Manager – Relations & Fundraising: Develop, maintain and continuously enhance a comprehensive and dynamic alumni database. Maintain an updated database of corporate contacts, alumni contributors, CSR opportunities, sponsorship records and donor information. Establish and maintain strong relationships with corporate partners, industry representatives and alumni to promote long-term collaboration with the University. Identify and approach corporate organizations and alumni for CSR funds, sponsorships, and donations to support university initiatives, research projects, conferences and student activities. Coordinate with various departments, centres, and faculty members to identify funding opportunities and support projects eligible for CSR or sponsorship funding. Collaborate with various departments in the preparation of CSR proposals, sponsorship proposals, presentations and fundraising documents for effective submission to corporate organizations and prospective donors. Follow up with corporate organizations and alumni regarding funding proposals, sponsorship commitments, and partnership opportunities. Assist in preparing acknowledgement letters, utilization reports, progress reports, and documentation related to CSR funds and sponsorships. Organize and support corporate outreach programs, alumni meets, networking events and fundraising campaigns conducted by CARCA and the University. Support the promotion of University activities, achievements, and initiatives through corporate engagement and alumni networking.

Excellent oral and written communication in English. Proficiency in man-management with excellent interpersonal skills. At least 15 years of post-qualification experience in heading administration of a government department or reputed Management Education Institute/University/College/Commercial organization of national/international repute, out of which at least 10 years in the level of Senior Administrative Officer. Experience in institutes of repute like IIMs, IIT, IISER etc. will be preferred. Proficiency in computer operations (MS Windows and MS Office) and Internet. The post is advertised as Regular/Contract. A retired officer, if selected, gets consolidated emolument as per Government of India Rules, i.e. the last pay drawn minus pension plus other perks and benefits. In that case the initial appointment is for 3 years on contract, and the contract may be extended annually subject to satisfactory performance and requirement of the Institute up to the age of 62 years. Candidates may also be considered for appointment on contract for one/two years on consolidated salary. That contract may be extended based on performance and requirements of the Institute. Appointments are governed by the relevant service rules and regulations of the Institute as amended from time to time.

Conduct the Board and Society meetings and follow-ups. Act as the First Appellate Authority under the RTI Act, 2005. Have thorough knowledge of the GeM portal, GFR 2017, FR&SR and relevant Central Government rules and procedures.

content_sections.heading: Qualification and Experience
content_sections.text: The notice does not print an experience requirement. A Master's degree with 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point-scale wherever the grading system is followed) in a concerned/relevant/allied subject from an Indian University, or an equivalent degree from an accredited foreign university. In addition, the candidate must have cleared the National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the UGC or the CSIR, or a similar test accredited by the UGC, like SLET/SET. Candidates who are or have been awarded a Ph.D. degree in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Minimum Standards and Procedure for Award of M.Phil./Ph.D. Degree) Regulations, 2009 or 2016 and their amendments are exempted from NET/SLET/SET. NET/SLET/SET is also not required for Master's programmes in disciplines for which NET/SLET/SET is not conducted by the UGC, CSIR or a similar UGC-accredited test. Candidates registered for the Ph.D. programme prior to 11 July 2009 are governed by the Ordinances, Bye-laws or Regulations of the institution awarding the degree. They are exempted from NET/SLET/SET if all of these conditions are met: The fulfilment of these conditions is to be certified by the Registrar or the Dean (Academic Affairs) of the University concerned. The Ph.D. degree has been obtained from a foreign university/institution with a ranking among the top 500 in the World University Ranking (at any time) by any one of: Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), the Times Higher Education (THE), or the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) of the Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Shanghai). A relaxation of 5% marks may be provided at Graduate and Master's level for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Differently-abled (physically and visually differently-abled) and Other Backward Class (OBC) (non-creamy layer) categories, for eligibility and for assessing good academic record during engagement of temporary faculty. It applies only to qualifying marks, without any grace mark procedure. A relaxation of 5% (from 55% to 50%) may be provided to Ph.D. degree holders who obtained their Master's degree prior to 19 September 1991. A relevant grade regarded as equivalent to 55% marks, wherever a recognised university follows the grading system, is also considered eligible. The notice asks candidates to satisfy themselves beforehand that they hold the minimum essential qualification. See the official notification for the full eligibility wording.

rows.qualification: Eligibility A or B, as set out below. Specialization / relevant discipline: NET or Ph.D. in English; Master's degree in English, English Literature, Linguistics, Film Studies, English Language & Literature, Communicative English or Translation Studies.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Terms
content_sections.text: Pay: Rs. 1500/- per lecture, subject to a maximum of Rs. 50,000/- per month. Payment will be made on an hourly basis as per University norms. The engagement is purely temporary, initially for one semester or as per requirement of the University. It may be extended on the basis of the University's requirement and the incumbent's satisfactory performance. The Guest Faculty will not get allowances, pension, gratuity and leave as admissible to regular teachers. The engaged candidate is not entitled to residential accommodation, official transport, leave encashment or any other allowances/facilities admissible to a regular employee. The University may modify, withdraw or cancel any communication to candidates if an inadvertent mistake in the selection process is detected at any stage, even after the engagement letter or joining.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The notice describes shortlisting followed by an interview before the Selection Committee. The marking scheme is not specified in the notice. Shortlisted candidates may be invited to appear before the Selection Committee. No TA/DA is admissible for attending the interview. The list of shortlisted candidates will be published on the official website ( www.cuj.ac.in ) under the Careers Section. The interview will be held only for shortlisted candidates on 20 November 2026 from 10:30 a.m. onwards. Reporting time is 9:30 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. The interview may continue the next day depending on circumstances, so candidates should come prepared accordingly. The interview date may change; any change will be notified on the University website.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required
content_sections.text: Duly filled-in application form with certificate, mark sheet and experience certificate etc. Ph.D. holders whose degree was awarded under the UGC Regulations 2009 or 2016: a certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure I) from the concerned University that the Ph.D. complies with the UGC regulation. Annexure I applies to candidates registered for the Ph.D. on or after 11 July 2009. Candidates registered for the Ph.D. before 11 July 2009: a certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure II) from the concerned University/Institute. It is signed by the Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice Chancellor or Dean (Academic Affairs). SC/ST/OBC candidates: a caste certificate from the competent authority in the prescribed format (Annexure III for SC/ST, Annexure IV for OBC). OBC candidates: a valid caste certificate of the current financial year in the Government of India proforma, stating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer. Candidates claiming the PH category: a medical certificate from the competent authority.

content_sections.heading: About AIIMS Bathinda
content_sections.text: The notice describes AIIMS Bathinda as one of the new AIIMS, set up by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) under an Act of Parliament. Its stated aim is to correct regional imbalances in quality tertiary healthcare and to attain self-sufficiency in graduate and postgraduate medical education. Applications are invited by the Executive Director, and the Institute is located at Jodhpur Romana, Mandi Dabwali Road, Bathinda, Punjab, 151001.

content_sections.heading: Department-wise Vacancies
content_sections.text: The notice lists 55 posts in four tables: Professor 17, Additional Professor 4, Associate Professor 16 and Assistant Professor 18. The vacancies are provisional and subject to variation. The notice marks vacancies reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities as (PwBD) within a category. If suitable candidates are not found for the Additional Professor posts, these posts can be filled by the lower cadre in the respective category in all the disciplines as advertised. The notice gives the example of the Additional Professor (SC) post in Nuclear Medicine, which can be filled by an Associate Professor (SC) or Assistant Professor (SC) candidate. Candidates eligible for the lower cadre may therefore also apply in departments where the higher post is advertised. If suitable candidates are not found for the Associate Professor posts, these posts can be filled by the lower cadre in the respective category in all the disciplines. For example, the Associate Professor (OBC) post in Cardiology can be filled by an Assistant Professor (OBC) candidate, so Assistant Professor-eligible candidates may also apply where the higher post is advertised. BLA = Both Leg and Both Arms affected; OL = One Leg; OH = One Hand; OA = One Arm; OAL = One Arm and One Leg; B = Blind; LV = Low Vision. PwBD candidates need at least 40% of the specified disability and must fulfil the functional requirements of the post to be eligible for the 4% horizontal reservation, on production of a valid disability certificate from the competent authority.

content_sections.heading: About the Centre of Excellence for Rare Diseases
content_sections.text: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhopal is located at Saket Nagar, Bhopal (MP) 462020. The Technical Coordinator (I) will work at its Centre of Excellence for Rare Diseases, which functions under the National Policy for Rare Diseases (NPRD), 2021 of MoHFW. The post will report to the Nodal Officer of the CoE, Dr. Bhavna Dhingra, Professor and I/C Head, Department of Medical Genetics, AIIMS Bhopal.

content_sections.heading: Posts and Eligibility
content_sections.text: There is one post of Technical Coordinator (I), reserved as UR. The minimum essential qualification is a Master's degree in public health / Community Medicine / Health Management / Hospital Management / Public Health Informatics and related subjects OR MSW or equivalent from a recognized university, with at least 5 years' experience of working in the Public Health Sector. The notice also requires familiarity with Public Health Systems (Rare Diseases) and Government Health Schemes. The prescribed qualification is the minimum, and merely possessing it does not entitle a candidate to selection. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility of the post. The age limit is up to 45 years (as on the closing date of application). Age relaxation is admissible for SC/ST/OBC candidates and for departmental candidates (including projects), in accordance with the instructions issued by the Central Government/MoHFW guidelines from time to time. The relaxation is subject to submission of the concerned document for the category along with the original application. Pay: ₹60,000/- per month (consolidated). Duration: one year, extendable as per the requirement of the CoE, subject to fund availability under NPRD, 2021. The engagement is purely contractual and time-bound; no permanent position shall be created and there will be no liability for regularization or absorption. The appointment is made from the human resource support sanctioned to the CoE and gives no right to appointment within the sanctioned staff strength of AIIMS Bhopal or MoHFW, New Delhi. MoHFW has no employer-employee relationship with the engaged Technical Coordinator. The contract expires automatically on completion of the period unless renewed with mutual consent, and can be terminated by either side with 30 days' notice or salary in lieu thereof. Leave is governed by the AIIMS Bhopal leave policy for extramural/short-term research projects; no hostel or other accommodation will be provided. The appointee can be posted anywhere as per the requirement of the CoE, including rural areas/field sites. Private practice of any type is prohibited.

content_sections.heading: AIIMS Bhopal Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Act as a focal point for the Rare Diseases Clinic at the CoE. Provide technical and strategic support for planning, coordination and implementation of rare disease-related activities. Coordinate with clinical departments for diagnosis, investigations and formulation of treatment plans. Facilitate documentation, application review and approval processes for patient support. Liaise with MoHFW, State Governments and other stakeholders for fund disbursement and compliance. Coordinate with the spokes in matters of proposals for equipment & consumables procurement, demand for funds, submission of Utilization Certificates, etc. Track drug procurement and ensure timely availability and logistics for therapy. Guide and monitor ABHA ID generation and digital health record maintenance. Ensure timely and accurate data reporting and analytics for MoHFW and internal reviews. Organize capacity-building sessions, trainings and awareness programmes at the CoE. Develop and disseminate IEC materials and media content for public and stakeholder awareness. Support development of treatment guidelines, SOPs and other technical documentation. Manage patient data and regularly update the Rare Disease Registry and associated digital platforms. Assist in preparation of reports, summaries and digital dashboards. Maintain proper patient records in both digital and physical formats, ensuring confidentiality. Provide counseling, guidance and continuous support to rare disease patients and their caregivers.

content_sections.heading: What to Bring
content_sections.text: Candidates must bring the duly filled application form in the prescribed format (attached to the notice) to the interview. Incomplete applications or applications without the prescribed format will not be considered. The form asks for personal details, category, age as on the last date of application, whether age relaxation is required, addresses, mobile number, email, qualifications from 10th class onwards, experience (newest to oldest) and any other information related to Public Health / Rare Diseases / Government Health Schemes work. Self-attested copies of all documents (one set). Proof of date of birth (class 10th certificate). Eligibility qualification mark-sheets and degrees. Experience certificates (minimum 5 years in the Public Health Sector). Category certificate for age relaxation (SC/ST/OBC). Other relevant testimonials. Two recent passport-size colour photographs. No Objection Certificate from the current employer (if in government service). Original documents for verification. A candidate who does not bring the original certificates, two photographs and one set of self-attested photocopies will not be allowed to participate in the interview.

content_sections.heading: What Happens on the Day
content_sections.text: The selection committee will conduct a walk-in interview for the post of Technical Coordinator (I). If a large number of eligible candidates appear, the committee may shortlist candidates through an MCQ based written test conducted on the day of the interview, and only the shortlisted candidates shall be interviewed. The final merit shall be prepared based on the marks obtained in the selection process. The interview is held only by appearing personally at the venue; there is no provision for an online interview. Any candidate found ineligible at any stage would not be allowed to proceed for the interview. No TA/DA will be given for appearing in the selection process or for joining the post. The result will be displayed on the AIIMS Bhopal website, and the selected candidate must join within seven days of the issue of the Offer letter.

content_sections.heading: Department-wise Vacancies
content_sections.text: The notice lists 58 vacancies in total across 25 departments. The department-wise figures below add up to 58. 3 (three) posts are reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities in the non surgical departments as per Government of India policy. One per cent each is reserved for persons with benchmark disabilities under clauses (a), (b) and (c), and one per cent for those under clauses (d) and (e): (a) blindness and low vision; (b) deaf and hard of hearing; (c) locomotor disability including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims and muscular dystrophy; (d) autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability and mental illness; (e) multiple disabilities from amongst persons under clauses (a) to (d) including deaf-blindness, in the posts identified for each disability. The numbers of vacant posts are inclusive of backlog vacancies. Candidates from General and other categories will also be considered for adhoc appointment against vacant posts of a reserved category (marked with an asterisk *) if reserved category candidates are not available. In General Medicine 3 posts, in General Surgery 2 posts and in Obstetrics & Gynaecology 1 post will be considered for adhoc appointment against OBC posts. EWS posts are not carried forward or considered as backlog vacancy if unfilled. Other category candidates may be allowed provisionally to apply, and will be considered for the post as UR candidates only if the EWS seat is otherwise not filled up.

content_sections.heading: Qualification and Experience
content_sections.text: Persons possessing a qualification included in Part II of the 3rd Schedule should also fulfil the conditions specified in Section 13(B) of the Act. Age is counted on the last date of submission of applications, 20.11.2026 up to 5:30 p.m., which the notice calls the crucial date for age, educational qualification and experience. Reservation and age relaxation are provided as per Govt. of India norms. For discipline-specific eligibility of each post, candidates should refer to the official notification.

content_sections.heading: About National Library
content_sections.text: The National Library is an institution of the Government of India under the Ministry of Culture. Under its programme "Young Professional Graduates from Library & Information Science as LIS Interns", it engages professional LIS graduates for one year to work in its language sections and divisions, including the Reading Room, Stack area, Acquisition division and Laboratory division.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details (Language-wise)
content_sections.text: The National Library needs 25 (twenty five) LIS Interns, allotted across 23 languages. Hindi and Tamil have 2 interns each; every other language has 1. The total number of LIS interns and their language-wise allocation may be changed as and when required.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The same eligibility applies to all 23 language positions. Age limit: the age of the candidate must be below 35 years on the last date of application. The notice does not mention any age relaxation. Earlier interns: the Library does not engage the same Intern more than once. Candidates who have already completed their Internship programme at National Library shall not be considered. Language competence after selection: if, after final selection, an Intern is found not well competent in reading/writing the concerned language, a language board will be constituted, and on its recommendation the Library will terminate that internship with immediate effect. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of each language position.

rows.essential_qualification: Master Degree in Library and Information Science or its equivalent, obtained on or before the last date of application. Must have proper knowledge of the concerned language.
rows.desirable: The concerned language at Intermediate level as one subject.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The amount paid to the LIS Intern is to be treated as "Stipend": Rs 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty five thousand only) per month to each Intern. The stipend amount includes the medical insurance policy of the candidate. The candidate must obtain a compulsory medical insurance policy from a recognized insurance company for the period of the LIS Internship. The stipend will be paid within the 5th of every month. The internship lasts 01 (One) Year from the date of engagement of each Intern, with 40 hours per week of on-task activity. Five Day Week: all days except Saturday, Sundays and other public holidays followed at the National Library. Interns normally work at the Divisions posted from 9.30 am to 6:00 pm. There would be rotation duties on Saturdays/Sundays as well as week days (8.00 am to 8.00 pm), as per a roster prepared by the competent authority. 10 (ten) Casual Leaves can be availed in one year. Compensatory leave can be accumulated by working on Saturday, Sundays and other public holidays with prior approval; a maximum of two days in a month can be accumulated, and a maximum of five days can be availed at a time with the approval of the competent authority. After successful completion of one year, interns would be given a Completion Certificate with grading: Grade A+ Outstanding (85 marks and above), Grade A Excellent (75 to 84), Grade B Very Good (60 to 74), Grade C Good (50 to 59), Grade D Average (below 50 marks).

content_sections.heading: National Library Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: The notice gives one list of typical areas of responsibility for all LIS Interns: Entry in MARC 21 format Cataloguing of books/ serials/other materials. Classification/Circulation system/ Preservation of materials. Acquisition System, DB Act System, Sorting section etc. Stack area/Books/Newspaper receiving section etc. Organization of materials and data, including Indexing and abstracting. Reference services/ Reading Room/ E-resource centre/ bibliographic section. Open Source Software in KOHA installation and entry. Assisting in monitoring, checking and supervising, under direction of ALIOs, the work performed by the trained manpower engaged by an outsourcing agency for retrospection data storage and technical processing of unprocessed books. Activities for specific groups (children and young adult reading and storytelling activities; outreach to researchers and scholars; information assistance to individuals with a disability). Other special sectional/divisional works as and when required. Attending/organizing NL regular seminar/ workshop/ exhibition etc. Work in every section of the National Library, including office administration/accounts, for exposure. Visit to other Libraries/ MoC organizations. Targets start from the second month after joining, as interns first learn the processes through training at various divisions/sections. The monthly target is 300 for every language except English (400), for 11 months. The target set for one year is 3,300 per intern (4,400 for the English intern), giving 6,600 for Hindi and Tamil with two interns each and a total of 83,600 for all 25 interns. 75% of total working hours is to be spent reaching the target at the Internship Unit, and 25% in other sections/divisions/units as assigned by the Coordinators. If interns are engaged in checking and supervision of the outsourcing agency's work, their target will be increased by 150% of the fixed target. Target cannot be calculated when a special task is given, until the task is completed; urgent work may also be assigned by the coordinators. The Assistant Library & Information Officer (ALIO) of the concerned Language Section / Division supervises and guides each intern; the Language Division LIO also supervises. Interns would be trained with KOHA Open Source Software. Each intern maintains a daily report card in a diary, verified and counter-signed by the concerned ALIOs, and submits it every month. A compiled report is submitted every four months in hard copy and soft copy; the final one-year report is signed by all concerned LIOs/ALIOs and may be signed by the PLIO. A progress meeting of LIS Interns with all LIOs and ALIOs is held on the last Friday of every month under the chairmanship of the PLIO. Any shortfall of target must be duly signed by the Intern and the concerned ALIOs.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for National Library Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Applications for the LIS Internship must be submitted online through the link available on the National Library website; no hardcopy will be accepted. The notice's own "CLICK HERE FOR APPLY" link opens an online form. The notice does not print a last date for applying. Open the application link given on the National Library website (the notice's "CLICK HERE FOR APPLY" link). Apply for the position of the language you have proper knowledge of. Provide your e-mail address and mobile number; all intimation is given to candidates through e-mail only. Follow the National Library website for regular updates on the recruitment of LIS Interns.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection runs in this order: short-listing on merit, then an examination on LIS (MCQ), a practical exam and an interview. The Top-Scorer in each language would be selected as LIS Intern, and a panel would be drawn accordingly. A Screening/Selection Committee scrutinises all applications and short-lists on merit, based on the highest percentage at Master of Library & Information Science, BLISC, Graduation, 12 Standard and 10 Standard. Short-listed candidates would be called for interview on a 1:10 basis (top 10 candidates by percentage) or any other criteria decided by the Competent Authority. Total marks are 100: 45% weightage on Academic & Professional Qualification (Academic 15 marks, Professional 30 marks) and 55% weightage on the subjective, practical and interview stages. These stages carry 100 marks, reduced to 55%. The notice does not mention the number of questions, the duration, negative marking or the dates of these stages.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: Every LIS Intern should submit a Medical Certificate from Govt. Hospitals before joining. No TA/DA would be provided for joining as LIS Intern in National Library. Criteria relating to targets, supervision, job descriptions, certification and grading may be changed on the recommendation of an expert committee.

content_sections.text: The researchers assist in data collection, field surveys, analysis and documentation for the Working Plan. The studies include socio-economic survey, soil survey, biodiversity, NTFP including medicinal and aromatic plants, forest carbon stock, bamboo/rattan, soil erosion and watershed assessment, forest fire impact, wildlife habitat and human-wildlife conflict, and the impact of mining on forest areas. Work is in the interior forest areas of the division and, where required, the peripheral area adjoining the forest boundary for Trees Outside Forests. Overall coordination and supervision of field teams and research activities in accordance with NWPC, 2023. Preparation of study designs, sampling frameworks and data-collection protocols. Analysis and interpretation of field data and preparation of thematic reports under the guidance of the DFO/Working Plan Officer (WPO). Compilation and maintenance of Division-level datasets, including compartment histories, growing-stock data and GIS layers, in the formats prescribed under NWPC, 2023. Maintenance of accurate records, registers and data repositories. Any other work assigned by the DFO(WPO) from time to time. Conduct field surveys and collect data in accordance with approved format under NWPC, 2023. Undertake local community/stake holder interaction for socio-economic and NTFP assessments. Undertake soil sampling, botanical and zoological enumeration and biodiversity documentation. Compile, enter and validate field data. Assist the SRF in preparation of reports, maps and other project outputs/documents. Any other work assigned by the DFO(WPO)/SRF from time to time. The Research Fellows are monitored and supervised by the Working Plan Officer-cum-DFO and submit a fortnightly progress report to the Divisional Forest Officer.

basic_details.job_title: AIIMS Deoghar Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online for 2 Field Investigator, Health Economist Posts
basic_details.short_information: The Department of Evidence Synthesis (DOES), All India Institute of Medical Sciences Deoghar, has invited applications for two contractual, project-based posts under the Health Technology Assessment in India (HTAIn) Project funded by the Department of Health Research (DHR), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India: one Health Economist/Scientist C (₹67,000/- + HRA per month) and one Field Investigator (₹30,000/- to ₹32,000/- per month). The engagement is for 12 months. Applications go by email as one single PDF file to [email protected] by 5 December 2026, 5:00 PM. No hard copy

important_dates.communication of eligibility by email: Within 48 hours of receipt of application

how_to_apply: Get the application form from the Institute's website (www.aiimsdeoghar.edu.in), or use ANNEXURE-II (Application Form) at the end of the notification.
Fill the form and affix a passport size photo in the space given.
Attach self-attested copies of the enclosures listed below.
Combine the application form with all annexures and enclosures into ONE SINGLE PDF file.
Email the PDF to [email protected] so that it reaches by 05.12.2026, 5:00 PM. Late applications will not be considered.
Write the subject line "Application for Health Economist/SCIENTIST C" or "Application for Field Investigator".
Only the soft copy is to be sent. The notice says: do not send the hard copy of the application.
Enclosure-1: self-attested copies of educational qualifications.
Enclosure-2: experience certificates.
Enclosure-3: relevant publications in indexed journals, if applicable. Details of only SCOPUS or PubMed/MEDLINE indexed papers should be attached separately.
Enclosure-4: NOC from the present employer, if applicable.

The application form also asks for academic and technical qualifications from High School onwards, work/research experience, research experience in Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (write Nil if none), number of publications, PMIDs of the best 2 Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis, and present employment.
important_instructions: It is the candidate's responsibility to ascertain and ensure eligibility. Misinformation detected at any stage makes the candidate liable for legal action. Permission to appear in the selection process does not approve eligibility. A candidate may be disqualified at document verification if essential eligibility criteria are not fulfilled. The engagement does not confer any right to regular appointment or absorption in AIIMS Deoghar, DHR or any other Government organization. Canvassing of any kind will lead to disqualification. Private practice of any type is prohibited. The appointee can be posted at any place as per project requirement, including rural areas and field sites. The appointee is expected to conform to the rules of conduct and discipline applicable to Institute employees. For queries, the notice gives Mr. Chandan Kumar, Administrative Officer HTAIn AIIMS Deoghar (Mobile: 7667893100).

content_sections.heading: About AIIMS Deoghar and the HTAIn Project
content_sections.text: The notice is issued by the Department of Evidence Synthesis (DOES) of AIIMS Deoghar, Jharkhand, which hosts a DHR-HTAIn Centre. The posts sit under the Principal Investigator, Dr. Seshadri Reddy Varikasuvu, Associate Professor, Department of Biochemistry, and Head, Department of Evidence Synthesis. The notice states that the appointments are purely temporary and project-based.

content_sections.text: The notice announces 2 posts in total. It does not print any category-wise break-up.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Experience: 2 years of experience in Health Economics for Junior Staff and 6 years for Senior Staff. Age limit: 40 Years. The 3 years' work experience is attached to the Graduate option only, as printed; the Master's and Pharm D options are listed with "OR". Age limit: 35 Years. The age cut-off date is the last date of submission of application. Age relaxation for Government servants and SC/ST/OBC candidates is in accordance with DoPT instructions issued from time to time. Further relaxation may be considered for exceptionally qualified and experienced candidates or retired professionals, if found suitable. The notice says eligibility criteria, qualifications, age limits and job roles are derived from the HTAIn Guidelines (March 2024) issued by DHR. Candidates should check ANNEXURE-I of the official notification for the full eligibility of each post.

rows.desirable: Ph.D. in a related field; proficiency in MS Office, VBA, and TreeAge

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Health Economist/Scientist C: ₹67,000/- + HRA per month, consolidated remuneration. Field Investigator: ₹30,000/- to ₹32,000/- per month, consolidated remuneration. The notice does not mention HRA for this post. The engagement is contractual and purely temporary for 12 months. It may be extended for a maximum of one more year based on performance, or till completion of the project, whichever is earlier. Project staff performance is reviewed every six months. If it is not found satisfactory, the engagement could be terminated with one month's notice or one month's stipend in lieu thereof. Leave is admissible as per the terms of engagement and prevailing Institute norms.

content_sections.heading: AIIMS Deoghar Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Contribute to technical and organizational planning of HTA projects. Undertake HTA studies approved under the concerned institute. Contribute to writing, editing, and publication of reports and journal articles related to HTA studies. Maintain confidentiality of HTAIn Secretariat and Technical Appraisal Committee/Board proceedings. Adhere to DHR policies and procedures. Perform any other duties assigned by the Project Heads. content_sections.text: Besides the 2 years of relevant experience, applicants need proven experience in at least one of these areas: Campus placement operations at a reputed Institute or University. Recruitment and talent acquisition within a Corporate House or MNC. Manpower development, corporate training and talent management. Working or having experience in IITs/IIMs/IISERs/NITs/CFTIs. content_sections.heading: NIT Rourkela Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Look after the training and placement activities and internship of the students. Oversee the end-to-end placement process, including candidate sourcing, screening, job offers and on boarding. Generate regular reports and analytics to track placement metrics, identify trends and evaluate program effectiveness. Monitor post-placement feedback and promptly address issues or concerns raised by employers or participants. Keep close liaison with industry, Government and non-Government organizations for placement of students. Work with the Coordinators for Industry–Institute Interaction to organize lectures, expert talks and interactive sessions by industry professionals. Guide students for competitive examinations such as TOEFL, GRE, GATE, CAT, etc. Arrange and organize study tours of the students. Accompany and provide facilities, including hospitality, to the HR Team of the companies during campus placement drives. Arrange training programmes for soft skills and interview facing skills using institutional and external expertise. Organize entrepreneurship workshops, hackathons, etc. Create a database on Alumni and their present position. Develop a database on placement records of graduated students and a database of recruiting industries and organizations. Support activity in branding and promotional activities. Willingness to travel occasionally for placement-related meetings, employer visits or recruitment events, and readiness to work in flexible office timing. Any other duties assigned from time to time by Head, CDC or Competent Authorities.

A candidate must meet one of the two qualification routes printed in the notice: Post Graduate from recognized University in respective subject with at least 50% marks and Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) from National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) recognized institution; or Post Graduate with at least 50% marks from recognized University in respective subject and B.A.Ed. / B.Sc.Ed. from any National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) recognized institution. The signed declaration printed with the form. Self-attested copies of all relevant documents/certificates. Supporting documents named on the form: Leaving Certificate, Caste Certificate, SSC, HSC, Graduation, Post Graduation, Professional qualification and Experience Certificate. Original documents, which must be produced for verification at the time of interview. The application form asks for name, father's name, residential address, mobile number, email ID, date of birth, gender, caste category (SC/ST/OBC/Un-reserved), whether the candidate belongs to the Physically Handicapped or another special category, marital status, domicile of DNH/Daman/Diu, medium of study in SSC, education details (SSC, HSC, Graduation, Post Graduation, B.Ed. with board/university, year, marks and percentage), experience and any other achievements related to the post.

Preferred: Master's degree in Physical Education (M.P.Ed.), Sports Science, Sports Management, Physical Education & Sports, or an equivalent relevant discipline from a recognized institution. Experience: minimum 5 years of relevant experience in university/college sports, sports administration, facility management, coaching, sports academy operations or a comparable environment. Desired skills: sound knowledge of fitness training, strength and conditioning, gym equipment, exercise techniques and safety protocols; strong communication and interpersonal skills; comfortable working closely with students. content_sections.heading: Nalanda University Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Sports Infrastructure & Facilities: oversee the day-to-day functioning, utilisation and upkeep of playgrounds, courts, gymnasium, indoor/outdoor sports facilities and equipment; coordinate maintenance, repairs and infrastructure upgrades. Sports Planning & Execution: develop and execute the University's annual sports calendar, including regular activities, tournaments, leagues, annual sports meets, fitness initiatives and recreational programmes. Coaching & Student Development: conduct/supervise regular coaching and practice sessions, identify sporting talent, mentor students, develop University teams and prepare students for competitive events. Competitions & Events: organise intra-University and inter-university competitions and coordinate team selection, registrations, equipment, travel and other logistics. Sports Administration: maintain records of facilities, equipment, inventory, student participation and achievements; support procurement and budget planning; prepare periodic reports. Team & Stakeholder Coordination: coordinate with coaches, trainers, ground staff and relevant University departments for smooth and safe conduct of all sporting activities. Student Engagement & Sports Culture: drive participation across the student community while promoting fitness, teamwork, discipline, sportsmanship and competitive excellence. Supervise the day-to-day functioning of the women's gymnasium, games and physical education, and ensure a safe, disciplined and welcoming fitness environment. Conduct regular fitness, strength, conditioning, mobility and general exercise sessions for students. Guide users on the correct and safe use of gym equipment, exercise techniques and appropriate workout routines. Develop basic individual and group fitness programmes based on fitness levels and goals. Monitor students during workouts and provide guidance on posture, form, warm-up, cool-down and injury prevention. Conduct basic fitness assessments and track progress, wherever required. Ensure gym equipment is properly used, maintained and stored; promptly report maintenance or safety concerns. Maintain required records related to gym usage, equipment and activities. Support the University in organising fitness challenges, wellness activities, sports camps and related student-engagement initiatives. Ensure adherence to University rules, gym timings, safety standards and hygiene protocols.

The engagement is purely temporary and contractual. It is co-terminus with the tenure of the project or 06 years, whichever is earlier. It is initially up to 30 November 2026, extendable up to November 2027, subject to availability of fund and requirement. It may be extended or curtailed based on the conduct and performance of the incumbent and the requirement of the institute, and may be extended further on the recommendation of the Review Committee. It expires automatically when the project tenure ends. The engagement gives no right or claim to regularization for a permanent post of CSIR-CFTRI/CSIR. content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Applicants are shortlisted by a designated committee according to the current requirement. Candidates shortlisted for interview are displayed on the CSIR-CFTRI website and informed by e-mail at the address given in the online application. If there are a large number of applications, the committee may shortlist by percentage of marks in the essential qualification, higher educational qualifications than the minimum, desirable qualification/experience, or any other methodology it deems fit. Based on interview performance, the result of selected candidates for each post code is declared and posted on the CFTRI website. Selection for engagement, the panel of waitlisted candidates and its validity are as per CSIR rules vide OM No. 5-1(342)/2017-PD dated 02.09.2024, amended from time to time. No TA/DA is given for attending the interview. The notice does not give the interview date or venue.

Give the correct e-mail address in the form; shortlisted candidates are told the interview date by e-mail there. Check https://cftri.res.in/ regularly for any addendum or corrigendum. Experience: minimum 3-5 years of experience in Monitoring & Evaluation within public health, development, or related sectors. Experience in managing and analysing survey data. Proficiency in data analysis using STATA or similar statistical analysis packages. Preferred skills: sound knowledge of public health programmes, health systems, research ethics, family planning, RMNCH+A, and relevant national and international frameworks. Preferred skills: strong analytical, quantitative research, problem-solving and report-writing skills. Preferred skills: familiarity with other statistical software and data visualization tools would be an advantage. Experience overseeing data quality assurance and monitoring systems for research or M&E projects. Proven experience working with government health systems, research institutions, development partners, or NGOs. Experience in reproductive, maternal, newborn, child health, family planning, or women's health programmes is highly desirable. Preferred skills: leading large survey teams, stakeholder management including engagement with government officials, and fluency in English and Hindi. Preferred skills: knowledge of survey budgeting, operational research management, community-based research and public health programmes, particularly RMNCH+A. Preferred skills: proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint and Word. Knowledge of STATA, SPSS, R etc. will be an added advantage. content_sections.heading: KGMU Manager cum Data Analyst Job Description
content_sections.text: The Data Analyst will be responsible for managing, processing, analysing and interpreting survey data. The role includes ensuring data quality and accuracy, and contributing to analytical reports, presentations and other research outputs. Contribute to developing and refining survey tools, manuals and other research-related documents. Train and support field and research staff on data collection, data management and quality assurance procedures. Manage and maintain survey datasets and the data collection system. Monitor data collection across study sites, and conduct data cleaning, validation, recoding and labelling. Prepare analysis-ready datasets, codebooks and data dictionaries, and develop statistical analysis plans. Perform statistical analyses using STATA or other relevant software, and prepare analytical summaries, tables and reports. Ensure data security, confidentiality, regulatory compliance and documentation, and adhere to Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion, and Safeguarding and PSHEA initiatives. Plan, budget, coordinate and manage household- and facility-based surveys, studies, trials and pilot projects from inception to completion. Lead field logistics, communication, coordination and documentation processes. Act as the lead liaison with the Chief Medical Officer, CMS, MoICs and HoDs of survey facilities/districts. Oversee the development, translation, adaptation, pilot testing and finalization of survey tools and manuals. Lead training for research staff, field teams and facility personnel, and supervise research coordinators and research officers. Monitor study progress, data quality, deliverables, timelines and budgets, and prepare progress reports. Organise regular review meetings, and support reports, presentations, policy briefs and dissemination of findings. Participant identification and recruitment: identify eligible participants attending OPDs, screen them against study criteria, explain the study, and enrol them. Obtain written informed consent as per the approved study protocol. Provide family-planning counselling without bias, address myths, and support informed and voluntary choice. Data collection: collect baseline information, administer questionnaires, and complete case record forms. Data entry and records: enter data into the electronic data-capture system and maintain study records. Participant follow-up: maintain the follow-up schedule, and record method continuation, side effects and adverse events. Administrative work: prepare monthly recruitment and follow-up reports, and assist the Principal Investigator with progress reports.

content_sections.heading: About CTIL
content_sections.text: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, established the Centre for Trade and Investment Law to provide legal and technical inputs on international trade and investment law issues. CTIL works as a think tank and advisory centre on legal issues under the World Trade Organisation (WTO), free trade agreements and other international economic law issues. Its office is at 6th Floor, NAFED House, Siddhartha Enclave, Ashram Chowk, Ring Road, New Delhi -110014. CTIL also hosts the Trade Remedies Advisory Cell (TRAC). TRAC supports the domestic industry in preparing applications, collating information or data, and providing legal advice for trade remedial investigations before the anti-dumping and safeguard authorities of India. The notice is signed by the Registrar, IIFT.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Candidates must be Indian nationals and qualified ICWA/CMA/CA. They must also meet the following post-specific criteria printed in the notice: Must hold a master's degree in areas such as cost accounting (ICWA/CMA/CA) or a related discipline. Consistently good academic record with at least 55% (or an equivalent grade on a point scale wherever the grading system is followed) at bachelor's and master's levels. Must have a minimum of 8 years post-qualification experience (PQE), out of which a minimum of 3 years must be in the relevant field, for example Trade Remedies, international trade and allied field. PQE means work experience obtained after the candidate's successful qualification as an ICWA/CMA/CA. Excellent cost accountancy skills, with a demonstrated interest and/or experience in trade remedies and related fields. Strong written and spoken communication, and presentation skills in English. Ability to provide sound and rigorous cost accounting analysis. Strong research, drafting and analytical skills, specifically in trade and investment law fields. Relevant work experience or research and studies produced in trade remedies, international trade or a related discipline is desirable. Strong preference will be given to candidates who have experience in trade remedies, international trade and allied field. The upper age limit is 50 years, counted on the last date of receiving the applications, as the notice's table heading states. The eligibility criteria also state that the candidate must not be more than 50 years of age at the time of recruitment. The notice does not mention any age relaxation. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the post.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The selected candidate will be paid a fixed monthly remuneration in the range of ₹1,45,000–2,65,000 for PhD candidates and ₹1,37,500–2,65,000 for candidates without a PhD. The remuneration will be fixed on the following basis: The range of remuneration given for the position. Years of experience (overall and relevant experience); or Last pay drawn. This will be considered only in special cases where the Selection Committee determines that the candidate is exceptional. The appointment will be on a contractual basis, initially for a period of one year. The contract may be extended further based on performance and requirements. CTIL wants the selected candidate to join immediately.

Submit the online application by 18 November 2026. Applications are accepted online only. Only applications received through this link will be considered.

content_sections.text: Applications will be evaluated first. Only candidates shortlisted for the second round, which consists of a written test and an interview, will be contacted by email. Written test: The written test will assess the candidate's competence and skills in international trade law, international investment law or, more generally, the wide disciplines of international economic law. Interview: Documents will be verified against original testimonials at the time of the interview, for applicants who are called. The notice does not mention the dates of the written test and the interview.

content_sections.heading: About PESCO
content_sections.text: The Punjab Ex-Servicemen Corporation (PESCO) is a Punjab Government Undertaking with its Head Office at SCO 89-90, Sector 34-A, Chandigarh. According to the notice, its work includes finding employment and self-employment avenues for Ex-Servicemen, Widows and Dependents, and providing specialised manpower or security services. PESCO is also moving from a manual system to a fully automated, paperless, ERP-based system, which the DGM (IT) will lead.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice lists three posts, one vacancy each, all on contractual basis.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: PESCO requires medically fit retired Defence Services personnel for these posts. Working knowledge of Punjabi, Punjab Domicile and proficiency in computers are required for all appointments. An experienced retired Defence Services officer of the rank of Col/Lt Col/Maj or equivalent with good knowledge of computers as OIC/Administrator (ESM or Non-ESM). Master Degree in Computer Science, IT, Info Systems or Software Engineer. Vendor certification like SAP Certified Application Associate, Oracle / ERP Certification, Scrum Master / Agile Certifications. Experience: 5-10 years. Punjabi proficiency – 10 certificate and Punjab domicile mandatory. Preference will be given to candidates from premier Institutes like IIT, IIIT or NIT, and to ESM. An experienced retired Defence Services officer (ESM) of the rank of Lt Col/Maj or equivalent with good knowledge of computers. Background: Retired Commissioned Officers of Defence Services. Education: Post Graduate (preferably MBA or equivalent). Experience: Minimum 5 - 10 years of leadership experience. Communication: Fluent in English, Punjabi, and Hindi. Punjab Domicile and Punjabi certificate 10th Mandatory. Resident of Punjab/ Chandigarh with understanding of the Punjab industrial ecosystem is highly desirable. Open only to Ex-Servicemen. Col/Lt Col/Maj should have commanded a unit/sub unit/est or equivalent level and medically fit. The notice does not mention a separate educational qualification for this post, apart from the Punjabi, Punjab Domicile and computer proficiency required for all appointments. Age is counted as on 01 November 2026. Candidates should check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of each post.
